projects.title: The classification of compact 1-manifolds
projects.summary: A Lean 4 (mathlib) proof of the classification of 1-manifolds, specifically that every compact, connected, Hausdorff topological space charted on the half-line [0,∞) is homeomorphic to the circle S¹ or to the closed unit interval [0,1]. The proof follows David Gale's outline: shrink to a finite atlas of interval charts, then induct on the atlas size, merging two overlapping charts at each step; a connected overlap glues two charts into one (two boundary charts glue onto [0, 1]), while a disconnected overlap has exactly two components and yields the circle.

main_results.informal: Every compact connected Hausdorff space charted on the nonnegative real half-line is homeomorphic to the circle or the closed unit interval.

projects.title: 2-Coloring Cycles in One Round
projects.summary: Formalizes certified upper and lower bounds for one-round randomized algorithms that 2-color cycles.

main_results.informal: Proves that every one-round classical algorithm has monochromatic-edge probability at least 0.23879.
Proves that an explicit one-round algorithm attains monochromatic-edge probability strictly below 0.24118.

projects.title: A formalization of Borel determinacy in Lean
projects.summary: Formalizes Martin's theorem that every Borel Gale-Stewart game is determined.

main_results.informal: Proves that every Borel Gale-Stewart game on a nonempty discrete alphabet is determined.
Proves Borel determinacy for the bundled game representation used in the formalization.

projects.title: The Aaronson–Ambainis influence conjecture
projects.summary: Proves that a real polynomial of degree at most d, bounded between zero and one on the Boolean cube and with variance at least epsilon > 0, has a coordinate of squared-difference influence at least (epsilon/d)^7. Also proves explicit bounds with epsilon^(5/2)/d^6, together with determinant pairings, fractional-certificate inequalities and coordinate averaging. The internal packing-cover duality supports the proof; generic finite LP duality is already pooled as StandardLP.strongDuality. The sharper constant is conditional on the stated Agarwal–Ben-David fractional block-sensitivity bound. Quantum simulation consequences are outside this formalization.

source.title: A proof of the Aaronson–Ambainis conjecture

main_results.informal: For every real polynomial in N variables of total degree at most d, bounded between zero and one on the Boolean cube, positive variance at least epsilon guarantees a coordinate whose uniform mean squared change under a bit flip is at least (epsilon/d)^7.
Under the same hypotheses, a coordinate has squared-difference influence at least 8 sqrt(15) epsilon^(5/2) / (125 pi^4 d^6).

For a real polynomial of degree at most d bounded in absolute value by one on the sign cube, positive variance at least epsilon guarantees a coordinate whose uniform mean squared half-difference under a bit flip is at least sqrt(15) epsilon^(5/2) / (500 pi^4 d^6).
Assuming the explicitly stated Agarwal–Ben-David fractional block-sensitivity bound, the zero-one cube influence bound improves to 32 sqrt(15) epsilon^(5/2) / (125 pi^4 d^6).

projects.title: Exceptional Set in the abc Conjecture
projects.summary: Formalizes reductions and optimization bounds for a power-saving estimate on exceptional triples in the abc conjecture.

source.title: Bounds on the exceptional set in the abc conjecture

main_results.informal: Recasts the abc conjecture as a uniform big-O bound for bounded exceptional triples.
Bounds the refined exceptional-triple count by the dyadic structured-box supremum.
Derives the Section 4 optimization bound from the determinant, geometry, and Fourier hypotheses.

projects.title: Continuity and zero-class properties of abstract linear control systems
projects.summary: Proves that every abstract linear control system with bounded L-infinity inputs between real or complex Banach spaces is zero-class, and hence has continuous input-response trajectories. No integral representation or reflexivity assumption is required. Includes finite-p continuity, a finite-p system with constant response norm, and a scalar zero-class system without integral representation or Orlicz-heart admissibility. Reusable infrastructure includes Phillips' lemma, strongly continuous semigroup bounds, half-line Lp concatenation and shifts, invariant Hahn-Banach extensions, and periodic invariant means.

source.title: Continuity of solutions to abstract linear control systems

main_results.informal: For every abstract linear control system with L-infinity inputs between real or complex Banach spaces, the norms of its input-response operators tend to zero as time tends to zero from the right.
main_results.source_ref: Theorem 1.5 of version 2, completed in Lean on 2026-10-03.

main_results.informal: For every bounded input of such a system, its input-response trajectory is continuous on the nonnegative half-line.
main_results.source_ref: Corollary 1.6.

main_results.informal: For every abstract linear control system with finite exponent p at least one and complete state space, each Lp input has a continuous input-response trajectory on the nonnegative half-line.
main_results.source_ref: Proposition 1.3.

main_results.informal: For every finite exponent p at least one, there exist real Banach input and state spaces and an abstract linear control system whose input-response operator has norm one at every positive time.
main_results.source_ref: Proposition 3.1.

main_results.informal: There exists a scalar abstract linear control system with identity semigroup and response norm equal to time, which has no integral representation and is not admissible for any of the formalized Young-function Orlicz hearts.
main_results.source_ref: Proposition 3.3; formal Young functions include the paper's class.

main_results.informal: For a pointwise null sequence of bounded linear functionals on real or complex bounded sequences, each sequence of atomic coefficients is absolutely summable, its sum of norms tends to zero, and its diagonal coefficient tends to zero.
main_results.source_ref: Lemma 2.2.

projects.title: Kolokolnikov's ACMAX conjecture
projects.summary: Proves that every simple graph on n ≥ 4 vertices with 2(n−2) edges has algebraic connectivity at most 2, attained by the complete bipartite graph K₂,ₙ₋₂. Develops Laplacian test-vector bounds, sparse cut certificates, and non-backtracking walk estimates used in the proof.

source.title: Maximizing algebraic connectivity for certain families of graphs, Conjecture 1.5

main_results.informal: For n ≥ 4, the algebraic connectivity of K₂,ₙ₋₂ is 2, and every simple graph on Fin n with exactly 2(n−2) edges has algebraic connectivity at most 2. Algebraic connectivity is the second-smallest eigenvalue of the combinatorial Laplacian, defined using Mathlib's ordered spectrum.
For a graph on any nonempty finite vertex type and any real vector whose coordinates sum to zero, algebraic connectivity times the squared norm is at most the Laplacian quadratic form.
A nonzero real vector with coordinate sum zero and Laplacian quadratic form at most twice its squared norm certifies algebraic connectivity at most 2.
For n ≥ 4, the complete bipartite graph with parts of sizes 2 and n−2 has algebraic connectivity exactly 2.

projects.title: Aumann's Agreement Theorem
projects.summary: Formalizes Aumann's agreement theorem for information partitions and a common-prior setting, together with a p-belief variant bounding posterior disagreement by 2 * (1 - p).

source.title: We Can't Agree to Disagree, Formally: Aumann's Theorem and Assumption Accounting in Lean

main_results.informal: If it is common knowledge at a state that two agents assign fixed posterior probabilities to an event, and the common-knowledge cell has equal posterior under their priors, then the two posterior probabilities are equal.
Generalizes the agreement theorem to a family of agents indexed by an arbitrary type.
Proves that common p-belief of fixed posteriors bounds the difference between any two agents' real-valued posteriors by 2 * (1 - p).

projects.title: Disproof of the Aharoni-Korman Conjecture
projects.summary: Formalizes Hollom's counterexample to the Aharoni-Korman fishbone conjecture for partially ordered sets.

main_results.informal: Proves that not every partially ordered set has either an infinite antichain or a chain meeting every antichain in a partition.

projects.title: Davis–Kahan rotation of eigenvectors
projects.summary: Formalizes the sin-Theta, tan-Theta, sin-two-Theta, and tan-two-Theta theorem families from Section 2 of Davis and Kahan (1970), for real or complex separable Hilbert spaces, including common-domain unbounded operators and symmetric-norm estimates. The tan-Theta endpoint requires Rayleigh–Ritz trial data with residual orthogonal to the trial subspace.

main_results.informal: With finite symmetric residual norm, a spectral gap gives sine-angle ideal membership and controls its symmetric norm by the corresponding residual norm.

For Rayleigh–Ritz trial data with residual orthogonal to the trial subspace, a positive directed spectral gap between the trial compression and the unwanted reducing block gives the symmetric-norm tangent-angle residual estimate and tangent pole exclusion, assuming the residual has finite symmetric norm.

Under the printed oriented gap and common-domain self-adjointness hypotheses, finite symmetric residual norm gives directed sine-double-angle ideal membership, and twice the residual norm bounds the gap times its norm.
Finite symmetric perturbation norm gives ambient sine-double-angle ideal membership and the whole-space gap bound under the theorem's reducing and perturbed-gap hypotheses.
The residual tangent-double-angle estimate holds with the theorem’s source-facing block hypotheses.

projects.title: Normalized capped log-household clearing and dynamic programming
projects.summary: Proves conditional uniqueness of a rate solving the unit-wage normalized clearing equation: mean household assets equal α / ((1 - α) * (r + δ)), with α = 9/25 and δ = 2/25. Households have capped log utility, discount 24/25, no borrowing, and monotone finite earnings transitions with positive one-step access to a lowest-income state; an explicit cap-slack inequality is required. Finite Tauchen chains instantiate the household model. Bisection converges to a given solution of this normalized equation along a stationary-distribution selection. Equivalence to full competitive market clearing for arbitrary earnings scales is not established. Preserves Bellman contraction, Berge maximum theorems, stationary Markov theory, Euler inequalities, consumption concavity and marginal-propensity bounds.

main_results.informal: For capped log households with discount 24/25, no borrowing and a finite Tauchen chain with persistence in [0,1), two rates in (-2/25, 1/24) whose stationary household distributions have mean assets equal to 9 / (16 * (r + 2/25)) coincide, provided the explicit asset-cap inequality holds at their larger rate. This is the prescribed unit-wage normalized clearing equation; a bridge to full competitive equilibrium for arbitrary earnings scales is not supplied.

Given a rate satisfying the same unit-wage normalized clearing equation in a compact interval inside (-2/25, 1/24), a stationary-distribution selection and the stated cap, monotonicity and reachability hypotheses, bisection on normalized excess supply brackets that rate, bounds midpoint error by the initial width divided by 2^(n+1), and has left endpoints converging to it. Existence of a solution to this equation is assumed.
A continuous objective maximized over a nonempty compact-valued correspondence that is upper and lower hemicontinuous has a continuous maximum value at the parameter.
A monotone operator on bounded continuous real functions that discounts constants by a nonnegative factor below one is a contraction with that factor.

projects.title: The Anderson Conjecture: A Weakly Quasi-Complete Ring Need Not Be Quasi-Complete
projects.summary: Formalizes a counterexample to Anderson's question, constructing a weakly quasi-complete Noetherian local ring that is not quasi-complete via the Jensen-Heitmann-Loepp transfinite construction.

main_results.informal: Proves that there exists a weakly quasi-complete Noetherian local ring that is not quasi-complete.

projects.title: Anomalous diffusion by fractal homogenization
projects.summary: For each positive Hölder exponent below one third, constructs a divergence-free periodic drift on the two-dimensional torus exhibiting anomalous dissipation for every mean-zero periodic H1 initial datum. The same drift admits uniform Hölder time estimates along a sequence of diffusivity intervals and two distinct vanishing-diffusivity limits for an explicit nonempty class of smooth data. Includes weak existence and uniqueness, Sobolev and Fourier/Galerkin infrastructure, flow derivatives, quantitative homogenization, and the multiscale construction. The no-selection result is the corrected version documented upstream, not the printed generality of the original paper's Proposition 5.5.

source.title: Anomalous diffusion by fractal homogenization, Lean formalization

main_results.informal: For every alpha strictly between zero and one third, one periodic, divergence-free drift has joint spatial and temporal alpha-Hölder regularity and continuity into the spatial Hölder class. It exhibits anomalous dissipation with a positive rate depending only on the initial L2-to-gradient ratio, uniform Hölder-in-time L2 bounds along diffusivity intervals accumulating at zero, and two distinct transport limits along separated diffusivity sequences for a smooth mean-zero data class containing arbitrarily high cosine modes.
main_results.source_ref: Upstream Statements/FullTheorem/AnomalousDissipationFull.lean and CITATION.cff, date-released 2026-10-02; the pinned completion commit is fad71d10bff031522cc598a37770238248186964, with committer timestamp 2026-10-02 16:04:04 UTC. Anomalous dissipation is the dimension-two case of Theorem 1.1 of arXiv:2305.05048; uniform time regularity and no-selection use upstream's documented corrections to Sections 5.4 and 5.5. The README explicitly records predominantly AI-produced proofs under the authors' supervision.

main_results.informal: For every positive alpha below one third there exists a periodic, divergence-free alpha-Hölder drift and a rate function taking values in (0,1], depending only on the initial L2-to-gradient ratio, such that the limsup as positive diffusivity tends to zero of integrated gradient dissipation is at least the squared rate times the initial L2 energy, for every mean-zero periodic H1 datum and corresponding weak solutions.
Every bounded measurable periodic drift with positive diffusivity and periodic-cell L2 initial datum has a weak solution, unique up to spatial almost-everywhere equality at every time in [0,1].

projects.title: Apportionmentlib
projects.summary: Formalizes apportionment rules and proves the Balinski-Young impossibility theorem: no anonymous quota rule can be population-monotone.

main_results.informal: Proves that no anonymous quota apportionment rule can satisfy population monotonicity.

projects.title: Archon-FirstProof-Results
projects.summary: Collects formal solutions from the Archon FirstProof benchmark, including polynomial and graph-theoretic results.

main_results.informal: Proves the benchmark harmonic-mean inequality for real-rooted polynomial transforms.
Proves the benchmark light-subset existence theorem in the graph Laplacian setting.

projects.title: A tight bound for Green's arithmetic triangle removal lemma in vector spaces
projects.summary: Proves the arithmetic triangle removal lemma in F_p^n with the polynomial bound of Fox and Lovász. If X × Y × Z contains fewer than (ε/3)^(C_p) N^2 solutions of x + y + z = 0, where N = p^n, C_p = 1 + 1/c_p and c_p is the Kleinberg–Sawin–Speyer exponent, then removing at most εN elements leaves none. Also proves the Kleinberg–Sawin–Speyer slice-rank bound p^((1 - c_p) n) on multicolored sum-free families, the lower bound (m/N)^(C_p) N^2 on the number of triangles spanned by m vertex-disjoint triangles, and that the exponent C_p is optimal, with an explicit threshold ε₀. The tightness construction formalizes Pebody's coupling theorem for decreasing mass functions and the Kleinberg–Sawin–Speyer construction of large multicolored sum-free families, using Behrend's three-term-progression-free sets.

source.title: A tight bound for Green's arithmetic triangle removal lemma in vector spaces

main_results.informal: For a prime p, ε ≥ 0 and X, Y, Z ⊆ F_p^n, if fewer than (ε/3)^(C_p) p^(2n) triples (x, y, z) ∈ X × Y × Z satisfy x + y + z = 0, then there are X' ⊆ X, Y' ⊆ Y, Z' ⊆ Z with |X \ X'| + |Y \ Y'| + |Z \ Z'| ≤ ε p^n such that no triple in X' × Y' × Z' sums to zero.
main_results.source_ref: Theorem 1.

main_results.informal: For a prime p, a finite family of triples (x_i, y_i, z_i) in F_p^n with x_i + y_j + z_k = 0 exactly when i = j = k has at most p^((1 - c_p) n) members, where p^(1 - c_p) is the infimum over 0 < x < 1 of x^(-(p-1)/3) (1 + x + ... + x^(p-1)).
main_results.source_ref: Theorem 2 (Kleinberg, Sawin and Speyer).

main_results.informal: For a prime p and X, Y, Z ⊆ F_p^n, if X × Y × Z contains m vertex-disjoint triples summing to zero, then it contains at least (m/N)^(C_p) N^2 triples summing to zero, where N = p^n.
main_results.source_ref: Theorem 3.

main_results.informal: For a prime p, η > 0 and 0 < ε < ε₀(p, η), every δ such that, in every dimension n, fewer than δ p^(2n) zero-sum triples can be destroyed by removing ε p^n elements, satisfies δ ≤ ε^(C_p - η); ε₀ is an explicit function of p and η.
main_results.source_ref: Theorem 1, second part, via the construction of Section 3.

projects.title: Analytic Hamiltonian KAM on compact action domains
projects.summary: Proves a nondegenerate analytic Hamiltonian KAM theorem on compact complex action domains whose real slice is the closure of a nonempty open set with null boundary. A positive perturbation threshold, chosen independently of the perturbation, yields a pairwise disjoint family of analytic invariant tori covering all but a prescribed relative measure error. Includes Fourier estimates, generating transformations, resonance measure bounds, infinite iteration, global Hamiltonian trajectories, and examples with a noninjective frequency map. The final torus interface asserts nonresonance but does not additionally assert a quantitative Diophantine bound or the Lagrangian property.

main_results.informal: For a positive-dimensional analytic, real-compatible unperturbed Hamiltonian with nonzero Hessian determinant on the real interior of the specified compact domain, and any positive angle width and tolerance, a positive uniform perturbation threshold gives a compact positive-measure good set partitioned into pairwise disjoint analytic nonresonant invariant tori. The complementary bad set has measure less than the tolerance times the initial phase volume. Each torus has a closed embedding, an injective derivative, small displacement, and trajectories solving the original perturbed Hamiltonian equation for all real time. The analytic width is a positive output bounded by the input width.
The same KAM conclusion holds when the perturbation is pointwise strictly below the chosen threshold throughout its prescribed phase domain.
A differentiable symplectic transformation mapping into the analytic Hamiltonian's phase domain carries the vector field of the pulled-back Hamiltonian to the original Hamiltonian vector field.

projects.title: Artin-Wedderburn Theorem
projects.summary: Formalizes the Artin-Wedderburn theorem for prime and simple Artinian rings.

source.title: A First Course in Noncommutative Rings

main_results.informal: A nontrivial prime Artinian ring is isomorphic to a matrix ring over a division ring.

projects.title: Asymptotically attaining the Moore bound
projects.summary: Proves that, for each fixed positive diameter k, the largest order of a finite simple graph with maximum degree at most d and extended diameter at most k is asymptotic to d^k as d tends to infinity. Constructs regular halved-flag graphs over every finite field, with exact order and diameter, a sharp degree cap, and matching asymptotics through all prime powers. Also proves the corresponding lower-limit bound for the edge extremum defined using line-graph diameter. Reusable infrastructure includes common bases for complete flags, odd-even sorting routes, exact flag enumeration, projective-line completion counts, and bipartite graph expansion. The analytic bridge retains the Wiener-Ikehara and prime-counting dependency closure from the Apache-2.0 PrimeNumberTheoremAnd project. The paper describes AI-assisted formalization supervised by the human authors.

source.title: Asymptotically attaining the Moore bound

main_results.informal: For each positive natural k, n(k,d)/d^k tends to 1 as the natural degree bound d tends to infinity. Here n(k,d) is the maximum number of vertices of a finite simple graph with maximum degree at most d and extended diameter at most k.

For each natural ell at least 2, the lower limit of h(ell,d)/d^ell is at least 1. Here h(ell,d) is one plus the maximum number of edges of a finite simple graph with maximum degree at most d whose line graph has extended diameter at most ell.

For every positive k and prime power q, the concrete halved-flag graph is regular, has order [2k+1]_q!/(q+1)^k, degree at most (q+1)^k((q+1)^k-1), and extended diameter exactly k. Along all prime powers q tending to infinity, its actual degree divided by this cap and its order divided by the kth power of its actual degree both tend to 1.
Any two complete flags in an n-dimensional vector space over a division ring admit an n-step route that changes only ranks of the prescribed alternating parity at each step.
For every positive real epsilon, every sufficiently large real x admits a prime strictly between x and (1+epsilon)x.

projects.title: Finite hypergraph rounding and the asymptotic triangle-packing gap
projects.summary: Formalizes a finite ceiling-carrying nibble theorem for uniform hypergraphs that are near-regular outside a small exceptional set and have suitably bounded codegrees, and derives the uniform subquadratic gap between fractional and integral triangle packing in finite graphs, together with its fractional-cover formulation.

source.title: Asymptotic triangle cover--packing development accompanying Linear-Error Clique Partitions of Split Graphs via Structured Triangle Packing

main_results.informal: For every uniformity and positive error tolerance, sufficiently large finite uniform hypergraphs with bounded codegrees, near-regular degrees outside a small exceptional set, and a global degree ceiling admit a matching covering the prescribed fraction of their vertices.
main_results.source_ref: Finite near-regular hypergraph nibble theorem used in the Paper III development.

main_results.informal: For every positive error tolerance, all sufficiently large finite graphs have fractional triangle-packing optimum at most their integral triangle-packing optimum plus the error tolerance times the square of the number of vertices.
main_results.source_ref: Paper III AX1, fractional-integral triangle-packing gap.

main_results.informal: For every positive error tolerance, all sufficiently large finite graphs have fractional triangle-cover optimum at most their integral triangle-packing optimum plus the error tolerance times the square of the number of vertices.
main_results.source_ref: Paper III AX1, cover-side formulation.

projects.title: Balanced and vertex-distinguishing edge colourings
projects.summary: Formalizes Balister–Kostochka–Li–Schelp (2004), Theorems 1, 6, 10(2) and Corollary 12. Least-cost edge colourings balance palette multiplicities within two. Degree-count bounds then yield vertex-distinguishing colourings and the Burris–Schelp bound for graphs of large maximum degree and minimum degree at least five. Theorem 10(2) explicitly assumes k ≥ 3. Includes simultaneous Kempe exchanges, palette-counting and linear-programming dual bounds; does not formalize Theorem 10(1), Corollary 11 or the whole Burris–Schelp conjecture.

source.title: Balanced edge colorings

main_results.informal: Every least-cost proper k-edge-colouring is balanced: for palettes P and Q of equal cardinality, the number of vertices seeing P is at most the number seeing Q plus two.
main_results.source_ref: BKLS (2004), Theorem 1

main_results.informal: A proper three-edge-colouring can be replaced by a four-edge-colouring that separates vertices with equal keys, under the paper's restrictions on repeated degree-three palettes and key classes.
main_results.source_ref: BKLS (2004), Theorem 6

main_results.informal: For k at least three and at least the maximum degree, the degree-count bounds in BKLS Theorem 10(2) guarantee a vertex-distinguishing proper edge-colouring with k+1 colours.
main_results.source_ref: BKLS (2004), Theorem 10(2), with k ≥ 3

main_results.informal: For a finite simple graph with minimum degree at least five and maximum degree at least sqrt(2|V|)+4, let k be the least integer with n_d at most binomial(k,d) for every d. A vertex-distinguishing proper edge-colouring exists with k+1 colours, and every such colouring uses at least k colours.
main_results.source_ref: BKLS (2004), Corollary 12

projects.title: The Bannai-Bannai-Stanton Bound on Distance Sets
projects.summary: Formalizes the Bannai-Bannai-Stanton theorem: a distance set `S` in `ℝ^d` realizing `s` distinct distances has size at most `Nat.choose (d + s) s`. Follows the short polynomial-method proof of Petrov and Pohoata via a generalized Croot-Lev-Pach rank lemma, with auxiliary results on the diagonal linear-independence argument for polynomials, monomial counting of bounded degree, and a rank bound for sums of matrices.

main_results.informal: A distance set `S` in Euclidean space `ℝ^d` realizing `s` distinct distances satisfies `S.encard ≤ Nat.choose (d + s) s`.

projects.title: Strict Beck–Fiala rounding for incidence matrices
projects.summary: Proves the rational integer-making form of Beck–Fiala rounding for finite zero-one incidence matrices with column degree bounded by a positive t. Every row has discrepancy strictly less than t, and initially integral coordinates are preserved. Includes the necessity of the positive-bound hypothesis. This is distinct from the Komlós discrepancy bound and from the non-strict hyperedge-selection rounding used in triangle packing.

source.title: "Integer-making" theorems

main_results.informal: Given a finite zero-one integer matrix with at most t ones per column, t at least one, and a rational vector in the unit cube, there is a zero-one integer vector whose discrepancy in every row is strictly less than t.
main_results.source_ref: Rational unit-cube integer-making form with the stated strict discrepancy bound.

main_results.informal: The strict rounding can additionally be chosen to leave every initially integral coordinate unchanged.
main_results.source_ref: Strengthened conclusion of the floating-coordinate proof in the pinned source.

main_results.informal: The same universally quantified strict rounding claim without the assumption t at least one is false, already for a one-by-one zero matrix with t equal to zero.
main_results.source_ref: Boundary-condition witness in the pinned formalization.

projects.title: A machine-checked bound of 0.6934 for Besicovitch's 1/2-problem
projects.summary: Proves the planar Besicovitch threshold is at most 6934/10000, improving the published 7/10 record. The development formalizes the finite six-point reduction, thirty rational Gram certificates, the endpoint isolation argument, and Besicovitch's classical lower-bound example.

source.title: The bound sigma_1(R^2) <= 6934/10000 for Besicovitch's 1/2-problem

main_results.informal: The planar one-dimensional rectifiability threshold is at most 6934/10000, improving the published upper bound 7/10.
Every threshold strictly above 6934/10000 forces countable one-rectifiability in the plane.
The planar threshold is at least one half, witnessed by Besicovitch's purely unrectifiable example.
Thirty exact rational Gram certificates prove the weighted six-point score is at most -1/2000 for every separated admissible pair in the unit ball.

projects.title: BicausalOT: measurable selection and coupling strategies
projects.summary: Develops Kuratowski–Ryll-Nardzewski selection, Jankov–von Neumann uniformization, and finite-horizon Bellman identities for locally feasible coupling strategies. Exact Borel measurable optimal strategies and initial couplings are obtained on Polish Borel spaces for weakly continuous probability kernels and nonnegative extended-real lower semicontinuous costs. Equivalence with optimization over bicausal path laws is not established.

main_results.informal: A weakly measurable multifunction from an arbitrary measurable space to a Polish space with nonempty closed values admits an everywhere-defined Borel-measurable selector.

projects.title: Chebyshev Quotients and Demazure Multiplicities
projects.summary: Formalizes positivity results for the coefficients of Chebyshev-type polynomial quotients attached to integer partitions, modelling Demazure multiplicities. Proves that the relevant generating function is a polynomial and that its coefficients are eventually positive (Theorem 1), gives explicit Cauchy-product and matrix-inverse formulas for the coefficients (Theorem 2), and establishes their nonnegativity through a Dyck-path lattice counting model (Theorem 3).

source.title: Chebyshev quotients, Demazure multiplicities, and Dyck-path models

main_results.informal: Proves that the generating function attached to a partition is a polynomial whenever its parts are bounded by the parameter `m`.
Proves that the coefficients of the generating function attached to a partition are eventually strictly positive.
Proves that every coefficient of the generating function is nonnegative, via the explicit Dyck-path lattice counting model.

projects.title: The BKAR forest interpolation formula
projects.summary: Proves the Brydges–Kennedy–Abdesselam–Rivasseau forest interpolation formula for smooth functions on a finite complete graph’s edge-coupling space, with unordered forest-cube contributions, ordered sector variants, and choice independence.

main_results.informal: A smooth function evaluated at the all-one configuration is the sum over forests of cube integrals of mixed partial derivatives at path-minimum interpolation points.

projects.title: Block sensitivity can exceed spectral sensitivity squared
projects.summary: Constructs a total Boolean function on 14011 blocks of 144 bits with block sensitivity at least 14011 and squared spectral sensitivity at most U = 7149 + 2 sqrt(150108). Proves the strict separation lambda(f)^2.12 < bs(f), multiplicativity of spectral sensitivity under arbitrary block composition, and an exponential lower bound with factor 14011/U > 1.768 for the self-composed family. Includes reusable finite product probability, an asymmetric Lovasz local lemma, partial Boolean assignments, certificate-family spectral bounds, and a Paley doubly regular tournament. The formalized explicit exponent is 2.12; the exact logarithmic exponent is also retained.

source.title: Block Sensitivity can exceed Spectral Sensitivity Squared

main_results.informal: There exists a total Boolean function on ZMod 14011 times Fin 144 whose block sensitivity strictly exceeds its spectral sensitivity raised to the real exponent 2.12.
main_results.source_ref: Upstream Main.lean; bs_lambda.txt Sections 5-12 and 14.

main_results.informal: There exists a gate labelling whose certificate-union indicator f has bs(f) at least 14011, lambda(f)^2 at most U = 7149 + 2 sqrt(150108), and lambda(f)^alpha at most bs(f), where alpha = 2 log(14011)/log(U) > 2.
main_results.source_ref: Upstream Main.lean; bs_lambda.txt Sections 5-12 and 14.

main_results.informal: A single gate labelling yields, for every natural m, an m-fold self-composition F_m satisfying (14011/U)^m * lambda(F_m)^2 <= bs(F_m). The auxiliary theorem ratio_gt proves 14011/U > 1.768.
main_results.source_ref: Upstream Main.lean; bs_lambda.txt Section 14, division-free bound.

main_results.informal: For any Boolean functions on finite coordinate types, spectral sensitivity of their block composition equals the product of their spectral sensitivities, including the degenerate cases.
main_results.source_ref: Upstream Spectral/Multiplicative.lean; composition theorem used in Section 14.

main_results.informal: In a finite uniform product of nonempty alphabets, events supported on specified coordinate sets have positive probability of all being avoided if each event probability is at most its weight times the product of one minus the weights of its dependent neighbours, with every weight strictly between zero and one.
main_results.source_ref: Upstream LLL/Asymmetric.lean; asymmetric local lemma in Section 10.

projects.title: The Bollobás–Nikiforov conjecture
projects.summary: Proves the Bollobás–Nikiforov conjecture (2007): every finite noncomplete simple graph G on at least two vertices satisfies λ₁(G)² + λ₂(G)² ≤ 2 (1 - 1/ω(G)) |E(G)|, where λ₁ ≥ λ₂ are the two largest adjacency eigenvalues and ω(G) is the clique number. The inequality is derived from a weighted spectral inequality for symmetric entrywise nonnegative matrices supported on the edges of G, which in turn rests on a complete positivity theorem for planar Gram matrices and a rank-two Gram inequality. The rank-two Gram inequality also identifies the conic parameter of Coutinho, Spier and Zhang with the clique number. The supporting library develops the completely positive cone and its closedness, the Motzkin–Straus inequality in completely positive form, total nonnegativity of truncated-square and convex kernels via Cauchy–Binet, weighted Laplacian updates, Schur complements, Perron eigenvectors, the Schur product theorem and Cauchy interlacing over Mathlib.

source.title: The Bollobás–Nikiforov inequality for nonnegative edge weights

main_results.informal: For every finite simple graph G on at least two vertices that is not complete, the two largest adjacency eigenvalues satisfy λ₁(G)² + λ₂(G)² ≤ 2 (1 - 1/ω(G)) |E(G)|, with ω(G) the clique number and |E(G)| the number of edges.

If B is a real symmetric matrix, indexed by a finite type with at least two elements, that is entrywise nonnegative, has zero diagonal and vanishes off the edges of a graph G on that type, then the sum of the squares of its two largest positive eigenvalues is at most (1 - 1/ω(G)) times its squared Frobenius norm.

If planar vectors z₁, …, zₙ lie in a closed half-plane through the origin and X is their Gram matrix, then X ∘ X plus the weighted Laplacian with weights X_ij² on the pairs i < j with X_ij < 0 is completely positive.
For every real positive semidefinite matrix X of rank at most two, ∑_{i,j} (A_G)_ij (X_ij)₊² ≤ (1 - 1/ω(G)) ‖X‖_F², where (·)₊ is the positive part.

For every graph G on a nonempty finite vertex type, the rank-two conic parameter χ''_{vec,3}(G) of Coutinho, Spier and Zhang, defined as the supremum of ‖X‖_F² over positive semidefinite X of rank at most two with nonnegative entries on the edges and unit off-edge mass, equals the clique number ω(G).
Motzkin–Straus inequality; for every entrywise nonnegative vector y, yᵀ A_G y ≤ (1 - 1/ω(G)) (∑ᵢ yᵢ)².
Schur product theorem over the reals; the Hadamard product of two positive semidefinite matrices is positive semidefinite.
The cone of completely positive real matrices is closed.
Cauchy–Binet; the product of two totally nonnegative real matrices is totally nonnegative.
Perron; a real symmetric entrywise nonnegative matrix on a nonempty finite index type has an entrywise nonnegative unit eigenvector for its largest eigenvalue.

projects.title: Boolean Isoperimetry and Conway--Guy Coherent Gaps
projects.summary: Formalizes Harper's vertex-isoperimetric theorem for the Boolean cube: among all families of a fixed cardinality, the simplicial initial segment has the smallest closed radius-one Hamming neighborhood. Develops the supporting binomial-cascade identities, Kruskal--Katona shadow bounds, coordinate compressions, and the final dimension induction. Applies the coherent-gap certificate method to prove normalized consecutive-gap rigidity for the Conway--Guy sequence from its exact recurrence.

source.title: Optimal numberings and isoperimetric problems on graphs; A sum packing problem of Erdős and the Conway--Guy sequence

main_results.informal: For every family of vertices in an n-dimensional Boolean cube, the simplicial initial segment of the same cardinality has a closed radius-one Hamming neighborhood no larger than that of the family.
In every dimension, any real row whose consecutive subset-sum gaps relative to the Conway--Guy reference row are at least one dominates that row coordinatewise.

projects.title: Exact Boolean multiplicative complexity of four-term polynomial multiplication
projects.summary: Proves that multiplying two binary polynomials with n coefficients needs exactly 0, 1, 3, 6, and 9 AND gates for n = 0, 1, 2, 3, and 4, with XOR and constants free and arbitrary reuse of earlier nonlinear wires. The main lower bound excludes every eight-gate circuit for n = 4. Develops Boolean algebraic normal forms equivalent to all Boolean functions, a general circuit model, dimension bounds, circuit rewiring, a Reed-Muller minimum-weight theorem, and exterior-algebra and jet arguments controlling nonlinear feedback.

source.title: Unrestricted Boolean Multiplicative Complexity of Four-Term Binary Polynomial Multiplication: Rational Places, Hasse Jets, and the Failure of Nonlinear Feedback
source.notes: The complete Lean release predates the arXiv v1 submission of 2026-08-31T04:45:12Z. The selected September 22 commit corrects release metadata; eligibility rests on the complete August 31 Lean release at 2ebc0cf42039e4b5de84cb7f9d97cad4791c669d. The August 29 release contained computational artifacts, not the Lean formalization. The author discloses GPT-5.6 Sol for original research and proof development, Opus 5 as a critical referee, and Codex for release preparation. Gregory Morse directed and reviewed the work and assumes responsibility. AI provenance records the proof-producing agent workflow; human direction alone is not classified as mixed formalization. The complete upstream MIT notice is retained in LeanPool/BooleanMultiplication.lean. Only the published n <= 4 dependency closure is imported; no n = 5 or n = 6 claim is made.

main_results.informal: The empty polynomial multiplication map needs zero AND gates.
main_results.source_ref: Proposition 2.3; the n = 0 target has no output coordinates.

main_results.informal: Multiplying two one-coefficient binary polynomials needs exactly one AND gate.
main_results.source_ref: Proposition 2.3.

main_results.informal: Multiplying two two-coefficient binary polynomials needs exactly three AND gates.
main_results.source_ref: Proposition 2.3.

main_results.informal: Multiplying two three-coefficient binary polynomials needs exactly six AND gates.
main_results.source_ref: Proposition 2.4; the lower bound is proved internally.

main_results.informal: Multiplying two four-coefficient binary polynomials needs exactly nine AND gates, allowing free XOR, constants, and unrestricted nonlinear reuse.
main_results.source_ref: Theorem 9.1.

main_results.informal: No eight-AND circuit with free XOR, constants, and arbitrary nonlinear reuse computes all seven output coefficients of the product of two four-coefficient binary polynomials.
main_results.source_ref: Theorem 9.1, lower bound.

projects.title: Brauer Group Core
projects.summary: Formalizes central simple algebra infrastructure, Wedderburn-Artin structure theorems, and finite-field triviality for Brauer groups.

source.title: Central Simple Algebras and Galois Cohomology

main_results.informal: Constructs the Brauer group of a field from Brauer equivalence classes of central simple algebras.
Constructs the Brauer group functor from fields to commutative groups via scalar extension.
Proves a Wedderburn-Artin decomposition for simple Artinian rings as matrix algebras over division rings.
Proves that every element of the Brauer group of a finite field is trivial.
Gives an algebra equivalence form of Wedderburn-Artin for finite-dimensional central simple algebras.
Proves simplicity of tensor products of central simple algebras over a field.
Proves centrality of tensor products of central algebras over a field.
Shows that the division algebra factor in a matrix presentation of a central simple algebra is central over the base field.

projects.title: Brill–Noether theory and gonality of finite graphs
projects.summary: Formalizes Brill–Noether existence through genus five, chains of marked banana graphs and loops, the treewidth lower bound for gonality, and a tricycle example whose gonality drops under regular subdivision. Includes divisor and transmission infrastructure and the Demazure-product support used by vertex gluing.

main_results.informal: Every finite connected loopless multigraph of genus g at most five has, for integers r and d, a divisor of degree d and rank at least r whenever (r + 1) * (g - d + r) ≤ g.

On a finite connected loopless multigraph, for every natural number k, any degree-k divisor of rank at least one bounds the treewidth by k; this is the witness formulation of the treewidth lower bound for divisorial gonality.
There is a graph whose divisorial gonality strictly decreases under a regular subdivision.

projects.title: Brooks' theorem for subcubic graphs
projects.summary: Proves that every finite simple graph of maximum degree at most three with no four-clique admits a three-colouring, without a connectedness assumption. Includes controlled greedy colouring, colouring across cut vertices, and a good-triple argument for cubic components. This is the subcubic case of Brooks' theorem, not the general-degree theorem.

source.title: On colouring the nodes of a network

main_results.informal: Every finite simple graph with maximum degree at most three and no clique on four vertices is three-colourable. The graph may be disconnected.
main_results.source_ref: The subcubic specialization of Brooks' 1941 colouring theorem; the linked Apache-2.0 Lean source proves exactly this specialization.

projects.title: Existence of Nash equilibria via Brouwer's fixed-point theorem
projects.summary: Formalizes Scarf's combinatorial lemma, derives Brouwer's fixed-point theorem on a simplex and on finite products of simplices, and uses it to prove the existence of a mixed Nash equilibrium in every finite game.

main_results.informal: Every finite game has a mixed Nash equilibrium.
main_results.source_ref: J. Nash, Equilibrium Points in N-Person Games, Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 36(1):48-49, 1950, doi:10.1073/pnas.36.1.48.

main_results.informal: Every continuous self-map of a standard simplex has a fixed point.
main_results.source_ref: H. Scarf, The Approximation of Fixed Points of a Continuous Mapping, SIAM Journal on Applied Mathematics 15(5):1328-1343, 1967, doi:10.1137/0115116.

main_results.informal: Every continuous self-map of a finite product of simplices has a fixed point.
main_results.source_ref: H. Scarf, The Approximation of Fixed Points of a Continuous Mapping, SIAM Journal on Applied Mathematics 15(5):1328-1343, 1967, doi:10.1137/0115116.

main_results.informal: Scarf's combinatorial lemma producing a colorful simplex.
main_results.source_ref: H. Scarf, The Approximation of Fixed Points of a Continuous Mapping, SIAM Journal on Applied Mathematics 15(5):1328-1343, 1967, doi:10.1137/0115116.

main_results.informal: The structure of a finite game with finitely many players and finite pure strategy sets.
main_results.source_ref: J. Nash, Equilibrium Points in N-Person Games, Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 36(1):48-49, 1950, doi:10.1073/pnas.36.1.48.

main_results.informal: The predicate that a mixed strategy profile is a Nash equilibrium.
main_results.source_ref: J. Nash, Equilibrium Points in N-Person Games, Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 36(1):48-49, 1950, doi:10.1073/pnas.36.1.48.

projects.title: Formalisation of the Bruhat-Tits Tree
projects.summary: Formalizes the Bruhat-Tits tree for GL₂ over the fraction field of a discrete valuation ring.

source.title: Trees

main_results.informal: Proves that the Bruhat-Tits graph is a tree.
Proves regularity of the Bruhat-Tits graph when the residue field is finite.
Proves surjectivity of the Bruhat-Tits Laplacian on harmonic cochains.

projects.title: Burkholder Martingale Transform Inequality
projects.summary: Formalizes Burkholder's sharp Lp inequality for real-valued martingale transforms: if `f` is a discrete martingale and `w` a predictable multiplier bounded by `1`, then the Lp norm of the transform `w ⋆ₘ f` is at most `(pStar p - 1)` times the Lp norm of `f`, where `pStar p` is the maximum of `p` and its conjugate exponent. The proof builds the Burkholder special function as a majorant of the relevant payoff in each exponent regime (`1 < p < 2`, `p = 2`, `p > 2`).

source.title: Boundary value problems and sharp inequalities for martingale transforms

main_results.informal: The sharp Lp Burkholder inequality: for a discrete martingale `f` and a predictable multiplier `w` with `|w n| ≤ 1`, the Lp norm of the martingale transform `(w ⋆ₘ f) n` is bounded by `(pStar p - 1)` times the Lp norm of `f n`.
The martingale transform of a martingale by a strongly predictable bounded multiplier is itself a martingale.
For every exponent `p > 1` there exists a Burkholder majorant, the special function dominating the payoff and driving the inequality.

projects.title: Caffarelli–Kohn–Nirenberg partial regularity
projects.summary: Partial regularity for three-dimensional incompressible Navier–Stokes suitable weak solutions with locally L^q forcing, q > 5/2: quantitative epsilon regularity and vanishing parabolic one-dimensional Hausdorff measure of the singular set. Includes the supporting Sobolev, singular integral, pressure, heat-potential and parabolic Morrey infrastructure, equivalence of suitable-solution formulations, and a nonzero shear-flow example. Includes the completed Leray, pressure, and linear regularity support needed by further Navier–Stokes regularity projects.

main_results.informal: For q > 5/2, sufficiently small unit-cylinder L^3 velocity, L^(3/2) pressure and L^q force masses give an almost-everywhere equal quantitatively bounded parabolic Holder representative on the closed half-cylinder and regularity at each point of its open interior.
A sufficiently small extended nonnegative limsup of the normalized squared weak-gradient mass implies regularity at an interior point of a suitable weak solution.
The singular set of a suitable weak solution with locally L^q forcing, q > 5/2, has zero one-dimensional Hausdorff measure in the parabolic metric.
The manuscript's suitable weak-solution predicate is equivalent to the predicate that explicitly requires integrability of all tested weak-equation and local-energy integrands.
The nonzero decaying sinusoidal shear flow with zero pressure and force is a suitable weak solution on all space and times in (0,1).

projects.title: Polynomial degree bounds for rational points on varieties
projects.summary: Proves the six main results of Castryck, Cluckers, Dittmann and Nguyen on dimension growth, uniform rational-point counts on curves and hypersurfaces, a lower-bound curve construction, and two-torsion in number-field class groups. Preserves the determinant method, Hilbert-function degree and dimension, bounded birational projections, and the required Bombieri-Vaaler and Mertens dependencies. Imports the main-result closure, excluding the separate intermediate-statement and counterexample library.

source.title: The dimension growth conjecture, polynomial in the degree and without logarithmic factors

main_results.informal: For every ambient projective dimension n, a constant depending only on n bounds the rational points of height at most B on every integral projective variety of degree d at least five by C d^(2n^2+5n-5) B^dim(X), for B at least one.

In ambient dimension n at least two and for B at least one, every integral projective curve of degree d has at most C(n) d^4 B^(2/d) rational points of height at most B, uniformly in its coefficients.
In ambient dimension n at least two and for B at least one, every integral affine curve of degree d has at most C(n) d^3 B^(1/d) (log B+d) integer points in the box of radius B.

In N at least three variables, an affine hypersurface of degree d at least five whose top form is absolutely irreducible has at most C(N) d^(3N+9) B^(N-2) integer points in the box of radius B, for B at least one.
For every positive degree d, an integral projective plane curve and a radius B at least one attain at least d^2 B^(2/d)/5 rational points of height at most B.
For number fields K of degree n at least three, the two-torsion cardinality is at most C(n) |disc K|^(1/2-1/(2n)) (log |disc K|)^(1-(n mod 2)).

projects.title: Finite Čencov-Petz Uniqueness
projects.summary: Formalizes the finite/discrete Čencov-Petz uniqueness theorem, showing that any continuous metric family on finite probability simplexes that is monotone under Markov morphisms is a scalar multiple of the Fisher information metric.

source.title: Statistical Decision Rules and Optimal Inference

main_results.informal: Proves that every continuous monotone metric family on a finite probability simplex is a scalar multiple of the Fisher information metric.
main_results.source_ref: N. N. Chentsov, Statistical Decision Rules and Optimal Inference, AMS Translations of Mathematical Monographs 53, 1982.

main_results.informal: Establishes the scalar Fisher-form identity at rational simplex points using split representations.
Proves the scalar Fisher-form identity for simplex points represented as pushforwards of uniform distributions under splitting maps.
Shows that the uniform-point scalar is independent of simplex dimension once the dimension is at least two.
Proves that the permutation-invariant bilinear form at a uniform finite simplex point is a scalar multiple of the Fisher bilinear form.

projects.title: Bounds for the centered Hardy-Littlewood maximal constant
projects.summary: Proves that the weak type (1,1) constant c_2 of the centered maximal operator over axis-parallel squares is at least the explicit radical phi, approximately 1.68551, using a weighted periodic lattice and integrable approximations. Also proves c_d <= 2^d in every natural dimension and 1.685 < phi < 1.686. The operator acts on real-valued integrable functions, with Lebesgue outer measure of strict level sets. Includes the maximal-function API, a Vitali covering argument, lattice witnesses, smearing estimates, and the limiting lower bound. No optimality of phi is claimed.

source.title: A lower bound 1.6855 for the planar centred maximal constant over squares
source.notes: First completed publicly on 2026-09-18 at 22:15:07 UTC in commit 06a726f113241d445903f0c0eae1ebe40d8b539f. The lower bound is documented and proved in upstream docs/PROOF.md; the weighted smearing argument adapts Aldaz (2000), Lemma 1.1, and the covering upper bound follows Tao's 245A Notes 5, Exercise 42. Upstream formalization.yaml and docs/HISTORY.md disclose AI generation of the configuration and proofs under Yongxi Lin's direction.

main_results.informal: The explicit radical phi is a lower bound for c_2, the infimum of all weak type (1,1) bounds for the centered maximal operator over axis-parallel squares in the real plane.
For every natural number d, including zero, the centered maximal operator over axis-parallel cubes in real d-space has weak type (1,1) constant c_d at most 2^d.
The explicit radical constant phi lies strictly between 1.685 and 1.686.

projects.title: Champernowne normality in every base
projects.summary: Proves that concatenating the base-b digits of the positive integers gives a normal digit sequence for every integer base b at least 2: every nonempty length-k word of digits below b has limiting frequency b^(-k). This is a discrete, all-base generalization of D. G. Champernowne's 1933 base-ten result, without a real-number expansion bridge. Includes reusable substring-counting inequalities, a digit-string equivalence, exact cohort counts, and quantitative prefix bounds used to establish the frequency limit.

source.title: Champernowne Sequence Normality Proof

main_results.informal: For every integer base b at least 2, the sequence formed by concatenating the base-b digits of 1, 2, 3, and so on is normal: each nonempty word w of digits below b has limiting occurrence frequency 1 / b^(length w), counting overlapping occurrences.
The decimal digit sequence 123456789101112... is normal in base ten.

For a nonempty length-k word of base-b digits with nonzero first digit and k at most m, its total occurrences inside all m-digit positive integers equal b^(m-k) + (m-k)(b-1)b^(m-k-1), with natural subtraction in the exponents.

For a nonempty length-k word of base-b digits starting with zero and k at most m, its total occurrences inside all m-digit positive integers equal (m-k)(b-1)b^(m-k-1), with natural subtraction in the exponent.

projects.title: Uniqueness of Shannon Capacity-Achieving Priors
projects.summary: Formalizes uniqueness of the capacity-achieving input distribution for a Markov-kernel channel in three aligned layers: a finite-alphabet theorem (compactness, continuity, and strict concavity of mutual information on Mathlib's weak topology for `ProbabilityMeasure`), a concrete discharged theorem for compact-Polish channels with a common strictly positive jointly continuous density, and a general measure-theoretic packaging that isolates the abstract well-conditioning hypotheses, plus a counterexample showing pairwise-distinct rows do not give an injective prior pushforward (the non-degeneracy required for uniqueness).

source.title: Elements of Information Theory

main_results.informal: For a Markov kernel between finite alphabets (nonempty input) whose rows are linearly independent (`Kernel.RowMatrixFullRank`), a capacity-achieving input prior exists and is unique.
main_results.source_ref: R. G. Gallager, Information Theory and Reliable Communication, Wiley, 1968, Section 4.5.

main_results.informal: For compact-Polish channels with a common strictly positive jointly continuous density, given injectivity of the prior-pushforward map and upper semicontinuity of mutual information (the latter carried as a field of `Kernel.ContinuousPositiveDensity`, not derived), the capacity-achieving prior is unique.
General measure-theoretic packaging: under abstract well-conditioning hypotheses, the capacity-achieving prior is unique.

projects.title: Chip-Firing with Lean 4
projects.summary: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Baker and Norine's Riemann-Roch theorem for finite graphs. Chip configurations on a finite graph, modulo chip-firing moves, form an abelian group analogous to the group of line bundles on a compact Riemann surface. Each class can be assigned a rank, analogous to the dimension of a linear series. These ranks then satisfy a formula of the form r(D) - r(K-D) = deg D + 1 - g, in exact analogy to Riemann surfaces. This formula is formalized, along with the analog of Clifford's theorem for finite graphs.

main_results.informal: For a finite connected graph, the ranks of a divisor and its canonical complement satisfy the graph Riemann–Roch formula.
For a special divisor on a finite connected graph, its rank is at most half its degree.

projects.title: A Detailed Proof of the Chudnovsky Formula
projects.summary: Formalizes the Chudnovsky brothers' rapidly convergent series for 1/π, proving Mathlib's `chudnovskySum = π⁻¹`. Follows Milla's elementary complex-analytic proof: Weierstrass and Eisenstein theory, Liouville and parallelogram-residue calculus, the Kummer hypergeometric bridge and the main modular identity relating the j-invariant to the lattice periods, Baker's division-value machinery, and the singular-moduli inputs at the CM point τ = (1 + √-163)/2 — integrality of j(τ) via modular polynomials and Kronecker's congruence, and rationality of the Weierstrass s₂ invariant via Masser's Appendix A.1.

source.title: A Detailed Proof of the Chudnovsky Formula

main_results.informal: Proves the Chudnovsky series identity, i.e. Mathlib's `chudnovskySum = π⁻¹`: the series (12 / 640320^(3/2)) · ∑ₙ (-1)ⁿ (6n)! (545140134 n + 13591409) / ((3n)! (n!)³ 640320^(3n)) sums to 1/π.

projects.title: Chvátal's conjecture and sharp Boolean correlation
projects.summary: Formalizes Chang, Liu, and Liu's proof that a hereditary family on a finite nonempty ground set has a largest intersecting subfamily that is a star. Develops the sharp Boolean Fourier correlation inequality, its antipodal and quadratic forms, sharpness examples, and the weighted star theorem for nonnegative decreasing weights.

source.title: A proof of Chvátal's conjecture via a sharp correlation inequality
source.notes: GPT-6 generated the formalization under Boon Suan Ho's direction; the mathematical proof is due to Chang, Liu, and Liu. No human expert review or source-author endorsement is claimed. The upstream MIT copyright and permission notice is retained in every imported file.

main_results.informal: Every intersecting subfamily A of a hereditary finite family D on a finite nonempty ground type has cardinality at most that of some star of D.
One star of D is itself intersecting and simultaneously dominates all intersecting subfamilies of the hereditary family D in size, on a finite nonempty ground type.

For increasing Boolean functions f and g on any finite cube, the sum of squared Fourier coefficients of g weighted by the largest influence of f on each nonempty index is at most the harmonic mean of Cov(f,g) and Cov(f,g*), with zero-denominator value zero.
For increasing Boolean f and g and every real t, twice their squared Fourier energy over index pairs with odd intersection is bounded by t^2 Cov(f,g) + (1-t)^2 Cov(f,g*).
If g is also self-dual and the finite coordinate type is nonempty, Cov(f,g) is at least one quarter of f's minimum coordinate influence.
The AND function attains equality in the sharp correlation bound for every increasing Boolean second function, including constants.
For any nonnegative antitone real weight on subsets of a finite nonempty ground type, one full-cube star is intersecting and its total weight dominates every intersecting family.

projects.title: Circuit Complexity in Lean 4
projects.summary: A Lean 4 formalization of classical Boolean circuit complexity, including the Shannon counting lower bound, Schnorr's XOR gate lower bound, a gate-elimination lower bound, CNF/DNF lower bounds for parity, and nondeterministic quantification complexity bounds.

main_results.informal: For N at least 6, there exists a Boolean function on N inputs that cannot be computed by any fan-in-2 AND/OR circuit of size at most 2^N / (5N).
Any fan-in-2 AND/OR circuit computing the N-input XOR function (or its complement) has at least 2(N-1) internal gates.
Any circuit over bounded fan-in k AND/OR computing a function with n' essential inputs has size at least n' / k.
Any DNF formula computing the N-input XOR function requires at least 2^(N-1) terms.
Any CNF formula computing the N-input XOR function requires at least 2^(N-1) clauses.
If a function f has circuit complexity s, then the existential quantification of f over a k-bit block has circuit complexity at most 2^k * (s + 1).

projects.title: circuitlib: a circuit verification library for Lean 4
projects.summary: A categorical semantics framework for digital circuits over Belnap's four-valued logic, following Ghica-Kaye-Sprunger. Its main theorems prove that combinational circuits (monotone functions on wire vectors) and sequential circuits (causal monotone stream functions) form symmetric monoidal categories, with a verified full adder as demonstration.

main_results.informal: The category of sequential circuits, whose morphisms are causal monotone stream functions as in Ghica-Kaye-Sprunger's denotational semantics, is symmetric monoidal, with all coherence laws (pentagon, triangle, hexagons, symmetry) proven.
The category of combinational circuits, with wire counts as objects and monotone wire-vector functions as morphisms, is symmetric monoidal under juxtaposition of wire bundles.
Causality is preserved by parallel composition, the key lemma making sequential circuits closed under the tensor product.
Belnap's four truth values under the information order form a join-semilattice, the wire-value semantics in which every circuit denotes a monotone function.
Correctness of a full adder assembled categorically from two half adders, gates, braidings, and whiskerings, computing the Boolean sum and carry bits; a demonstration of the framework.

projects.title: Regularity of asymptotically axisymmetric Navier–Stokes solutions
projects.summary: Proves the Constantin–Ignatova–Vicol regularity theorem for suitable weak solutions of the three-dimensional forced Navier–Stokes equations with analytic forcing, anisotropic Type II bounds on the angular mean, and an axisymmetric core at each time. Includes the fully axisymmetric theorem, meridional smallness, interior spatial analyticity, the nonanalyticity consequence for singular solutions, and the comparison, Serrin, and Gustafson–Kang–Tsai results used in their proofs. Reuses Lean Pool's Caffarelli–Kohn–Nirenberg suitable-solution and analysis library.

main_results.informal: A smooth suitable weak solution on the unit parabolic cylinder with globally finite energy, bounded C^2 spatially analytic force, anisotropic Type II bounds on its angular mean, and a positive axisymmetric core at every time is axisymmetric throughout the cylinder and bounded near the origin up to the terminal time.
An axisymmetric smooth suitable weak solution obeying the stated anisotropic Type II bounds and bounded C^2 force is bounded near the origin up to the terminal time.
Under the axisymmetric anisotropic hypotheses, the weighted meridional quantity tends uniformly to zero on a smaller cylinder as the terminal time approaches.
Smooth solutions with locally uniformly spatially analytic forcing are locally uniformly spatially analytic in the interior.

For a smooth suitable weak solution with globally finite energy, bounded C^2 forcing, angular-mean anisotropic bounds, and an axisymmetric core at every time, failure of boundedness near the origin implies that the force is not spatially analytic, is nonzero somewhere in the unit cylinder, and has a nonzero point in every smaller terminal cylinder.

projects.title: Classical graph colouring through lists, orientations and spectra
projects.summary: Proves Kőnig's edge-colouring theorem for finite bipartite simple graphs by reusing Lean Pool's Vizing partial-colouring and Kempe-chain infrastructure. A stable-matching theorem for strict preferences and incomplete acceptability lists supplies kernels for Galvin's orientation of the line graph. This gives list edge colouring from lists of size at least the maximum degree and the Dinitz array theorem. Gallai–Hasse–Roy–Vitaver relates graph colourings to directed paths (with a bridge to Lean Pool's digraph simple-path API), while Wilf's and Hoffman's eigenvalue bounds control the chromatic and independence numbers. Two interface corollaries turn the spectral colouring bounds into directed-path bounds. Existing Vizing, matching-cover, poset and equitable-colouring results are reused or left in their established Lean Pool projects rather than copied.

source.title: The List Chromatic Index of a Bipartite Multigraph
source.note: Formalizes the finite simple-graph case. The Kőnig edge-colouring proof comes from jtraverso/konig-edge-colouring at 7c60f7efb69c1747aaf39e5dfa7a89d907cd84ef (Palomar PALOMAR-2026-10-15-000019). The Galvin, Dinitz and stable-matching proofs come from PALOMAR-2026-10-18-000029. Gallai–Roy comes from jtraverso/gallai-roy at e737218bf80c3d3684d670f5f8aa9a8257e1a52f (PALOMAR-2026-10-16-000015), and the spectral bounds from jtraverso/spectral-graph-bounds at 8d8b4ce17e56165b5f1ad3b285fb141666804e1c (PALOMAR-2026-10-18-000016). The source's copied Vizing files are omitted in favour of the existing Lean Pool project.

main_results.informal: A finite bipartite simple graph has a proper edge colouring using its maximum degree many colours.
The chromatic index of a finite bipartite simple graph equals its maximum degree.
Finite strict-preference matching instances with incomplete acceptability lists have a stable matching.
Every finite bipartite simple graph admits a proper edge colouring from arbitrary edge lists of size at least its maximum degree.
An n by n array of lists of at least n symbols per cell admits a choice of symbols distinct within every row and every column.
If every directed path in an orientation of a finite graph has at most k vertices, then the graph is k-colourable.
Every k-colourable finite graph has an orientation with no directed path on more than k vertices.
main_results.source_ref: Gallai–Hasse–Roy–Vitaver theorem; PALOMAR-2026-10-16-000015.

main_results.informal: The average degree of a finite graph is at most its largest adjacency eigenvalue.
main_results.source_ref: Collatz–Sinogowitz; PALOMAR-2026-10-18-000016.

main_results.informal: The largest adjacency eigenvalue is at most the maximum degree.
main_results.source_ref: Collatz–Sinogowitz; PALOMAR-2026-10-18-000016.

main_results.informal: A finite graph is colourable with floor of its largest adjacency eigenvalue plus one colours.
If a finite graph has an edge, every proper colouring uses at least one minus the ratio of the largest and smallest adjacency eigenvalues colours.

projects.title: Classical matching and factor theorems in finite graphs
projects.summary: Develops augmenting-path and odd-component certificates for maximum matchings, bipartite matching-cover duality, perfect matchings in bridgeless cubic graphs, Tutte's f-factor criterion, and decompositions of even-regular graphs into two-factors. Includes the finite Dilworth and Mirsky partition theorems as an order-theoretic companion. All graph results use Mathlib's SimpleGraph and matching predicates. Hall's and Tutte's one-factor theorems are imported from Mathlib; the general matching and factor conclusions are proved here. The collection integrates five Palomar-registered developments and does not claim new mathematical results or a formalization of polynomial-time algorithms.

source.title: A Short Proof of the Factor Theorem for Finite Graphs
source.note: This source anchors the f-factor development. The other four frozen source repositories, their commits and Palomar IDs are linked in the imported module docstrings; each main result below identifies its mathematical source.

main_results.informal: A matching in a finite simple graph has maximum cardinality if and only if it has no augmenting path, with distinct unmatched endpoints and alternating edges.

A finite simple graph has a spanning subgraph with prescribed nonnegative integer vertex degrees f exactly when Tutte's odd-component inequality holds for every pair of disjoint vertex sets S and T.
Every finite simple graph of degree 2k at every vertex is the edge-disjoint union of k spanning subgraphs of degree two at every vertex, including k equal to zero.
A finite partially ordered set has an antichain A and a partition into the size of A chains.

main_results.informal: A finite partially ordered set has a chain C and a partition into the size of C antichains.

projects.title: Common-neighbour counterexamples for Saxl graphs
projects.summary: Proves that for every base size B at least two and every prescribed degree bound, there is a finite faithful primitive permutation group of at least that degree and exact base size B whose generalized Saxl graph contains two nonadjacent vertices with no common neighbor. The supporting library constructs an explicit infinite family from binary deleted permutation modules over finite fields and proves the required base-size, irreducibility, primitivity, and graph-theoretic properties.

For every odd d with 3 ≤ d and every tail, the explicit affine wreath-product family has exact base size tail + 2, acts primitively, and its displayed pair has no common neighbor in the corresponding generalized Saxl graph.

projects.title: Spectral theorem for compact self-adjoint operators
projects.summary: Formalizes the spectral theorem for compact self-adjoint operators on a Hilbert space: such an operator admits a Hilbert basis of eigenvectors. The development passes from weak compactness of Hilbert closed balls and Rayleigh-quotient extrema to an eigenvector at the operator norm, finiteness of the point spectrum outside any neighbourhood of zero, finite-rank cutoff approximation, and finally the orthogonal decomposition into eigenspaces.

projects.title: Counterexamples to graph compactness and two-degenerate extremal bounds
projects.summary: Formalizes two counterexamples in extremal graph theory. The first gives a finite family of connected bipartite cyclic graphs whose family extremal number grows strictly slower than every member's extremal number, disproving the Erdős--Simonovits compactness conjecture. The second constructs a connected bipartite two-degenerate graph with extremal number at least c n^(3/2+ε), disproving the proposed universal n^(3/2) upper bound under the stated bipartition degree condition.

source.title: Ten Advances in Mathematics and Theoretical Computer Science

main_results.informal: There is a nonempty finite family of connected bipartite cyclic graphs such that every member has a uniform positive n^(4/3)-scale extremal lower bound, while every family-free host on n vertices has its sixteenth power of the edge count bounded by a constant times n^21. Consequently the family is not compact and the Erdős--Simonovits compactness conjecture is false.

There is a connected bipartite two-degenerate finite graph H such that each side of every two-coloring has a vertex of degree greater than two, yet ex(n,H) is eventually at least c n^(3/2+ε) for some positive constants c and ε.

projects.title: Composition Algebras over Commutative Rings
projects.summary: Develops conic algebras, Cayley--Dickson doubling, and finitely generated projective composition algebras over an arbitrary commutative ring, following Garibaldi, Petersson and Racine. Composition algebras are alternative over every base. Over a nontrivial base, if the underlying module has constant rank, that rank is 1, 2, 4 or 8. Over LG rings, a class containing all fields and semilocal rings, composition algebras are classified by their norms, and reduced composition algebras are shown to be split. Along the way the project proves Witt cancellation for quadratic forms over LG rings by the elementary Dias--Baeza--Knebusch route, Artin's theorem that a ring is alternative if and only if its two-generated subrings are associative, freeness of constant-rank projective modules over LG rings, and the classification of composition algebras over the reals and over finite fields. These main results do not assume that 2 is invertible.

source.title: Albert Algebras over Commutative Rings

main_results.informal: Witt cancellation over an LG ring. If the orthogonal sums of q1 and of q2 with q3 are isometric, where q2 is nonsingular and q3 is regular on finitely generated projective modules, then q1 and q2 are isometric.
Artin's theorem. A non-associative ring is alternative if and only if every subring generated by two elements is associative.
Over an LG ring, a finitely generated projective module of constant rank is free.
Every composition algebra over every commutative ring is alternative, with no hypothesis on 2, on the rank, or on nontriviality of the base ring.

A composition algebra of constant rank over a nontrivial commutative ring has rank 1, 2, 4 or 8; it is the base ring in rank 1, commutative and associative in rank 2, associative but not commutative in rank 4, and alternative but not associative in rank 8.
Over an LG ring, composition algebras with isometric norms are isomorphic.
Over an LG ring, every reduced composition algebra is split.

projects.title: Hurwitz's Classification of Euclidean Composition Algebras
projects.summary: Formalizes Hurwitz's classification of nontrivial finite-dimensional real Euclidean composition algebras: every such algebra has dimension 1, 2, 4, or 8 and is real-linearly equivalent to the real numbers, complex numbers, quaternions, or octonions through a map preserving the unit, multiplication, and norm form. The development also constructs the octonions from an explicit Fano multiplication table, proves Degen's eight-square identity, and shows that Cayley--Dickson doubling preserves the composition law for associative inputs.

source.title: Über die Composition der quadratischen Formen von beliebig vielen Variablen

main_results.informal: Every nontrivial finite-dimensional real Euclidean composition algebra is linearly equivalent to the real numbers, complex numbers, quaternions, or octonions through a map preserving the unit, multiplication, and norm form.
The real dimension of a nontrivial finite-dimensional Euclidean composition algebra is exactly 1, 2, 4, or 8.
The Cayley--Dickson double of a nontrivial associative Euclidean composition algebra again satisfies the composition law.
Any octonion that associates in the third slot with every pair has zero imaginary coordinates and hence lies on the real line.

projects.title: Oracle Computability and Turing Degrees
projects.summary: Formalizes oracle-relative computability via partial recursive functions, Turing reducibility and the Turing degrees as an upper semilattice, a Gödel numbering with a universal oracle machine, the jump operator, and the arithmetical hierarchy.

Universality of the oracle evaluator `evalo`, that is, `RecursiveIn (Set.range g) f` holds iff there is a code `c` with `evalo g c = f`.
`f` is Turing reducible to `g` (`f ≤ᵀ g`) when `f` is recursive in the singleton oracle set `{g}`.
The type of Turing degrees, the antisymmetrization of partial functions under Turing reducibility.
The original function is Turing reducible to its jump, `f ≤ᵀ f⌜`.
The Turing degrees form an upper semilattice with the Turing join as supremum.

projects.title: Verified interval-Cauchy real arithmetic
projects.summary: Represents real numbers as Cauchy sequences of nested rational intervals quotiented into a field, with executable interval ring arithmetic, proven-convergent rational bounds for sqrt, exp, and pi, and an IsComputable typeclass that packages such approximations to drive classical (noncomputable) comparison instances, after O'Connor's certified exact real computation.

main_results.informal: A sequence of converging rational lower and upper bounds representing a single real number.
The quotient of interval-Cauchy sequences by equality of value, an ordered field whose ring operations are executable interval arithmetic.
A typeclass packaging an explicit interval-Cauchy approximation of a real number, used to drive its classical comparison instances.
The field instance on the quotient; inversion extracts a sign witness classically and is noncomputable.
Computes converging rational interval bounds for the square root of a rational interval.

projects.title: Bennett--Bernstein, Freedman, and Hoeffding concentration inequalities
projects.summary: Develops variance-sensitive sub-gamma moment-generating-function estimates, Bennett and Bernstein bounds, a Freedman--Bernstein upper tail for finite adapted sums, conditional and independent-variable Hoeffding inequalities.

A finite adapted sum of conditionally sub-gamma increments satisfies the corresponding variance-sensitive Freedman--Bernstein upper-tail bound.

A sum of finitely many independent random variables valued in the unit interval exceeds its mean by t with probability at most exp(-2 t squared divided by the number of terms).

projects.title: Newman normalizer bounds for congruence subgroups
projects.summary: Characterizes the normalizer of Gamma0(N) in SL(2, R), for every positive level N, by explicit integral matrices scaled by a square root. Extends the necessary matrix form to GammaDelta(N) for every subgroup Delta of the units modulo N. Preserves Atkin-Lehner elements, rational representatives, integral matrix lattices, prime valuations and a generic normalizer argument. The upstream finite presentations, group orders and modular-curve automorphism classifications are outside this import's scope.

source.title: The normalizer of Gamma0(N) in PSL(2, R)

main_results.informal: For N > 0, put h = 2^min(3, floor(v_2(N)/2)) times 3^min(1, floor(v_3(N)/2)) and n = N/h^2. A real determinant-one matrix normalizes Gamma0(N) exactly when it equals plus or minus 1/sqrt(e) times [[a*e, b/h], [N*c/h, d*e]], for integers a, b, c, d and a positive divisor e of n satisfying a*d*e^2 - b*c*n = e.

For N > 0 and Delta a subgroup of the units modulo N, let epsilon be gcd(N, u^2 - 1 for representatives u in Delta), and let h be the product over primes p dividing N of p^min(v_p(epsilon), floor(v_p(N)/2)). Every determinant-one real matrix normalizing GammaDelta(N) has the same integral Newman form with this h and n = N/h^2. This is a necessary bound; no converse for GammaDelta(N) is asserted.
At every positive level, h(N) is the greatest divisor of 24 whose square divides N.
