projects.title: A 21-state Turing machine for Goldbach's conjecture
projects.summary: A concrete 21-state binary Turing machine halts on the blank tape exactly when Goldbach's conjecture is false. The proof connects it to the earlier 25-state machine, verifies both machines' prime-search semantics, and preserves finite-machine execution, tape-scanning and reachability infrastructure. This imports only the Goldbach dependency closure of Cryptids, excluding its Riemann, ZF and Busy Beaver developments.

main_results.informal: The explicit 21-state binary Turing machine halts from the blank tape if and only if some even natural number greater than two is not the sum of two primes.
The explicit 21-state and 25-state binary machines have the same blank-tape halting behavior.
The candidate machine has 21 states, strictly fewer than the reference's 25.
The 25-state reference machine halts from the blank tape exactly when Goldbach's conjecture is false.

projects.title: Period Lengths of Rational Cut-and-Project Gap Sequences
projects.summary: Formalizes the closed-form minimal periods of one-dimensional rational cut-and-project gap sequences at the level of the paper's residue model, plus a fully geometric aperiodicity theorem for irrational slopes. For coprime α, β ∈ ℕ and window parameter ω ≥ 0, write N = ⌊ωα⌋ + ⌊ωβ⌋ + 1 and D = α² + β². The strip-to-residue reduction of the paper — sorting the hits of the length-N progression twisted by the geometric multiplier −αβ⁻¹ (mod D) — is taken as the definition of the gap sequence rather than derived from the lattice; for it, the multiset convention has minimal period N/D when D ∣ N and N otherwise, and the set convention (multiplicities flattened to {0,1}) has minimal period 1 when N ≥ D and N otherwise. The irrational case is geometric from first principles: for positive irrational slope and ω > 0, the accepted points of ℤ² sorted by the physical projection have a gap sequence with no finite period, via injectivity of the projection and Kronecker density of the internal image.

source.title: Period lengths of one-dimensional rational cut-and-project sequences

main_results.informal: The gap sequence of the residue model of the rational cut-and-project multiset (sorted hits of the length-N progression under the multiplier −αβ⁻¹ mod D) has minimal period N/D if D divides N and N otherwise, where N = ⌊ωα⌋ + ⌊ωβ⌋ + 1 and D = α² + β².
The set-convention residue-model gap sequence (multiplicities flattened to {0,1}) has minimal period 1 if N ≥ D and N otherwise.
For positive irrational slope and window parameter ω > 0, the projected gap sequence has no finite period.

projects.title: The density Hales–Jewett theorem and Szemerédi's theorem
projects.summary: A Lean 4 formalization of the density Hales–Jewett theorem: for every finite alphabet α and every density δ > 0, all sufficiently large n have the property that any set of at least δ·|α|^n words of length n over α contains a combinatorial line. The basis for the formalization is the combinatorial proof of Dodos, Kanellopoulos, and Tyros. As a consequence, we also formalize Szemerédi's theorem on the integers: for every k ≥ 3 and δ > 0, the following holds for all sufficiently large n. Any subset of {0, …, n−1} of size at least δ·n contains a nonconstant arithmetic progression of length k. The thresholds are explicit: the density Hales–Jewett theorem holds for n ≥ A(4|α|, |α| + ⌈1/δ⌉) and Szemerédi's theorem for n ≥ A(4k + 1, k + ⌈1/δ⌉), where A is the Ackermann function, built on Shelah's bound for the Hales–Jewett numbers from the ShelahHalesJewett project. Varnavides' theorem gives at least n²/A(4k + 1, k + ⌈1/δ⌉) such progressions.

main_results.informal: Every positive-density subset of sufficiently long words over a finite nontrivial alphabet contains a combinatorial line.

For δ > 0, the density Hales–Jewett number of k letters and density δ is at most A(4k, k + ⌈1/δ⌉).
For k ≥ 3, δ > 0 and n ≥ A(4k + 1, k + ⌈1/δ⌉), every subset of {0, …, n − 1} with at least δn elements contains a nonconstant arithmetic progression of length k.
Under the same hypotheses, the subset contains at least n²/A(4k + 1, k + ⌈1/δ⌉) arithmetic progressions of length k.

projects.title: Descriptive counting complexity and parsimonious completeness of #SAT
projects.summary: Defines counting problems on finite nonempty relational structures, existential second-order witness counts, and first-order counting reductions. projects.title: Dilatations of categories and commutative rings
projects.summary: Constructs categorical dilatations from sieves of permitted numerators and denominator morphisms, and proves their universal property for Sigma-regular functors satisfying the sieve containment condition. Develops restriction and union of centers, dual codilatations, and ordinary localization as a special case. The composition isomorphism retains the explicit Sigma-regularity hypothesis left open in the original paper. For commutative rings, an exponent-profile center recovers the ring dilatation; the naive single-index comparison is refuted over Z[X]. A finite category example refutes a general intermediate-category characterization. Independent ring modules provide fraction arithmetic, a universal property, reindexing, and the unique isomorphism for two-stage dilatations.

source.title: Dilatations of categories, via their Lean formalization

projects.provenance_note: Mayeux's paper discloses Claude assistance under the author's direction; it does not quantify the share of generated proofs. The development incorporates Mayeux and Zhang's earlier ring formalization. This port includes substantial AI proof repair, optimization, and documentation.

main_results.informal: For a nonempty indexed center in a category C and a functor F from C to D, assume that localization of D at the images of the chosen denominators is faithful and that each pushed-forward numerator sieve lies in the sieve generated by its mapped denominator. There is a unique functor from the dilatation to D whose composite with the canonical functor from C is F.
main_results.source_ref: Section 5; original Theorem 3.10.

main_results.informal: The successive dilatation at Z and the pushforward of W is isomorphic to the dilatation at the combined center Z.sum W, assuming that the composite canonical functor to the successive dilatation is Sigma-regular for Z.sum W. This regularity is an explicit hypothesis, not a theorem of the development.
main_results.source_ref: Section 8.2 and Appendix B; conditional original Proposition 3.15.

main_results.informal: For two families of numerator sieves with the same denominator morphisms, dilating at their combined two-copy center is isomorphic to dilating at the pointwise union of the sieves.
main_results.source_ref: Section 8.3; original Proposition 3.18.

main_results.informal: For any multicenter in a commutative ring A, the categorical dilatation of the multiplicative one-object category of A at all finitely supported exponent profiles is isomorphic to the one-object category of the ring dilatation A[M]. At profile nu, the denominator is the product of a_i raised to nu_i and the numerator ideal is the product of (M_i + (a_i)) raised to nu_i.
main_results.source_ref: Theorem 10.1; corrected original Proposition 5.1.

main_results.informal: For A = Z[X], ideal (X), and denominator 2, there is no equivalence from the categorical dilatation at the naive one-index center to the one-object category of the ring dilatation that commutes strictly with the canonical functors from the base category.
main_results.source_ref: Section 10.2 and Appendix B.

main_results.informal: The constructed category with three arrows from X to Y admits no equivalence to a dilatation of the base category with two such arrows that commutes strictly with the canonical base functors. This is an explicit counterexample, not a classification of intermediate categories up to arbitrary equivalence.
main_results.source_ref: Theorem 11.1.

main_results.informal: For a multicenter M in any commutative ring A and any subset K of its indices, first dilate along K and then along the complementary ideals and denominators mapped to the first-stage ring. There is exactly one isomorphism of algebras over the first-stage ring from this two-stage dilatation to A[M], compatible with its canonical map.
main_results.source_ref: Appendix C, Proposition C.1 and Lemma C.2.

projects.title: Directed Topology in Lean 4
projects.summary: Foundational library for directed topological spaces, dipaths, dihomotopy, the fundamental category functor, and a directed Van Kampen pushout theorem.

main_results.informal: Definition of a directed topological space as a topological space with a class of directed paths closed under constant paths, concatenation, and monotone reparametrization.
A directed path in a directed space.
Dihomotopy equivalence relation on dipaths between fixed endpoints.
Proves the directed Van Kampen theorem, showing that the directed fundamental category functor sends the standard open cover square to a pushout in the category of categories.

projects.title: Euclidean Distance Geometry
projects.summary: Develops the basepoint-centered Gram approach to finite Euclidean distance geometry. Proves both directions of Schoenberg's characterization, including a rank-controlled factorization of positive-semidefinite matrices; proves that three affinely independent centers in Euclidean three-space determine at most two points with prescribed distances; and verifies the Cayley--Menger determinant for segments and triangles, including the triangle-area identity underlying Heron's formula.

source.title: Remarks to Maurice Fréchet's article Sur la définition axiomatique d'une classe d'espace distanciés vectoriellement applicable sur l'espace de Hilbert

main_results.informal: For n at least one, a symmetric hollow n-by-n matrix is a squared-distance matrix of points in k-dimensional Euclidean space exactly when its basepoint-centered Gram matrix is positive semidefinite and has rank at most k.
In a finite-dimensional real inner-product affine space, prescribed distances to centers whose affine span has codimension one admit at most two solutions.
Three affinely independent centers in three-dimensional Euclidean space admit at most two points with any prescribed triple of distances.
The Cayley--Menger determinant of three planar points equals minus sixteen times the squared area of their triangle.

projects.title: DomainTheory
projects.summary: Formalizes Dana Scott's domain theory through Scott information systems and PRG-19 neighbourhood systems, including approximable maps, products, function spaces, fixed points, recursive presentations, and initial-algebra constructions for denotational semantics.

source.title: Domains for Denotational Semantics

main_results.informal: Defines Scott information systems, with a distinguished bottom token, finite consistency predicate, entailment relation, and Scott's six axioms.
Defines PRG-19 neighbourhood systems, Scott's neighbourhood presentation of domains.
Defines approximable maps between neighbourhood systems as relations preserving finite approximations.
Proves that an initial algebra for a functor embeds into every other solution through Scott's subdomain relation.
Proves the fixed-point equation for Scott-continuous self maps on complete lattices.

projects.title: Dross's fractional triangle decomposition theorem
projects.summary: Formalizes the exact nine-tenths minimum-degree threshold for fractional triangle decomposition of finite graphs. The proof uses a finite max-flow/min-cut argument and induction that peels high-degree triangles.

source.title: Fractional Triangle Decompositions in Graphs with Large Minimum Degree

main_results.informal: Every finite graph whose minimum degree is at least nine tenths of its number of vertices has a fractional triangle decomposition: nonnegative triangle weights sum to one at each edge.
main_results.source_ref: Dross (2016), fractional triangle decomposition theorem.

projects.title: Duality theory in linear optimization and its extensions
projects.summary: Formalizes Farkas-like theorems and strong LP duality, including extensions to a linearly ordered field with bot and top.

main_results.informal: Farkas' lemma for linear equalities over nonnegative variables.
Farkas' lemma for linear inequalities over nonnegative variables.
Extended Farkas theorem for matrices and vectors over a linearly ordered field with bot and top.
Strong duality theorem for extended linear programs.
Strong duality theorem for linear programs in standard form.

projects.title: Sharp coupon collection and randomized local search
projects.summary: Proves the sharp additive minus-one-half correction for the mean time to collect uniformly sampled coupons from an independent uniform initial set, and for one-bit randomized local search on strictly coordinate-monotone Boolean fitness functions. The centering uses the average of the floor and ceiling half-dimension harmonic numbers, so the limit covers both parities. Develops finite Markov transitions, first-hitting-time expectations, geometric tail bounds, and the exact finite-dimensional mean formulas used in the proof.

source.title: Collecting Coupons with Random Initial Stake

main_results.informal: For n coupon types, with each coupon independently present initially with probability one half, the expected remaining number of independent uniform coupon draws minus n times the average of H_floor(n/2) and H_ceil(n/2) converges to minus one half as n tends to infinity.
main_results.source_ref: Doerr and Doerr, Collecting Coupons with Random Initial Stake, Theorem 1.

main_results.informal: For any family of strictly coordinate-monotone real-valued Boolean fitness functions, the uniform-start mean number of one-bit elitist RLS mutation iterations to reach the all-one string, excluding the initial evaluation, has the same all-dimension additive minus-one-half correction.
main_results.source_ref: Doerr and Doerr, Collecting Coupons with Random Initial Stake, Theorem 3 (RLS corollary).

projects.title: Weierstrass models and singular points for Tate's algorithm
projects.summary: Formalizes Weierstrass models of elliptic curves over a commutative ring, their b- and c-invariants and discriminant, the change-of-coordinates group action, the discriminant's membership in the Jacobian ideal, and the construction of the singular point of a singular model over a perfect field, together with the Kronecker symbol and the Kodaira type enumeration.

source.title: Elliptic Curve Handbook

main_results.informal: Defines a Weierstrass model of a possibly singular elliptic curve by its five a-invariants.
Proves the identity relating the discriminant to the c-invariants, 1728 * discr = c4^3 - c6^2.
Proves that the discriminant is invariant under the rst change-of-coordinates transformation.
Expresses the discriminant as an explicit combination of the Weierstrass polynomial and its partial derivatives, witnessing membership in the Jacobian ideal.
Proves that a model with a singular point has vanishing discriminant.
Proves that the explicitly constructed singular point of a singular model over a perfect field is indeed a singular point (Connell, Proposition 1.5.4).
main_results.source_ref: Ian Connell, Elliptic Curve Handbook, February 1999, Proposition 1.5.4.

main_results.informal: Proves that the change of coordinates moving the singular point places it at the origin.
Enumerates the Kodaira reduction types, including the extra types arising over imperfect residue fields of characteristic 2 or 3.

projects.title: The Erdős–Graham–Ruzsa–Straus two-prime theorem
projects.summary: A complete machine-checked proof that for any two distinct odd primes p and q there are infinitely many n with binom(2n,n) coprime to pq, including the iterated carry-controlled digit-clearing step that Bloom and Croot defer to the 1975 paper, via a per-move lexicographic measure, an elementary staircase lemma, and a Dirichlet-approximation seed.

source.title: On the prime factors of (2n choose n)

main_results.informal: Proves that for distinct odd primes p and q there are infinitely many n with p and q both not dividing the central binomial coefficient binom(2n,n), via the mu-measure descent.
Reassembles the same theorem via bad-bit-mask strong induction, with the low-case clearing discharged by Egrs75.MuFinish.egrs_clearing_low_mu.
The Kummer bridge, stating that an odd prime p does not divide binom(2n,n) exactly when every base-p digit of n is at most (p-1)/2.
Proves that the ratio of logarithms of two distinct primes is irrational.

projects.title: Convex geometry and the Erdős–Ginzburg–Ziv problem
projects.summary: For every fixed positive dimension d, the Erdős–Ginzburg–Ziv constant of (ZMod p)^d equals p times its hollow-family constant plus o(p) as p tends to infinity through primes. Includes the convex-flag Helly and centerpoint theorems, flag decomposition, balanced combinations, relative expansion, and the polynomial hollow-family bound.

main_results.informal: For each positive dimension d, s((F_p)^d) = p w((F_p)^d) + o(p) as p tends to infinity through primes.
For each positive d and ε > 0, sufficiently large primes satisfy s((F_p)^d) ≤ (w((F_p)^d) + ε) p.

projects.title: Ehrhard's inequality and Gaussian log-MGF convexity
projects.summary: Ehrhard's convex-set inequality for finite-dimensional Gaussian laws, including singular covariance, and convexity at every real order of the normalized logarithmic moment-generating function of a finite convex Gaussian functional with all positive exponential moments. Includes Gaussian interpolation, quantile transport, representation of Ehrhard-type laws as monotone convex Gaussian images, weak closure, and normalized moment bounds.

source.title: A Gaussian Convexity for Logarithmic Moment Generating Functions with Applications in Spin Glasses

main_results.informal: For a finite-dimensional Gaussian law, convex sets A and B, and t in [0,1], Gaussian CDF lower thresholds a and b for their probabilities give the CDF lower threshold (1-t)a+tb for the probability of their Minkowski combination. Singular covariance and unit masses are allowed; a zero-mass set has no finite admissible threshold.
For a finite convex real function of a finite-dimensional Gaussian vector with every positive exponential moment finite, log E[exp(qF)]/q, defined at q=0 by E[F], is convex on the whole real line.
A real probability law is of Ehrhard type exactly when it is the pushforward of the standard Gaussian law by a finite monotone convex function; constant functions and Dirac laws are included.
The weak limit of a sequence of Ehrhard-type real probability laws is again of Ehrhard type.

An Ehrhard-type law with integrable exponential and E[exp(X)]=1 has an integrable square, variance at most -2 E[X], and the stated Gaussian negative exponential-moment bounds. A finite second positive exponential moment yields the further normalized moment comparison.

projects.title: Ehrhart's sharp volume inequality
projects.summary: Proves Ehrhart's sharp upper bound for the volume of a centered full-dimensional convex body whose origin is its unique interior lattice point. The development builds the weighted complex-analytic and variational machinery needed for the bound and verifies sharpness using the centered simplex, including its barycenter and exact volume.

source.title: Ten Advances in Mathematics and Theoretical Computer Science

main_results.informal: In every positive dimension, a compact full-dimensional convex set with barycenter zero and origin as its unique interior lattice point has volume at most (n + 1)^n / n!.
The centered dilation of the standard n-simplex has normalized volume exactly (n + 1)^n / n!, so the volume bound is sharp.
The centered dilation of the standard simplex has barycenter zero.
In every positive dimension there exists a centered convex body with a unique interior lattice point that attains the sharp volume bound.

projects.title: Eilenberg–Zilber theorem for bisimplicial objects
projects.summary: For a bisimplicial object X in an abelian category, constructs a chain homotopy equivalence between the total complex of the alternating face map double complex of X and the alternating face map complex of its diagonal. The equivalence is built from the shuffle map and the Alexander–Whitney map. On normalized complexes, shuffle followed by Alexander–Whitney is the identity, and the other composite is homotopic to the identity via the Eilenberg–Mac Lane recursive homotopy. The result is then transported to the unnormalized complexes along the Moore normalization comparisons. The development includes the combinatorics of (p, q)-shuffles, their signs, and the cancellation of diagonal boundary terms.

main_results.informal: For every bisimplicial object X in an abelian category, the total complex of the double complex obtained by taking alternating face map complexes in both simplicial directions is chain homotopy equivalent to the alternating face map complex of the diagonal simplicial object of X.
main_results.source_ref: Generalized Eilenberg–Zilber theorem for bisimplicial objects in an abelian category: Dold–Puppe, "Homologie nicht-additiver Funktoren. Anwendungen", Ann. Inst. Fourier 11 (1961), 201–312, Satz 2.9 (Eilenberg–Zilber–Cartier); the homology-level statement is Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra (1994), Theorem 8.5.1. The product case X_{p,q} = K_p ⊗ L_q is Eilenberg–Zilber, "On products of complexes", Amer. J. Math. 75 (1953), 200–204.

main_results.informal: The total complex of the bi-normalized Moore double complex of X is chain homotopy equivalent to the normalized Moore complex of the diagonal, via the shuffle and Alexander–Whitney maps; shuffle followed by Alexander–Whitney is the identity.
main_results.source_ref: Eilenberg–Mac Lane, "On the groups H(Π, n), II", Ann. of Math. 60 (1954), 49–139, Theorem 2.1a, stated there for products of complexes and generalized here to an arbitrary bisimplicial object in an abelian category.

projects.title: Linear elliptic PDE: solvability, regularity and spectral theory
projects.summary: A reusable analytic development of linear uniformly elliptic divergence-form PDE on Euclidean domains: Hilbert graph models of H¹ and H₀¹, bounded coefficient operators, Poincaré inequalities, zero-drift/nonnegative-potential Dirichlet existence and uniqueness, Gårding and Fredholm theory for general drift, interior H² and higher Sobolev regularity, smooth classical representatives, Sobolev and Hölder embeddings, C¹-domain extension and compactness, variational eigenvalues, and maximum principles. AI-generated proofs with human mathematical design and transcription; announced in arXiv:2609.32561 on 2026-09-26. The unfinished boundary-H² program is outside this completed dependency closure.

main_results.informal: On a bounded domain in positive dimension, a bounded measurable uniformly elliptic operator with zero drift and nonnegative zeroth-order coefficient has a unique H₀¹ weak solution for every L² datum, with a datum-independent norm bound.

In positive dimension, on an open measurable domain, an H₀¹ weak solution of a bounded measurable uniformly elliptic divergence-form operator with globally Lipschitz principal coefficients and an L² datum has interior L² second weak derivatives, with an estimate whose constant is chosen before the solution and datum.

In positive dimension, for a uniformly elliptic divergence-form operator with bounded measurable coefficients, globally Lipschitz principal-coefficient representatives in W^{k+1,∞}(ℝ^d), and lower-order coefficients in W^{k,∞}(ℝ^d), every H₀¹ weak solution on an open measurable domain with an H^k datum has interior H^{k+2} regularity. On each compact subset the iterated L² derivative bounds have a constant chosen before the solution, datum and its H^k bound. The pointwise Lipschitz hypothesis is separate from the weak-derivative bundles.
The inclusion H₀¹(Ω) → L²(Ω) is compact for bounded measurable Euclidean domains, discharging the compactness input to the Fredholm and spectral results.
In positive dimension, bounded open Euclidean domains with C¹ boundary admit a bounded linear H¹ extension operator with compact support control.

projects.title: The Convex-Octagon Case of Erdős Problem 97
projects.summary: Proves that among eight labelled points in the Euclidean plane in convex position, at least one point has no four other points at a common distance. The development reduces a geometric counterexample to a finite incidence model, classifies normalized row patterns up to symmetry, proves geometric and algebraic obstructions, and excludes seven canonical first-row masks with a kernel-audited exhaustive search over the remaining legal row masks and checked geometric obstruction witnesses. This is the modern four-equidistant formulation; Erdős's 1946 paper posed the stronger three-equidistant version. This is the convex-octagon case only; the general Erdős Problem 97 remains open.

source.title: On Sets of Distances of n Points

main_results.informal: Among eight labelled points in the Euclidean plane in convex position, some point has no four other points at a common distance.

projects.title: Leo Moser's finite distinct-subset-sums inequality
projects.summary: Formalizes the exact finite sum-of-squares inequality that Guy's 1982 account states as Theorem 2 and attributes to Leo Moser: a finite set A of natural numbers with distinct subset sums satisfies 4^|A| - 1 <= 3 * sum(a^2). It then derives direct and square-root lower bounds for the largest element of A. This does not claim the stronger historical asymptotic bound attributed jointly to Erdős and Moser, and Erdős Problem 1 remains open.

source.title: Sets of Integers Whose Subsets Have Distinct Sums

main_results.informal: If a finite set A of natural numbers has distinct subset sums, then 4^|A| - 1 is at most three times the sum of the squares of the elements of A.
main_results.source_ref: Richard K. Guy, "Sets of Integers Whose Subsets Have Distinct Sums," Theorem 2 (credited there to Leo Moser), Annals of Discrete Mathematics 12 (1982), 141-154, doi:10.1016/S0304-0208(08)73500-X.

main_results.informal: For a nonempty finite set A of natural numbers with distinct subset sums, 4^|A| - 1 is at most 3|A| times the square of its largest element.
The equivalent square-root lower bound on the largest element: sqrt((4^|A| - 1)/(3|A|)) is at most max(A).

projects.title: The Erdős–Tuza–Valtr conjecture
projects.summary: Formalizes the Erdős–Tuza–Valtr conjecture, a sharp refinement of the Erdős–Szekeres happy-ending theorem, proving that any general-position point set of size at least C(n+2,2)+2 contains the target cup–cap configuration.

source.title: On the Erdős–Tuza–Valtr Conjecture

main_results.informal: Proves the sharp upper bound — a general-position point set with at least C(n+2,2)+2 points contains the Erdős–Tuza–Valtr cup–cap configuration.
The configuration-relative induction lemma that, with the mirror-symmetry reduction, drives the main proof.

projects.title: Linear finite bipartization costs force countable graph colourings
projects.summary: A graph whose every finite subgraph on m vertices can be made bipartite by deleting at most C m edges has a proper colouring by natural numbers. Consequently the maximum finite-subgraph bipartization cost h_G(n), divided by n, tends to infinity for every graph that is not countably colourable, including every graph with chromatic cardinal aleph-one. The development preserves finite edge costs, rooted-pattern extension costs, closure chains, probability laws on Boolean products, finite minimax, Hilbert-space classes, and colouring along well-founded orders. It answers the limit question of Erdős Problem 111; it does not determine the exact growth of h_G.

source.title: Graphs whose finite subgraphs have linear bipartization cost are countably colorable

main_results.informal: For any real C, if each finite subgraph H of G has bipartization number at most C times its number of vertices, G admits a proper colouring by natural numbers. Vertex types may inhabit any universe.
If G has no proper colouring by natural numbers, h_G(n)/n tends to positive infinity along the whole natural-number sequence.
For every graph of chromatic cardinal aleph-one, h_G(n)/n tends to positive infinity. Here h_G(n) is the largest number of edge deletions needed to bipartize a subgraph on n vertices.
In any real Hilbert space, unit vectors can be partitioned into countably many classes, each with a positive lower bound for one plus the inner product of any two vectors in that class.

projects.title: Primitive Sets Above x (Erdos Problem 1196)
projects.summary: Formalizes Math Inc.'s proof around primitive sets above x for Erdos Problem 1196.

main_results.informal: Proves the main primitive-sets-above-x theorem.
States the formalized version of Erdos Problem 1196.

projects.title: Convex Three-Distance Degree-Six Theorem and Exceptional-Word Closures
projects.summary: Proves that every finite cyclically strictly convex planar configuration has a vertex incident to at most six edges from its three largest distance classes. The proof selects a maximal-gap vertex and coordinated majorants, closes all exceptional inner branches, performs the five-row enumeration, and transports all thirteen canonical cover words to four shared full-two-rung, anti-saturation, terminal-cage, and four-edge-cage predicates. It also proves exceptional-count rigidity and an explicit heptagon refutation of a tempting stronger majorant claim, with rational regression witnesses. This settles the all-n k=3 instance of the paper's suggested degree-2k convex bound; Morić--Pritchard proved the corresponding top-three edge bound for sufficiently large n. It does not settle the general-k suggestion or the general Erdős problem 132.

source.title: On the Graph of Large Distances

main_results.informal: For every nonempty finite cyclically strictly convex planar configuration with three strictly ordered largest squared-distance classes d₁, d₂, and d₃, some vertex is incident to at most six pairs whose squared distance is one of those three classes.
main_results.source_ref: Erdős--Lovász--Vesztergombi, printed p. 542, suggest the stronger convex bound degree at most 2k. Morić--Pritchard, "Counting large distances in convex polygons" (arXiv:1103.0412), Theorem 1.4, prove m₁ + m₂ + m₃ ≤ 3n for sufficiently large n, which gives the same degree-six consequence in that range. The novelty here is the all-n theorem: it removes the sufficiently-large-n restriction. ErLV89 Theorem 2.7, printed p. 548, proves only degree at most 3k-1, which specializes to eight.

main_results.informal: Cyclic strict convexity and the three-largest-distance-class hypothesis construct the full maximal-gap, thirteen-word reduction package together with route-specific closure evidence, without any remaining coordinated-majorant or geometric-adapter assumption.
main_results.source_ref: New proof-producing assembly theorem in this project. It combines the ErLV89 majorant framework with the project's maximal-gap tail, terminal-color, five-row, and thirteen-word transport lemmas.

main_results.informal: Every one of the thirteen canonical maximal-gap cover words transports to its routed full-two-rung, anti-saturation, terminal-cage, or four-edge-cage realization, and hence supplies the corresponding degree bound.
main_results.source_ref: New geometric transport theorem in this project. The thirteen-word classification and its four-predicate closure interface are not statements of ErLV89.

main_results.informal: A thirteen-tag routing interface over four shared geometric realization predicates maps B:3→2 and D:3→2 to Row1B32WordRealization, B:3→1, BA, D:3→1, and DC to OnePenultimateWordGeometry, DD to Row4DDWordRealization, and the remaining six tags to FullTwoRungGeometry. Each inhabited routed predicate supplies a vertex of degree at most six, with the one-penultimate route proving the stronger bound five.
main_results.source_ref: New derived variant contributed and proved in this Lean Pool project. The thirteen-word classification and its closures are not statements of ErLV89.

main_results.informal: Every raw full-two-rung realization has its displayed vertex of degree at most six. A rigid normalization derives the canonical coordinates, the diameter branch is impossible, the long branch is counted from four raw boundary arcs, and the short branch contradicts the exact two-rung identity and metric dichotomy.

This implication from the abstract reduction interface is retained as the final assembly map. Its hypothesis is now discharged by convex_top_three_draft_reduction_complete, yielding the unconditional theorem convex_top_three_degree_six; ErLV89 itself proves only the degree-eight bound obtained from 3k−1 when k=3.
main_results.source_ref: Erdős--Lovász--Vesztergombi, printed p. 542: “Perhaps in the convex case there always exists an x_i such that the degree of x_i is at most 2k.” Alongside it, Theorem 2.7, printed p. 548, proves only: “If S is the set of vertices of a convex polygon then the graph G(S, k) has a point of degree at most 3k−1.” Thus degree six for k=3 is the stronger suggested variant; the proved source bound is eight, while this project's global closure proves degree six.

main_results.informal: Every exceptional jointly minimal pair lies in case (1,2), (2,1), or (2,2). In (1,2), every first substitute has at least one right move while every second substitute has exactly two left moves and zero right moves. In (2,1), every first substitute has exactly two right moves and zero left moves while every second substitute has at least one left move. Only in (2,2) are those exact substitute counts proved on both sides.

Assuming the three top distance classes and TopThreeAdjacent for both starting edges z–x and t–u, each forced two-move chain in an exceptional inner-move case has the rank ladder from the third-largest through the second-largest to the largest distance, while its proposed intermediate exchange edge remains nonterminal.

In an explicit rational convex heptagon, a second-largest-distance edge is already terminal under both permitted cover moves, refuting the stronger claim that every non-diameter top-three edge admits a longer cover.
An explicit rational nine-point regression configuration realizes squared-distance classes 855625, 838525, and 811165 as its three largest classes.
An explicit rational six-point regression configuration realizes the three stated rational squared-distance values as its largest classes.

projects.title: A Conditional Fourteen-Point Case of Erdős Problem 132
projects.summary: Formalizes the planar Hopf--Pannwitz diameter bound and proves the fourteen-point low-multiplicity conclusion conditional on exactly two remaining published interfaces: the known maximum-cardinality bound for planar sets with at most six distances and the Szöllősi--Östergård classification of thirteen-point planar six-distance sets. Internally derives the exact failure profile and endpoint deletion, constructs the three classified templates, eliminates the nonregular cases by multiplicity, and excludes the regular tridecagon extension by explicit second and fourth moments. The general Erdős problem remains open.

source.title: Constructions of maximum few-distance sets in Euclidean spaces

main_results.informal: Every injectively labelled fourteen-point planar configuration has a realized distance represented by at most fourteen unordered pairs; the proof chooses that distance to be a diameter.
main_results.source_ref: The planar diameter bound, conventionally associated with Hopf--Pannwitz; Perles's clockwise-extreme endpoint proof.

main_results.informal: Assuming precisely the published planar few-distance cardinality and Szöllősi--Östergård classification interfaces, every injectively labelled fourteen-point planar configuration realizes at least two distances whose unordered-pair multiplicities are at most fourteen.
main_results.source_ref: Erdős Problem 132; Hopf--Pannwitz's planar diameter bound; Wei, "A Proof of Erdős--Fishburn's Conjecture for g(6)=13," EJC 19(4) P38 (2012), doi:10.37236/2917; Szöllősi--Östergård, EJC 27(1) P1.23 (2020), Table 1 and Theorem 16, doi:10.37236/8565.

projects.title: Planar Point Sets Whose Non-Diameter Distances Form a Geometric 3-Chain
projects.summary:
Formalizes a support theorem about planar point sets whose non-diameter squared distances are confined to a geometric progression of ratio three. The chain-quadruple theorem shows that no planar quadruple with all six squared distances in such a chain can span two chain steps, and classifies the seven labelled patterns that do occur: the rhombus of two glued equilateral triangles, in five positions of its long edge, and the equilateral triangle with its centroid, in two. A Gram obstruction then rules out any five-point chain configuration. The lift to n at least thirteen runs through the diameter graph: the Caro--Wei independence bound, proved here, produces an independent five-set once the diameter graph is known to have at most as many edges as the set has points. That edge bound is the Hopf--Pannwitz theorem of 1934, and it already exists in the pool; this project reproves it in its own model as a supporting lemma, claiming no novelty for it, and the overlap is set out in full below. The result is unconditional.
There is no prior write-up behind this development. The restriction to ratio 3 is ad hoc: the 3-chain statement was produced by the author's automated research pipeline in August 2026, while the cited source poses the ambient Erdos problem and does not state this restriction or result. This theorem does not resolve Erdos 132, whose distance spectra need not be geometric 3-chains. The descriptive labels used in the Lean docstrings are internal to this development and refer to no numbered result elsewhere.
Overlap disclosure. Erdos132ThreeChain.hopfPannwitz is NOT offered as a new result. The pooled project Erdos132N14 already contains the same diameter bound, and the version here exists only so that this project is self-contained. Its statement, verbatim from LeanPool/Erdos132N14/HopfPannwitz.lean, is

    theorem diameterEdges_card_le
        (P : Configuration ι) (S : Finset ι) {d : ℝ}
        (hd : 0 < d)
        (hmax : ∀ f ∈ pairs S, P.pairDistance f ≤ d) :
        (diameterEdges P S d).card ≤ S.card

where, from LeanPool/Erdos132N14/Basic.lean, `Configuration ι` is a structure carrying an injective `point : ι → ℂ`, `pairs S = (S ×ˢ S).filter fun e ↦ e.1 < e.2` for a `LinearOrder ι`, `pairDistance P e = dist (P.point e.1) (P.point e.2)`, and `diameterEdges P S d = (pairs S).filter fun e ↦ P.pairDistance e = d`. The corresponding statement here is

    theorem hopfPannwitz {X : Finset Point} {D : ℝ} (hD : IsSqDiameter X D) :
        ∑ v ∈ X, degree (DiameterAdj D) X v ≤ 2 * X.card

with `Point = ℝ × ℝ`, `sqDist` the squared Euclidean distance, `DiameterAdj D p q = (p ≠ q ∧ sqDist p q = D)`, `degree adj X v = (X.filter (adj v)).card`, and `IsSqDiameter X D` asserting that `D` is realised by two distinct points of `X` and dominates every squared distance inside `X`. The two are the same mathematical theorem — a positive maximal distance is realised at most as often as there are points — carried by different models: an injective map from a linearly ordered index type into the complex plane, counting a Finset of unordered pairs, against a Finset of points of the real plane, in squared distances and degree-sum form. Neither statement is an instance of the other without a model bridge: a LinearOrder on ℝ × ℝ, a dist-to-sqDist transfer, and a handshake lemma. The proofs differ too, Perles charging there against pendant deletion driven by Cramer's rule here. No project in the pool imports another, and CONTRIBUTING.md records that independence as the property the fast per-project build relies on, so this project reproves the bound rather than importing it. It is a supporting lemma of this development, not one of its results, and it is therefore not listed among the main results below.
Two supporting identities also exist elsewhere in the pool. From LeanPool/Erdos97ConvexOctagon/CayleyMenger.lean,

    theorem cm4_sqDist_eq_zero (a b c d : Plane) :
        cm4 (sqDist a b) (sqDist a c) (sqDist a d)
          (sqDist b c) (sqDist b d) (sqDist c d) = 0

over `Plane = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)` is the same four-point Cayley--Menger vanishing as this project's

    theorem gramDet_eq_zero (a b c d : Point) :
        gramDet (sqDist a b) (sqDist a c) (sqDist a d) (sqDist b c) (sqDist b d) (sqDist c d) = 0

over `Point = ℝ × ℝ`; both are one-line `ring` identities in the coordinates. From LeanPool/DistanceGeometry/SchoenbergHard.lean,

    theorem schoenberg {D : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ} (hD : IsPreDistMatrix D) :
        EmbedsIn D k ↔ (centeredGram D).PosSemidef ∧ (centeredGram D).rank ≤ k

characterizes Euclidean distance matrices in general dimension. This project never invokes it: the four-point condition is used directly as a `ring` identity and the five-point obstruction is a sum-of-squares contradiction, so no positive-semidefiniteness criterion is needed.

source.title: Erdős Problem #132

main_results.informal: Let n be at least thirteen, let a be positive, and let X be a finite set of points of the real plane with exactly n elements. Suppose D is the squared diameter of X, meaning that D is realised by two distinct points of X and dominates every squared distance inside X. Then for every natural number h, the set of squared distances realised by distinct points of X and different from D is not equal to the geometric 3-chain consisting of a times 3^j for j below h.

Let a be positive and let S be a four-element set of points of the real plane such that every squared distance between distinct points of S equals a times a nonnegative power of three. Then there is a positive r, itself equal to a times a nonnegative power of three, for which every squared distance between distinct points of S equals r or 3r.

Let c be positive and let A, B, C, D be points of the real plane with the squared distance from A to B equal to c and every other pairwise squared distance equal to c times a nonnegative power of three. Then each of the four squared distances from A and B to C and to D equals c or 3c, at least one of the two squared distances from A and B to C equals c, likewise for D, the squared distance from C to D equals c or 3c, the squared distance from A to C equals c or that from B to D equals c, the squared distance from B to C equals c or that from A to D equals c, and the whole labelling is one of exactly seven explicit patterns: five with a single edge of squared length 3c, and two in which the three edges of squared length 3c form a triangle.
Let a be positive. There is no five-element set of points of the real plane in which every squared distance between distinct points equals a times a nonnegative power of three.
Let c be positive. There are no four points of the real plane, each at squared distance c from a common point, whose six pairwise squared distances all equal c or 3c.

Let adj be a symmetric irreflexive relation with decidable adjacency on a type, and let V be a finite set of vertices. Then V has a subset S, no two elements of which are adjacent, whose cardinality is at least the sum over v in V of one divided by one plus the number of neighbours of v inside V.

Let adj be a symmetric irreflexive relation with decidable adjacency on a type, and let V be a finite set of at least thirteen vertices whose degrees inside V sum to at most twice the cardinality of V. Then V has a five-element subset no two elements of which are adjacent.

There is a five-element set of points of the real plane whose squared diameter is 4 and whose set of non-diameter squared distances is exactly the two-term geometric 3-chain consisting of 1 and 3. The configuration that the headline forbids for at least thirteen points is therefore realisable at five points with chain length two.

projects.title: Erdős Problem #137: powerful products of consecutive integers
projects.summary: Formalizes the abc-conditional finiteness results for Erdős Problem #137 (Erdős–Selfridge): a number N is powerful if every prime dividing N has its square dividing N, and the question is whether the product F(k,n) = n(n+1)⋯(n+k-1) of k ≥ 3 consecutive integers can be powerful for infinitely many n. Each route isolates its abc input (a radical lower bound) as a single explicit hypothesis and proves everything else outright, concluding that, conditionally, F(k,n) is powerful for only finitely many n for each fixed k ≥ 3.

source.title: Erdős Problem #137: powerful products of consecutive integers

main_results.informal: Under the Granville–Langevin radical bound RadLB k (an abc-conditional hypothesis) and k ≥ 3, the set of n ≥ 1 for which F(k,n) is powerful is finite.
Under RadLB k and k ≥ 3, there is a threshold beyond which F(k,n) is never powerful.
Unconditionally, the radical squared times the powerful part of m is at most m squared (rad m ^ 2 * B2 m ≤ m ^ 2).
A nonzero powerful number N satisfies rad N ^ 2 ≤ N.

projects.title: Erdős Problem 346: Ratio Limit Forces the Golden Ratio
projects.summary: Formalizes the limit-exists interpretation of Erdős Problem 346: for a strictly increasing positive integer sequence with a uniform ratio gap whose finite deletions are complete but whose infinite deletions are not, if the consecutive quotient sequence converges to some real limit greater than one, then that limit must equal the golden ratio and the quotient sequence tends to it.

source.title: Erdős Problem #346

main_results.informal: Existence of any limit greater than one for the quotient sequence forces convergence to the golden ratio, the intended Erdős–Graham conclusion.
If the quotient sequence converges to a limit greater than one under the completeness and incompleteness deletion hypotheses, that limit equals the golden ratio.
Under the same hypotheses, the quotient sequence converges to the golden ratio itself.

projects.title: Erdős Problem #367
projects.summary: Formalizes upper and lower bound results for powerful parts of products of consecutive integers, including abc-conditional upper bounds, an unconditional odd r-full lower bound, a Pell-style limsup theorem, and polynomial arithmetic cores.

source.title: Powerful parts of consecutive integers and Davenport-Zannier polynomials

main_results.informal: Proves an abc-conditional k = 3 upper bound for the product of square-full parts of three consecutive integers.
Proves a general-k upper bound for the square-full part of a product of consecutive integers from an explicit radical lower-bound hypothesis.
Gives an unconditional odd r construction where the product of r-full parts of two consecutive integers is larger than the stated power of n.
Proves an unconditional limsup form showing that the product of square-full parts of three consecutive integers exceeds any fixed multiple of n squared times log n.
Proves the integer-form arithmetic core yielding the E3 at least 13/9 lower-bound construction under explicit prime-supply data.
Verifies the degree-27 polynomial identity used in the Davenport-Zannier construction.
Proves the integer-form arithmetic core yielding the E3 at least 40/27 lower-bound construction under explicit prime-supply data.

projects.title: Sums of Distinct Factorials That Are Powers of Two (Erdos Problem 403)
projects.summary: Reconstructs the finiteness theorem for Erdos Problem 403: only finitely many sums of distinct factorials are powers of two, and every such power is at most 2^7 = 128 (the extremal solution 2! + 3! + 5! = 128). The sharp bound is proved in the factorial number system via a single fixed modulus 12!, with all computations kernel-pure.

source.title: Erdos Problem 403: sums of distinct factorials that are powers of two

main_results.informal: Every power of two that is a sum of distinct factorials is at most 2^7, with 128 the largest solution.
Only finitely many sums of distinct factorials are powers of two.

projects.title: The Erdős–Sós conjecture (Erdős Problem 548)
projects.summary: Proves the Erdős–Sós conjecture (1962), Erdős Problem 548: every graph on n ≥ k+1 vertices with at least (k−1)n/2 + 1 edges contains every tree on k+1 vertices as a (not necessarily induced) subgraph. The headline statement is the FrontierMath Erdős benchmark statement, reviewed by Thomas Bloom and carried verbatim by Google DeepMind's Formal Conjectures; the proof was found autonomously by GPT-6 Astra. It is a finite double counting over permutation words of the host vertices: rotating the first qualifying prefix of a cut word gives a gluing inequality for two rooted branches, and reversing the two blocks of a cut moves the root to a newly attached leaf. A strong induction on the order t of the tree bounds the adjacency-marked cut words by the rooted-copy count plus (t−2)·n!, so a tree-free host on n vertices has at most (t−2)n/2 edges, the sharp classical bound.

source.title: Erdős problem #548 (Erdős–Sós conjecture): proof

main_results.informal: Let n ≥ k+1. Every simple graph on n vertices with at least (k−1)n/2 + 1 edges contains every tree on k+1 vertices as a subgraph (an injective graph homomorphism). This is Erdős Problem 548, the Erdős–Sós conjecture, in the benchmark phrasing.
If a tree T on t ≥ 2 vertices is not contained in a graph G on n ≥ 1 vertices, then 2·|E(G)| ≤ (t−2)·n. This is the classical sharp form of the Erdős–Sós bound.

For a tree T on t ≥ 2 vertices rooted at r, a host graph G and a nonempty repetition-free host word of length n, the number of cut permutation words of that word whose cut ends at a neighbour of the first letter is at most the number supporting a rooted copy of T on the prefix plus (t−2)·n!.

For a permutation-closed family W of repetition-free words, all of the same length m, and families A, B, C of letter sets with C ⊆ A and A R ∧ B X → C (R ∪ X) for disjoint R, X, the marked cuts (l, k) with l ∈ W and k ≤ m qualifying for A plus those qualifying for B number at most the allowed cuts plus those qualifying for C.

projects.title: Finitely generated cones and finite LP duality
projects.summary: Proves that finitely generated cones in real normed spaces are closed, including a conic Carathéodory reduction and PointedCone API forms. Derives a finite-dimensional inequality form of Farkas' lemma and proves packing attainment with equality to the covering infimum for finite covering and packing linear programs. The Farkas and LP statements overlap the pooled Duality development; the generic cone-closedness results provide the project's distinct reusable API.

source.title: Affine Profile Reduction for Fractional Triangle Packings in Split Graphs

main_results.informal: The cone generated by a finite family in a real normed vector space is a closed set.
An infeasible finite system of nonnegative linear inequalities admits a nonnegative separating Farkas certificate.

Given a finite nonnegative matrix with a strictly positive entry in every column and nonnegative capacities, there is a feasible nonnegative packing whose unit-objective value is maximal and equals the infimum cost of nonnegative coverings with unit demand.

projects.title: Chordal graphs: minimal separators and simplicial vertices
projects.summary: A reusable formalization byproduct accompanying Paper II: defines chordal graphs through the cycle-and-chord characterization, proves induced-subgraph heredity and the clique property for finite minimal separators of fixed vertex pairs, proves Dirac's simplicial-vertex theorem, and proves the connected non-complete case of the two-vertex conclusion.

source.title: Complete-Split Extremizers for a Fractional Triangle-Cover Functional on Chordal Graphs

main_results.informal: A graph that embeds as an induced subgraph of a chordal graph is itself chordal.
Every induced subgraph of a chordal graph is chordal.
Every finite minimal separator of two fixed vertices in a chordal graph is a clique.
Every nonempty finite chordal graph has a simplicial vertex.
Every connected non-complete finite chordal graph has two non-adjacent simplicial vertices.

projects.title: Near-perfect triangle packings from sum-zero triples
projects.summary: Records a reusable formalization byproduct accompanying Paper III: pairwise edge-disjoint triangles in any finite complete graph such that every vertex is incident to at most three uncovered edges, using a cyclic-group sum-zero triple system, with a bridge to Mathlib's SimpleGraph API.

source.title: SumZeroTriangles.lean, a reusable formalization byproduct accompanying Linear-Error Clique Partitions of Split Graphs via Structured Triangle Packing

main_results.informal: For every finite vertex type, its complete simple graph has a family of pairwise edge-disjoint triangle graphs whose uncovered graph has degree at most three at every vertex.
Every finite complete graph has a family of pairwise edge-disjoint triangles leaving uncovered degree at most three at every vertex.

projects.title: A sharp 5/8 bound for Erdős Problem 865
projects.summary: Formalizes the resolution of Erdős Problem 865 on pairwise sums. For A ⊆ {1,…,N}, a pairwise-sum triple is a set of distinct a, b, c ∈ A with a+b, a+c, b+c all in A, and A is triple-free when it has none. The development proves that every triple-free A ⊆ [1,N] satisfies 8·|A| ≤ 5·N + 53, that any A exceeding this bound contains a triple, and — via the construction A = [M,2M] ∪ [4M,8M] for N = 8M — that the constant 5/8 is optimal, so f₃(N) = 5N/8 + O(1). The upper bound runs through a folded additive lemma over ℤ/mℤ (a four-set union bound) and a folding lemma, closed by strong induction on N.

source.title: A sharp 5/8 bound for an Erdős–Sós pairwise-sums problem

main_results.informal: Every triple-free set A ⊆ [1,N] satisfies 8·|A| ≤ 5·N + 53, i.e. |A| ≤ (5/8)·N + O(1).
Every A ⊆ [1,N] with 5·N + 53 < 8·|A| contains a pairwise-sum triple (the paper's Theorem 1.1 form).
For N = 8M with M ≥ 1 there is a triple-free A ⊆ [1,N] with 8·|A| = 5·N + 16, so the constant 5/8 is optimal.

projects.title: Escauriaza–Seregin–Šverák and Ladyzhenskaya–Prodi–Serrin regularity
projects.summary: Endpoint and Serrin regularity criteria for three-dimensional incompressible Navier–Stokes Leray–Hopf solutions: bounded L-infinity-in-time L3 velocity implies L5 integrability, uniqueness, and a smooth representative on positive times including the final time. Includes local endpoint regularity, both Carleman inequalities, spatial unique continuation, and half-space backward uniqueness. Retains the complete ESS production formalization.

main_results.informal: A Leray–Hopf solution whose spatial L3 mass is essentially bounded in time belongs to space-time L5, is unique among Leray–Hopf solutions with the same initial datum, and has an almost-everywhere equal smooth representative on all positive times through the final time.

A Leray–Hopf solution satisfying the critical Serrin mixed-norm condition with spatial exponent greater than three, including the L2-in-time L-infinity-in-space endpoint, is unique and has a smooth representative on positive times through the final time.

The endpoint L-infinity-in-time L3 criterion and the Serrin criteria for all spatial exponents greater than three jointly imply uniqueness and existence of a smooth representative up to the final time.

A weak Navier–Stokes solution on the unit cylinder with finite energy, L3/2 pressure, and velocity essentially bounded in time in spatial L3 has an almost-everywhere equal parabolically Holder representative on the closure of the half cylinder.
A Leray–Hopf solution whose spatial L3 mass is essentially bounded in time has no singular point at an interior positive time.
A Leray–Hopf solution whose spatial L3 mass is essentially bounded in time belongs to space-time L5 and is unique among Leray–Hopf solutions with its initial datum.
A vector field with explicit weak space-time derivatives obeying a parabolic differential inequality has unique continuation across a spatial boundary under the stated decay and boundary hypotheses.
A vector field on a three-dimensional half-space satisfying the heat differential inequality, growth bound, and zero initial trace vanishes.
The Gaussian Carleman inequality bounds weighted field and gradient energies by the weighted heat-operator energy under its support hypotheses.
The half-space Carleman inequality bounds weighted field and gradient energies by the weighted heat-operator energy under its support hypotheses.

projects.title: Euclidean Jordan algebras and the frame Peirce decomposition
projects.summary: The frame Peirce decomposition: relative to a Jordan frame, a Euclidean Jordan algebra is the internal direct sum of the blocks V_ij over unordered pairs of frame indices, and in finite dimension the diagonal blocks are lines, dim V_ii = 1 - the Faraut-Koranyi table entry. The frame is carried as data, so frame conjugacy is sidestepped and nothing here claims anything about the rank of J. Machine checked, not peer reviewed, no priority claim.

main_results.informal: A Euclidean Jordan algebra is the internal direct sum of the Peirce blocks associated with a Jordan frame.
In finite dimension, every diagonal block of a Jordan frame has dimension one.

projects.title: Even graphs are edge-disjoint unions of cycles
projects.summary: Decomposes every finite loopless edge set with even degree at each vertex into edge-disjoint simple cycles and derives a simultaneous fixed-point-free pairing of incident edges.

source.title: Reusable even-graph cycle decomposition accompanying Linear-Error Clique Partitions of Split Graphs via Structured Triangle Packing

main_results.informal: Every finite loopless edge set whose degree is even at every vertex is the edge-disjoint union of simple cycles of length at least three.
If every vertex has even degree, then the incident edges at every vertex admit a simultaneous fixed-point-free involutive pairing.

projects.title: Event Structures and Causal-Consistent Reversibility
projects.summary: Formalizes event structures with binary conflict, their configurations, computations, the trace monoid, and causal-consistent reversibility, proving correctness and causal-safety of rollback, uniqueness of minimal and maximal replays, and conditional replay-existence characterizations.

main_results.informal: Defines an event structure as a partially ordered set of events with an irreflexive symmetric conflict relation.
main_results.source_ref: M. Nielsen, G. Plotkin, G. Winskel, Petri nets, event structures and domains, part I, Theoretical Computer Science 13 (1981), 85-108, doi:10.1016/0304-3975(81)90112-2.

main_results.informal: Defines a configuration as a conflict-free, downward-closed set of events.
main_results.source_ref: G. Winskel, Event structures, Advances in Petri Nets 1986, LNCS 255, Springer, 1987, 325-392, doi:10.1007/3-540-17906-2_31.

main_results.informal: Proves that the original configuration is reachable from the rollback of an event when the configuration is finitely representable.
main_results.source_ref: Causal-consistent reversibility in the sense of V. Danos, J. Krivine, Reversible communicating systems, CONCUR 2004, LNCS 3170, Springer, 2004, 292-307, doi:10.1007/978-3-540-28644-8_19.

main_results.informal: Proves causal safety of rollback - events causally after the rolled-back event are removed.
main_results.source_ref: Causal-consistent reversibility in the sense of V. Danos, J. Krivine, Reversible communicating systems, CONCUR 2004, LNCS 3170, Springer, 2004, 292-307, doi:10.1007/978-3-540-28644-8_19.

main_results.informal: Proves uniqueness of the minimal replay of a log - any two minimal replays compatible with the log reach the same configuration.

Defines the trace monoid as lists of events quotiented by the congruence generated by swapping adjacent concurrent events; paths in the configuration graph are quotiented by the same trace equivalence to form asynchronous paths.
main_results.source_ref: A. Mazurkiewicz, Trace theory, Advances in Petri Nets 1986, LNCS 255, Springer, 1987, 278-324, doi:10.1007/3-540-17906-2_30.

projects.title: Chaos and the Julia set of the complex exponential
projects.summary: Formalizes the dynamics of z ↦ exp(z): escaping points, points with dense forward orbit, and repelling periodic points are dense in the complex plane; the map is chaotic in Devaney's sense and its Julia set is the whole plane. The development proves eventual covering of every compact set omitting zero, constructs contracting inverse branches, and rules out every locally uniform spherical subsequential limit on nonempty open sets. It includes general normal-sequence restriction lemmas, quantitative open mapping, and a two-target obstruction for arbitrary separated uniform codomains. The Lean proofs were primarily generated by AI under Lasse Rempe's direction. The initial six-lemma architecture adapts John Harrison's HOL Light formalization, credited with its retained BSD notice in the entry module.

source.title: The Exponential Map is Chaotic: An Invitation to Transcendental Dynamics

main_results.informal: The complex exponential is continuous, has dense periodic points, and the monoid action generated by its iterates is topologically transitive on the complex plane.
The Julia set of the complex exponential is the whole plane, where the Fatou set is defined by local normality of sphere-valued iterates with arbitrary locally uniform sphere-valued limits.
Points p with a positive period n and derivative norm greater than one for the nth exponential iterate are dense in the complex plane.
For every nonempty open set U in the complex plane and every compact set K omitting zero, all sufficiently large iterates of the exponential map send U onto a set containing K.
Points whose forward exponential orbit eventually leaves every centered Euclidean ball are dense in the complex plane.
The set of complex points with dense forward exponential orbit is uncountable.
On every nonempty open set in the complex plane, no strictly increasing subsequence of exponential iterates converges locally uniformly to any function into the Riemann sphere.

projects.title: Factorization Systems
projects.summary: Formalizes factorization systems, orthogonality, orthogonal complements, and the standard construction from weak factorization plus orthogonality.

source.title: Category Theory in Context

main_results.informal: Defines factorization systems on a category with specified left and right classes.
Constructs a factorization system from repleteness, weak factorizations, and orthogonality.
Defines orthogonality of two morphisms by existence and uniqueness of diagonal fillers.
Defines the right orthogonal complement of a morphism property.

projects.title: Optimal fully dynamic matching on the line
projects.summary: Constructs a measurable hierarchical policy for fully dynamic matching of uniformly arriving demand and replenishment on the unit interval. Proves logarithmic-over-inventory bounds for long-run root-mean-square distance from every initial inventory and for initialized finite-horizon expected average cost.

main_results.informal: For every inventory size m at least two, an online policy has long-run RMS cost at most (72000/log 2) log(m+1)/m from every initial inventory, and the same expected-average-cost bound after initialization for horizons at least 2m².

projects.title: Feige's sharp unit-slack inequality
projects.summary: For small-universe probability spaces, proves the sharp fixed-dimensional unit-slack lower bound for sums of independent nonnegative random variables: if each coordinate has mean at most one, then the probability that the sum lies below its mean plus one is at least (n/(n+1))^n, and this constant is optimal. The supporting library formalizes the Vlassis--Thomas exact distribution-free calibration theorem, Grünbaum's centroid-halfspace inequality and sharp simplex example, and the normalized-exponential bridge joining them.

source.title: Sharp Small-Deviation Inequalities for Sums of Independent Nonnegative Random Variables

main_results.informal: For every positive dimension n and every small-universe probability space, the sharp fixed-dimensional lower bound for the strict event that a sum of independent nonnegative random variables is below its expectation plus one is (n/(n+1))^n, and an explicit finite family proves optimality.

On every small-universe probability space, the Dirichlet statistic used in the proof is super-uniform for every independent family of measurable, integrable, nonnegative random variables whose coordinate means are at most one.
Every closed halfspace containing the centroid of a positive-volume convex body in finite-dimensional Euclidean space contains at least the sharp Grünbaum fraction of the body's volume.

projects.title: Fel's Conjecture on Syzygies of Numerical Semigroups
projects.summary: Formalizes Fel's conjectural formula for syzygies of numerical semigroups.

main_results.informal: Proves Fel's conjecture for the polynomial attached to numerical-semigroup syzygies.

projects.title: FinEqs - reducing equations defining a subset of n-space over a finite field
projects.summary: Formalizes the finite-field equation-reduction theorem and sharpness examples.

main_results.informal: Reduces equations on a small finite set to at most n equations in the same span.
Shows the cardinality bound in the reduction theorem is sharp.
Applies the reduction theorem to affine space over a finite field.
Applies the reduction theorem to nonempty projective zero loci.
Shows n - 1 coordinate-function combinations have at least q common zeros.

projects.title: Fundamental groups of finite connected graphs
projects.summary: Constructs the standard interval-cell realization of a finite connected directed multigraph and proves that its topological fundamental group is a free group of rank E - V + 1. The proof uses an explicit spanning-tree basis and develops a verified path-lifting cover, a contraction of the covering tree, root-change equivalences, the tree/triviality criterion, and the corresponding free-abelian result.

source.title: Algebraic Topology, Additional Topic 1.A: Graphs and Free Groups

main_results.informal: For a finite weakly connected directed multigraph, the topological fundamental group of its interval-cell quotient realization at any vertex is explicitly isomorphic to the free group on E + 1 - V generators.
The endomorphism group at a vertex in the graph's free groupoid is explicitly isomorphic to the topological fundamental group of the interval-cell realization.
The canonical path-lifting projection from rooted free-groupoid paths to graph vertices is a quiver covering, with bijective maps on every incoming and outgoing edge star.
The interval-cell realization of a directed arborescence is simply connected, via an explicit continuous contraction to its root.
The combinatorial fundamental group is trivial exactly when the graph's cycle rank E + 1 - V is zero.
The additive abelianization of the graph fundamental group is the free abelian group on E + 1 - V generators.

projects.title: Finite max-flow / min-cut
projects.summary: Develops finite networks with real nonnegative capacities, proves cut-flow weak duality and maximum-flow attainment, and derives max-flow/min-cut equality by an augmenting-path argument.

source.title: Reusable max-flow/min-cut component accompanying Linear-Error Clique Partitions of Split Graphs via Structured Triangle Packing

main_results.informal: Every finite network with real nonnegative capacities and distinct source and sink admits a feasible flow and a source-sink cut whose flow value equals the cut capacity.
The value of every feasible flow is at most the capacity of every source-sink cut.
Every finite network with real nonnegative capacities admits a maximum-value feasible flow.

projects.title: Sharp Five-Distance and Sup-Norm Gap Theorems
projects.summary: Formalizes sharp gap theorems for Kronecker sequences on tori: the Euclidean five-distance theorem on the 2-torus and the sup-norm gap bound, together with explicit arithmetic witnesses realizing the extremal cases - five distinct nearest-neighbour distances for the Euclidean and sup-norm metrics in dimension two, and nine distinct sup-norm distances in dimension three (Haynes-Marklof-Ramirez), via exact modular arithmetic on best simultaneous Diophantine approximations.

source.title: Higher dimensional gap theorems for the maximum metric

main_results.informal: Exhibits a base point on the 2-torus with an irrational coordinate and an N whose Euclidean nearest-neighbour distances realize exactly five distinct values, showing the Euclidean five-distance bound is sharp.
main_results.source_ref: A. Haynes and J. Marklof, A five distance theorem for Kronecker sequences, International Mathematics Research Notices 2022(24):19747-19789, doi:10.1093/imrn/rnab205, arXiv:2009.08444.

main_results.informal: Exhibits a base point on the 2-torus with an irrational coordinate and an N whose sup-norm nearest-neighbour distances realize exactly five distinct values, showing the sup-norm gap bound is sharp in dimension two.

Exhibits a base point on the 3-torus with an irrational coordinate and an N whose sup-norm nearest-neighbour distances realize at least nine distinct values, showing the sup-norm gap bound is sharp in dimension three.

projects.title: The 5/8 theorem
projects.summary: Proves Gustafson's 5/8 theorem — the Mathlib commuting probability of a nonabelian group is at most 5/8, with the infinite case immediate from commProb being zero — via the finite-group index bounds for the center and centralizers of noncentral elements.

source.title: What is the probability that two group elements commute?

main_results.informal: The commuting probability of a nonabelian group is at most 5/8.
The center of a finite nonabelian group contains at most a quarter of its elements.
The centralizer of a noncentral element of a finite group contains at most half of its elements.

projects.title: Flean: Floating-Point Numbers in Lean
projects.summary: Formalizes a configurable model of floating-point numbers in Lean 4, including normal and subnormal representations, conversions between rationals and floats, round-trip correctness, and rounding error bounds.

main_results.informal: Defines the floating-point number type parameterized by a precision and exponent configuration, with normal, subnormal, infinite, and NaN cases.
Rounds a rational number to the nearest representable floating-point value under a given rounding mode.
Interprets a floating-point value as the exact rational number it represents.
Proves the round-trip identity that converting a finite nonzero float to a rational and back recovers the original float.
Bounds the distance between a rational and its rounded floating-point representation.

projects.title: FLT Eichler-Shimura
projects.summary: Collects the definitions and theorems from the Anthropic Fermat's Last Theorem formalization needed for the Eichler-Shimura isomorphism, relating modular forms to cohomology of modular curves, and properties of the Galois representations of elliptic curves. Includes integer-multiplication results for elliptic curves with transcendental j-invariant, explicit function-field models of modular curves, and the genus formula for X_1(N).

main_results.informal: The Eichler-Shimura isomorphism for Gamma_0(N), identifying parabolic cohomology with binary-form coefficients with the direct sum of holomorphic and antiholomorphic cusp forms, with descended cohomological Hecke operators and compatibility with T_p away from the level and U_p at primes dividing it.

For an integral Weierstrass model W over Z and primes p and ell with ell distinct from p and not dividing the discriminant of W, Frobenius at ell acts on the p-adic Tate module of W over the algebraic closure of Q with characteristic polynomial X^2 - a_ell X + ell. This formulation assumes the expected cardinalities of the p-power torsion subgroups, proved elsewhere in this library.

Over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, if an elliptic curve has j-invariant transcendental over the rationals, every point-group endomorphism induced by a finite integral self-embedding of its function field (represented by IsogenyEndDatum) is multiplication by an integer.
For positive N, the modular-polynomial quotient Q(X)[Y]/(Phi_N(X,Y)) is isomorphic as a Q-algebra to the q-expansion function field of X_0(N), with X mapping to j(q) and Y to j(q^N).

For positive N, j and the nonzero N-torsion Fricke functions generate the full modular function field of Gamma(N) over C. Explicitly, every Gamma(N)-invariant meromorphic function on the upper half-plane with at most exponential growth at every cusp is a quotient of elements of C[j, f_v], with nonzero denominator and equality on punctured neighbourhoods of every point. The fraction field carries the modular action with kernel generated by Gamma(N) and -I. Its fixed field is C(j), and it is Galois over C(j) of degree [SL_2(Z) : <Gamma(N), -I>].

For N >= 5 and any algebraically closed field K of characteristic zero, the genus g of the Gamma_1(N) q-expansion function field after base change from Q to K satisfies 12g + 6c = [SL_2(Z) : <Gamma_1(N), -I>] + 12, where c is the number of cusps of Gamma_1(N).

projects.title: Fermat's Last Theorem for regular primes
projects.summary: Formalizes Kummer's proof of Fermat's Last Theorem for every odd regular prime exponent. The development proves both cases of the theorem and includes the required theory of cyclotomic integers, relative units, Hilbert 90 and 92, ramification, class groups, and Kummer's lemma.

source.title: Fermat's Last Theorem for regular primes

main_results.informal: Fermat's Last Theorem holds for every odd regular prime exponent.
The first case of Fermat's Last Theorem holds for every regular prime: no primitive solution exists when the exponent does not divide the product of the three terms.
The second case of Fermat's Last Theorem holds for every odd regular prime: no primitive nonzero solution exists when the exponent divides the product of the three terms.
A unit of the cyclotomic field of an odd regular prime that is congruent to an integer modulo the prime is itself a prime-th power.

projects.title: First Order Language of ZF Set Theory
projects.summary: Formalizes ZF set theory inside Lean's `FirstOrder.Language` framework, enabling meta-mathematical arguments such as elementary submodels.

source.title: Set Theory

main_results.informal: Bundles the ZF axioms (Emptyset, Pairing, Union, Powerset, Infinity, Regularity, Comprehension, Replacement) into a single model class.
States the principle of mathematical induction over ω externally for any bounded formula in LZFC.

projects.title: Formal Learning Theory Kernel
projects.summary: Formalizes major equivalences and separations in PAC, VC, Gold-style, and online learning theory.

main_results.informal: Characterizes PAC learnability by finite VC dimension.
Bundles the central PAC, VC, compression, Rademacher, and sample-complexity equivalences.
Relates finite VC dimension to compression with side information.
States the Gold-style characterization for identification in the limit.
Characterizes learnability by a bounded mind-change ordinal.
Characterizes online learnability by finite Littlestone dimension.
Separates PAC learnability from online learnability.
Separates explanatory learnability from PAC learnability.

projects.title: Beyond the Bethe approximation of the permanent
projects.summary: Constructs a deterministic polynomial-time approximation algorithm for the permanent of every nonnegative rational matrix, with exponential base strictly smaller than the square root of two. The development includes stable-polynomial inequalities, rational convex optimization, finite-precision arithmetic, and a Turing-machine complexity proof.

main_results.informal: There is a fixed rational algorithm approximating the permanent of every nonnegative rational n-by-n matrix within c^n for an absolute c below sqrt(2), with a deterministic polynomial-time Turing-machine implementation.

projects.title: Strengthened V0 Bounded Arithmetic Interfaces
projects.summary: Formalizes first-order and two-sorted bounded-arithmetic model infrastructure, including arithmetic model laws and string-addition laws for strengthened bundled V0-style interfaces with propositional induction, order, cancellation, decidability, and algebraic laws assumed as fields rather than derived from a separate raw V0 class.

source.title: Logical Foundations of Proof Complexity

projects.notice:
The upstream MIT LICENSE file leaves the copyright line as the unfilled
template text "Copyright (c) [year] [fullname]"; the repository owner of
record is "ruplet".

main_results.informal: Proves associativity of addition in IOPEN models.
Proves commutativity of addition in IOPEN models.
Shows that nonzero elements in IDelta0 models have predecessors.
Proves right cancellation for multiplication by a nonzero element in IDelta0 models.
Exposes string induction inside the strengthened bundled V0Model structure, whose fields include the comprehension and induction/order principles used downstream.
Exposes propositional induction inside the strengthened bundled V0Model structure, rather than deriving it from only the raw finite V0 axiom list.
Proves commutativity of string addition in V0 extension models extending the strengthened V0Model bundle.
Proves associativity of string addition in V0 extension models extending the strengthened V0Model bundle, using the bundled propositional induction field.
Proves that string addition associates with string successor in V0 extension models extending the strengthened V0Model bundle.

projects.title: Formalizing geometric measure theory
projects.summary: A development of foundations and central results in geometric measure theory, including Hausdorff content and density bounds, weak convergence and compactness for Radon measures, tangent-measure machinery, Mattila's Lemmas 14.5--14.7, and Marstrand's integrality theorem for positive finite densities.

source.notes: The geometric-measure-theory results follow Mattila, Geometry of Sets and Measures in Euclidean Spaces, Chapter 14. The weak-convergence, compactness, covering, and density results follow Evans--Gariepy, Measure Theory and Fine Properties of Functions, revised edition.

main_results.informal: If a Radon measure on Euclidean n-space has positive finite s-dimensional density on a set of positive measure, then s is a natural number.
main_results.source_ref: Mattila, Theorem 14.10 (Marstrand's theorem).

main_results.informal: Every n-uniform measure on Euclidean n-space is a constant multiple of Lebesgue measure.
main_results.source_ref: Mattila, Theorem 14.11.

main_results.informal: Vague convergence of Radon measures on Euclidean space is equivalent to the Portmanteau compact-set upper and open-set lower bounds.
main_results.source_ref: Evans--Gariepy, revised edition, Theorem 1.40.

main_results.informal: A sequence of Radon measures on Euclidean space that is uniformly bounded on every compact set has a vaguely convergent subsequence.
main_results.source_ref: Evans--Gariepy, revised edition, Theorem 1.41.
