projects.title: A 4AP-free permutation of the positive integers
projects.summary: Formalizes Boon Suan Ho's construction of a permutation of the positive integers with no four-term arithmetic progression as a subsequence, proving the binary-order lemmas, extension lemma, and computable limit.

source.title: A 4AP-free permutation of the positive integers

main_results.informal: There exists a bijection of the positive integers such that no four increasing positions map to a nonconstant four-term arithmetic progression, including negative common differences.
The explicit computable positive-integer permutation constructed in the development has the stated four-term progression avoidance property.

projects.title: Maxima of Coxeter frieze patterns are Fibonacci numbers
projects.summary: Formalizes the claim that the sequence of maxima of values of (Coxeter) arithmetic frieze patterns is the Fibonacci sequence, using a correspondence between arithmetic frieze patterns and n-flutes.

source.title: On upper bounds in frieze patterns

main_results.informal: Proves that the maximum value of an arithmetic frieze pattern of width n is exactly the n-th Fibonacci number, and that this bound is attained.
Proves that every entry of an n-flute is bounded above by the n-th Fibonacci number.
Proves the glide-reflection symmetry of Coxeter frieze patterns.
Proves the (n+1)-periodicity (horizontal translation invariance) of Coxeter frieze patterns.

projects.title: FrontierMath Ramsey Hypergraphs
projects.summary: Formalizes lower bounds for the Brian-Larson hypergraph extremal function H(n), including a uniform 26/25 improvement over the recursive benchmark k_n for n ≥ 15 and a Lubell-frame asymptotic lower bound.

source.title: Choosing between incompatible ideals

main_results.informal: Proves H(n) ≥ 26 * k(n) / 25 for every n ≥ 15.
main_results.source_ref: Epoch AI FrontierMath, A Ramsey-style Problem on Hypergraphs.

main_results.informal: Proves the uniform recursive construction bound A(n) ≥ 26 * k(n) / 25 for every n ≥ 15.
The substitution-frame recurrence that combines block witnesses and a valid support frame into a larger witness.
Proves that the Lubell support family forms a valid frame for every arity t ≥ 2.
Derives a fixed-t lower bound for the exact witness supremum from Lubell frames.
Proves the asymptotic lower bound liminf H(n) / k(n) ≥ 2 * log 2.
States the asymptotic consequence in terms of H(n) divided by n log n.

projects.title: The Fundamental Inequality of Valued Fields
projects.summary: Defines the ramification index and residue degree of an extension of valued fields and proves the fundamental inequality e * f ≤ finrank K L for finite extensions, via the valuation independence of products of coset representatives and residue-field basis lifts.

source.title: Valued Fields

main_results.informal: Defines the ramification index e(w/v) as the relative index of the value group of the restricted valuation inside the value group of the extension.
Defines the residue degree f(w/v) as the rank of the residue field extension.
Elements with valuations in distinct cosets and residues that are linearly independent give products that are linearly independent over the base field.
The fundamental inequality e(w/v) * f(w/v) ≤ finrank K L for finite extensions of valued fields.
main_results.source_ref: F.-V. Kuhlmann, Valued Fields, Chapter 4, §4.4.

projects.title: Polynomial-factor hardness of the closest vector problem
projects.summary: Formalizes polynomial-factor NP-hardness of the closest vector problem through an explicit reduction from 3-SAT. The development also derives NP-hardness of binary nearest codeword, binary syndrome decoding, and finite p-norm variants of GapCVP. It includes machine-level polynomial-time bounds, binary encodings, affine systems, Reed--Solomon-style interpolation, and the lattice and coding-theory reductions needed by the final results.

source.title: Ten Advances in Mathematics and Theoretical Computer Science

main_results.informal: GapCVP in the Euclidean norm with approximation factor n^(1/400), where n is the lattice dimension, is NP-hard as a promise problem: every NP language reduces in polynomial time to the promise problem on encoded well-formed instances (positive dimension, nonsingular integer basis, positive rational radius) with an integer target, whose YES instances have a lattice vector within the radius of the target and whose NO instances have every lattice vector at distance greater than n^(1/400) times the radius.
Binary nearest codeword is NP-hard as a promise problem.
Binary syndrome decoding is NP-hard as a promise problem.
For every rational p at least one, the finite p-norm version of GapCVP is NP-hard as a promise problem.

projects.title: Gaussian Moments Conjecture counterexamples
projects.summary: Proves explicit complex polynomial counterexamples to the Gaussian Moments Conjecture in every dimension at least three, using genuine expectations under finite products of standard real Gaussian measures. Retains reusable polynomial integrability, Stein identities, complex contractions, coefficient formulas, injective-coordinate marginals, and related moment results.

source.notes: Imports the completed Gaussian core and related moment infrastructure. The July manuscript predates the September Lean proof release. Five and six term counts refer to the natural complex coordinates; total degrees four and three also hold in the original real coordinates. The separate Jacobian-map and route-arithmetic files are excluded. No general inversion, Jacobian-reduction route, or resolution of the two-dimensional conjecture is claimed. Upstream MIT notice is retained in the project entry module. Upstream Lean authorship is inferred from the public codex/lean-formalization branch; its exact proof-authoring model and extent of human editing are unreported. This port and optimization are Codex-authored.

main_results.informal: For every n at least three, the Gaussian Moments Conjecture fails: some complex polynomial has all positive pure Gaussian moments zero, while a polynomial multiplier prevents eventual mixed-moment vanishing.

For every complex univariate polynomial A and positive m, the expectation of A(Q3) times P3 to power m equals m! times the degree-m coefficient of A(X) times (1+X) to power m-1. The explicit P3 has degree four and five terms in its natural complex coordinates.
The analogous arbitrary-A coefficient identity for the explicit four-variable polynomial P4, of degree three and six terms in its natural complex coordinates, gives an independent counterexample.

projects.title: Density-One GKP Divisibility and Its Carry-Language Characterization
projects.summary: Proves that the exponents k satisfying the Graham--Knuth--Patashnik divisibility condition have natural density one. The proof gives an exact all-depth modular sieve, quantitative bounds for possible failures in initial intervals, and a density-zero limit for the failure proportion. It also develops the Kummer digit-sum bridge, the binary-popcount reduction, and a verified ternary carry automaton. The universal GKP conjecture remains open because the possible density-zero failure set may be nonempty.

source.title: Concrete Mathematics: A Foundation for Computer Science, Second Edition

main_results.informal: The proportion of exponents k below N for which nine divides the central binomial coefficient indexed by 2^k tends to one as N tends to infinity.
At each ternary depth n+3, the number of possible failures below N is at most (N divided by 2*3^(n+2), plus one) times (n+9)*2^n.

At depth n+3, exactly (n+9)*2^n of the 2*3^(n+2) exponent classes remain uncertified; every other class gives divisibility by nine and avoids the deficient carry language for all exponents in that class.

The GKP conjecture is equivalent to the assertion that every nonexceptional power of two avoids the explicitly defined deficient-carry regular language. This is an exact reformulation and does not prove the remaining avoidance assertion.
For every natural number n, its central binomial coefficient is divisible by nine exactly when doubling the canonical ternary expansion of n creates at least two carries.

The deficient-carry automaton accepts exactly three concrete little-endian ternary word shapes: all digits zero or one; a unique top digit two; or a unique two followed by a higher zero with all other digits zero or one.
Among all ternary words of length n+2, exactly (n+7) times 2^n create fewer than two carries when doubled.
For every m from 27 through 6560, nine divides the central binomial coefficient indexed by 4^m; this is a bounded computational corollary, not the headline result.

projects.title: Counterexample to Goemans' unsplittable-flow cost conjecture
projects.summary: Refutes Goemans' cost conjecture for single-source unsplittable flow, Conjecture 1.3 of Traub, Vargas Koch, and Zenklusen's paper. A simple, loopless, acyclic graph with seven vertices and nine arcs admits a splittable flow of cost 58, but every unsplittable routing within the additive maximum-demand capacity bound costs at least 60, attained by an explicit routing. The development proves completeness of the walk enumeration and transfers the refutation from integers to any linearly ordered commutative ring, including the rationals and reals. Jason Hickey directed Claude's formal verification of the counterexample discovered by Dmitry Rybin with GPT-5.6 Pro; upstream also acknowledges Katherine Schlitz. Planarity is not part of the formalized claim.

source.title: A verified counterexample to Goemans' cost conjecture

main_results.informal: The rational form of Goemans' cost conjecture is false, even for simple, loopless, acyclic finite digraphs with explicit capacities, positive demands, and distinct terminals different from the source.
main_results.source_ref: Conjecture 1.3 of arXiv:2308.02651v1

main_results.informal: The same cost conjecture is false over every linearly ordered commutative ring, by transfer of the integer counterexample.
On the explicit seven-vertex, nine-arc instance, the minimum cost among unsplittable routings satisfying the additive maximum-demand capacity bound is exactly 60.
The given splittable flow on the counterexample instance costs exactly 58.
For each of the three terminals, the lists of arcs giving a walk from the source are exactly the two explicitly exhibited paths.

projects.title: Sharp list-scheduling and longest-processing-time bounds
projects.summary: Formalizes identical-machine scheduling for arbitrary finite job sets with real processing times. Proves Graham's sharp list-scheduling and LPT approximation bounds, constructs their tight instances, characterizes all positive instances attaining the LPT bound, and establishes the supremum for every sufficiently large fixed job count.

source.title: Graham's bounds for list scheduling and LPT on identical machines

main_results.informal: For nonnegative processing times on m nonzero identical machines, every list schedule has makespan at most (2 - 1/m) times the optimal makespan.
For nonnegative processing times on m nonzero identical machines, every longest-processing-time-first schedule has makespan at most (4/3 - 1/(3m)) times the optimal makespan.
For each nonzero machine count, 4/3 - 1/(3m) is the least universal approximation factor for LPT, over all finite nonnegative real job sets.

For at least two machines and a nonempty set of positive-length jobs, an LPT schedule attains Graham's bound exactly if the instance is a positive scalar multiple and permutation of Graham's 2m + 1 jobs.
For a nonzero machine count and every fixed job count n at least 2m + 1, the supremum of LPT-to-optimum makespan ratios over positive instances with n jobs remains 4/3 - 1/(3m).
Every finite real job-length vector on a nonzero number of machines admits an LPT schedule.
Every assignment of nonnegative-length jobs is matched or improved by a list schedule in some ordering of the jobs.

projects.title: Integer Moore determinants and iterated Fermat quotients
projects.summary: Proves Granville's integrality and congruence formulas for iterated Fermat quotients at odd primes, including the exceptional order p - 1. For 1 ≤ d ≤ p and integers x_j prime to p, it proves that the nonzero integer Moore determinant det(x_j^(p^i)) is divisible by p^C(d+1,3), and that the next power does not divide it exactly when the Fermat quotients q_p(x_j) are pairwise distinct modulo p. The development supplies polynomial coefficient identities, denominator-clearing and valuation estimates, a determinant reduction ladder, and weighted Vandermonde formulas over general commutative rings.

source.title: The p-divisibility of the integer Moore determinant and iterated Fermat quotients

main_results.informal: For an odd prime p, an integer x not divisible by p, any j ≤ p - 1, and any k, the iterated Fermat quotient F^(j)_k(x) is an integer.
main_results.source_ref: Upstream README, first main result; attributed there to Granville.

main_results.informal: Under the same prime and unit hypotheses, for j ≤ p - 2 and any k, j! F^(j)_k(x) is congruent to x q_p(x)^j modulo p, where q_p(x) = (x^(p-1) - 1)/p.
main_results.source_ref: Upstream README, second main result.

main_results.informal: For an odd prime p and an integer x not divisible by p, (p-1)! F^(p-1)_0(x) is congruent to x q_p(x)^(p-1) - x q_p(x) modulo p.
main_results.source_ref: Upstream README, exceptional congruence.

main_results.informal: For an odd prime p, 1 ≤ d ≤ p, and integers x_j not divisible by p with nonzero Moore determinant, p^C(d+1,3) divides det(x_j^(p^i)).
main_results.source_ref: Upstream README, Moore determinant lower bound, in divisibility form.

main_results.informal: Under those determinant hypotheses, its p-adic valuation is exactly C(d+1,3) if and only if the integer Fermat quotients q_p(x_j) have pairwise distinct residues modulo p. The Lean statement expresses exactness as failure of divisibility by p^(C(d+1,3)+1).
main_results.source_ref: Upstream README, equality criterion, including d = p.

projects.title: Graph removal and extremal stability
projects.summary: Formalizes the graph removal lemma for every fixed graph, Füredi's sharp stability inequality and Erdős–Simonovits stability for colourable forbidden graphs. A bridge theorem shows that near-extremal graphs with few labelled forbidden copies are close to a complete multipartite graph.

source.title: Füredi and Erdős–Simonovits stability; general graph removal lemma

main_results.informal: A clique-free graph near Turán's edge bound has a large colourable subgraph.
main_results.source_ref: Füredi's stability theorem.

main_results.informal: An L-free graph near the Turán density for a (p+1)-colourable L is close in edit distance to a complete p-partite graph.
main_results.source_ref: Erdős–Simonovits stability theorem.

main_results.informal: Few labelled copies of any fixed graph H can be destroyed by deleting few edges.
main_results.source_ref: Conlon–Fox, Graph removal lemmas, Theorem 1.1 (https://arxiv.org/pdf/1211.3487v1); Erdős–Frankl–Rödl (1986), Theorems 1.5 and 1.5′, are related precursors; formal source https://github.com/jtraverso/graph-removal-lemma/tree/589cf03ef1e4c80ea8cdd6be77778232c62dd37c.

main_results.informal: A graph near the Turán density with few labelled L copies is close in edit distance to a complete multipartite graph.

projects.title: Grothendieck's theorem for Bessel sequences
projects.summary: Every Bessel sequence with bound one in a complex Hilbert space has its Gram kernel represented by correlations of measurable functions bounded by one on the unit interval. The proof includes real and complex finite matrix decompositions, a Ball--Prodromou argument, and a countable moment-measure construction followed by standard Borel realization.

source.title: Grothendieck's theorem for Bessel sequences

main_results.informal: Every countable Bessel sequence with bound one in a complex Hilbert space admits measurable functions on the unit interval, pointwise bounded by one, whose Lebesgue correlations equal its Gram kernel.

Every complex kernel on a countable index type whose finite quadratic forms are Hermitian positive contractions has a bounded measurable realization on the unit interval with exactly the prescribed correlations.
Every finite real symmetric matrix between zero and the identity is a finite convex combination of rank-one matrices formed from vectors in the coordinate unit cube.

projects.title: Grothendieck's Vanishing Theorem
projects.summary: Formalizes Grothendieck's vanishing theorem for sheaf cohomology on Noetherian topological spaces.

main_results.informal: Proves vanishing of sheaf cohomology above the topological Krull dimension.

projects.title: Known Bounds for the Hadwiger-Nelson Problem
projects.summary: Formalizes the currently known bounds 5 <= chi(R^2) <= 7 for the chromatic number of the Euclidean plane. The upper bound constructs an explicit Isbell-style seven-coloring. The lower bound checks Parts' 481-vertex coloring certificate, develops a finite doubled triangular-lattice forcing gadget, proves its exact Euclidean embedding, and closes the four-color contradiction with a spindle construction. The exact chromatic number remains open.

source.title: A human-verifiable proof of the chromatic number of the plane being at least 5

main_results.informal: The chromatic number of the unit-distance graph on the Euclidean plane lies between five and seven, inclusive.
The unit-distance graph on the Euclidean plane admits no proper coloring with four colors.
An explicit Isbell-style coloring proves that the unit-distance graph on the Euclidean plane is colorable with seven colors.

projects.title: The Hajnal–Szemerédi theorem on equitable vertex colourings
projects.summary: Every finite simple graph of maximum degree at most r admits a proper colouring with r + 1 colours whose class sizes differ by at most one. When the vertex count is s(r + 1), every class can have exactly s vertices. The proof follows the Kierstead–Kostochka argument, preserving finite-subgraph and arbitrary-palette recolouring, reachability, terminal-class and discharging infrastructure. The polynomial-time algorithm from Section 3 is outside the imported scope.

source.title: A short proof of the Hajnal–Szemerédi theorem on equitable colouring

main_results.informal: Every finite simple graph whose vertex degrees are at most r has a proper colouring by Fin (r + 1) such that the size of any colour class is at most the size of any other colour class plus one.
If a finite simple graph has s(r + 1) vertices and every vertex degree is at most r, it has a proper colouring by Fin (r + 1) with every class of size s.

For any finite vertex subset S and finite natural-number palette P of size r + 1, if S has s(r + 1) vertices and every vertex has at most r neighbours within S, there is a proper colouring of S in P with all classes of size s.

projects.title: The Hanson-Wright inequality for sub-Gaussian quadratic forms
projects.summary: Proves the finite-dimensional Hanson-Wright concentration inequality for quadratic forms of independent mean-zero sub-Gaussian real random variables whose maximum least global-MGF sub-Gaussian scale is positive, for matrices with positive Frobenius and operator norms. The bound uses the fixed universal coefficient 1 / (256 * exp(1)^2). This is the MGF normalization of the usual result; no formal identification with an Orlicz psi-2 norm is claimed. The development derives the required moment-generating-function certificate instead of assuming it, and contributes reusable scalar Bernstein, Chernoff, cumulant, sub-Gaussian-process, and finite-maximum infrastructure.

source.title: High-Dimensional Probability (second edition)

main_results.informal: For independent mean-zero real random variables with finite least global-MGF sub-Gaussian scales and positive maximum coordinate MGF scale, and a matrix with positive Frobenius and operator norms, the centered quadratic form satisfies the Hanson-Wright two-regime exponential tail bound with the fixed universal coefficient 1 / (256 * exp(1)^2).

Given positive K and operator norm and C at least 64 * exp(1)^2, independent coordinates with global-MGF sub-Gaussian parameter K^2 satisfy the local quadratic cumulant-generating-function estimate needed for Hanson-Wright.
A finite family of independent, centered, uniformly bounded real random variables satisfies the classical scalar Bernstein tail inequality.

projects.title: The Hasse–Minkowski theorem over ℚ
projects.summary: Proves the local–global principle for quadratic forms over the rationals: a form is isotropic over ℚ exactly when it is isotropic over ℝ and over every p-adic completion, together with Meyer's theorem that an indefinite rational form in at least five variables is isotropic. The development builds the Hilbert symbol at every place of ℚ with Serre's explicit formulas (including the 2-adic case), proves Hilbert reciprocity and the existence theorem for prescribed local symbols, the Hasse invariant and the rank-two and rank-three local representability criteria, Legendre's ternary descent, and the rank-four and rank-≥5 inductions.

source.title: The Hasse–Minkowski theorem over ℚ

main_results.informal: A quadratic form over ℚ is isotropic if and only if it is isotropic over ℝ and over every p-adic completion ℚ_[p] (the Hasse–Minkowski local–global principle, in isotropy form).
Every indefinite quadratic form over ℚ in at least five variables is isotropic (Meyer's theorem).

projects.title: Homogenization at a polynomial scale in high contrast
projects.summary: Formalizes polynomial entry into the small-contrast regime, algebraic convergence of coarse blocks, and quantitative stochastic homogenization with correctors, Liouville classification and large-scale regularity. Uses locally uniformly elliptic measurable coefficient fields modulo almost-everywhere equality. The Dirichlet estimate has the documented negative-Sobolev formulation on adapted cells; the random radius is at least one and the effective matrix is existentially produced. Includes the complete production library and its pinned CoarseGraining dependency closure in an isolated support namespace.

main_results.informal: Under stationary unit-range assumptions and the source-tail bound, every generation beyond a scale of polynomial length has annealed contrast at most one plus the prescribed tolerance.
The annealed coarse blocks converge algebraically to a limiting positive-definite block, with two-sided order estimates.

Uniformly elliptic stationary unit-range laws satisfy the negative-Sobolev Dirichlet estimate, corrector estimates, Liouville classification and first-order approximation obtained by specializing the polynomial homogenization theorem.

High-contrast stationary unit-range laws admit an effective matrix and a random homogenization radius with polynomial length and quantitative tails, negative-Sobolev Dirichlet estimates on adapted cells, correctors, Liouville classification and large-scale regularity.
Coarse coefficients converge almost surely beyond a quantitative random scale, with the documented source-tail and stretched-exponential tail estimates.

projects.title: A complex structure on the six-sphere
projects.summary: Formalizes Levent Alpöge's construction of a complex-analytic atlas on the standard six-sphere. The development builds a compact complex threefold from torus fibrations with cusp and elliptic fibres, computes its homology and fundamental group, proves that its underlying topological space is homeomorphic to the six-sphere, and transports the complex atlas across that homeomorphism. It adapts Lean developments by Yury G. Kudryashov and Sebastian Kumar, together with the statement from the Formal Conjectures Authors.

source.title: HopfProblem: formalization of Alpöge's six-sphere construction

main_results.informal: The standard unit six-sphere admits a complex three-dimensional charted-space structure making it a complex-analytic manifold.
The standard unit six-sphere admits a complex three-dimensional charted-space structure making it a continuously differentiable complex manifold.
The formalized statement of MathOverflow question 1973: the standard six-sphere carries a complex three-dimensional manifold atlas.

projects.title: Hard-sphere Mayer NBC identity and fork-packing volume bound
projects.summary: A kernel-checked Lean formalization of the exact no-broken-circuit volume identity for hard-sphere Mayer cluster integrals and the stronger dimension-three fork-packing upper bound for each tree-owned NBC region. The development proves finite broken-circuit cancellation, the measurable finite-region decomposition, the anchored Euclidean product-measure theorem, and its explicit flat-coordinate transport.  Its geometric result is the attachment-aware estimate Vol(NBC_T) <= (17/32)^hardSphereNu T * hardSphereKappa^(k-1), where hardSphereNu T is the maximum cardinality of a packing of pairwise vertex-disjoint, order-compatible forks in T.  A formal fork is an ordered triple (a,b,c) with a < b < c, center a, leaves b,c, and tree edges {a,b} and {a,c}.  The central contribution is the complete pointwise-to-integral bridge together with the orientation-aware measure-preserving factorization that realizes the per-fork volume suppression.

main_results.informal: The absolute hard-sphere Mayer coefficient, multiplied by the factorial, equals the sum of nonnegative no-broken-circuit region volumes over spanning trees.

For a spanning tree in three dimensions, its no-broken-circuit region has volume at most (17/32) to the maximum disjoint compatible-fork packing size times the unit-ball volume to the number of tree edges.

projects.title: Homogeneous self-dual interior-point method for linear programming
projects.summary: Formalizes a homogeneous self-dual interior-point method for linear programming, including primal-dual data, Newton block solvability from full row rank, fixed Ye-Todd-Mizuno predictor/corrector local estimates, contraction bounds, and logarithmic stopping certificates for generated iterates.

source.title: An O(√nL)-iteration homogeneous and self-dual linear programming algorithm

main_results.informal: Packages the fixed Ye-Todd-Mizuno local theory, combining predictor and corrector estimates for the tight and wide central neighborhoods.
main_results.source_ref: Y. Ye, M. J. Todd, and S. Mizuno, An O(√nL)-iteration homogeneous and self-dual linear programming algorithm, Mathematics of Operations Research 19(1):53-67, 1994.

main_results.informal: Proves that the generated even iterate satisfies the gap stopping test at the logarithmic pair bound.
Proves that the generated even iterate satisfies the duality-measure stopping test at the scaled logarithmic pair bound.
Shows solvability of the Newton block system from the full-row-rank assumption through finite-dimensional linear algebra.
Bounds the fixed YTM contraction power by the corresponding exponential decay estimate.

projects.title: Chabauty–Coleman bounds for odd-degree hyperelliptic curves
projects.summary: Proves the rank-sensitive Chabauty–Coleman point-count bound for monic odd-degree hyperelliptic curves over the rationals and number fields at primes of squarefree reduction. The Jacobian group is the ideal class group of the affine coordinate ring; its identification with an algebraic Jacobian variety is outside this formalization. Includes Mumford representatives, reduction of divisor classes, multivariable formal groups, p-adic logarithms, and residue-disk zero counts. Independent upstream archive results are omitted.

source.title: Independence of rational points on twists of a given curve

main_results.informal: For a monic odd-degree hyperelliptic curve over Q whose coordinate-ring class group has rational rank at most r below the genus, and a prime p greater than 2r + 2 with an integral model of squarefree reduction, the affine rational point count plus one is at most the reduced affine point count plus one, plus 2r.

Over the fraction field of a Dedekind domain finite free over Z, the same class-group-rank bound holds at a prime of squarefree reduction when the residue characteristic exceeds 2r plus the absolute ramification index plus 1.

The set of rational affine points on a monic odd-degree hyperelliptic curve over a number field is finite when the rational rank of the ideal class group of its affine coordinate ring is smaller than its genus.

projects.title: Gödel's First and Second Incompleteness Theorems
projects.summary: Formalizes Gödel's first and second incompleteness theorems for first-order arithmetic, building on formalized arithmetization and provability-logic infrastructure.

main_results.informal: Proves Gödel's first incompleteness theorem: a Sigma1-sound Delta1-definable theory extending arithmetic is incomplete.
Proves Gödel's second incompleteness theorem: such a theory cannot prove its own consistency.

projects.title: Infinitary logic and countable model theory
projects.summary: Formalizes the syntax and semantics of infinitary logic and a broad collection of its classical theorems: Scott sentences and ranks, Karp's theorem, model existence, the sharp Morley--Hanf bound, Craig, Lyndon, and Malitz interpolation, López--Escobar definability, undefinability of well-ordering, the Silver--Burgess and Morley counting dichotomies, and an honest coded-fragment interface whose HF compactness theorem is derived from first-order compactness.

source.title: Infinitary Logic in Lean 4

main_results.informal: Every countable structure in a countable relational language has an associated infinitary sentence.
A countable structure satisfies the Scott sentence of another countable structure exactly when the two structures are isomorphic.
The Scott rank of a countable structure is the supremum of its element ranks plus one.
The Scott rank of every countable structure in a countable relational language is a countable ordinal.
Two relational structures admit a nonempty potential isomorphism exactly when they agree on every infinitary sentence over every branching carrier in their shared universe.
Every countable set of infinitary sentences in an equality-respecting consistency property over a countable language has a countable model.
Beth omega-one is a Hanf bound for every infinitary sentence.
The Hanf number of countable-conjunction infinitary logic is exactly beth omega-one.
A sentence with arbitrarily large models has, at every infinite cardinality, a model realizing only countably many complete types.
Every infinitary-small model belongs to a complete infinitary subclass contained in any prescribed sentence it satisfies.
A categorical sentence with arbitrarily large models has a complete categorical refinement at the same infinite cardinality.
Every sentence entailment has an interpolant using only the function and relation symbols shared by its two endpoints.
Disjoint projective infinitary classes can be separated by a single infinitary sentence.
Every sentence entailment has an interpolant whose positive and negative relation occurrences lie in the corresponding shared occurrence sets.
An entailment with universal consequent in a relational language has a universal interpolant over the shared vocabulary.
If a sentence has chains of every countable length, some model carries a relation-preserving map from the rationals.
The order types of all well-ordered models of one infinitary sentence are bounded below omega-one.
No single infinitary sentence defines exactly the well-orders.
A class of coded countable structures is Borel and isomorphism-invariant exactly when it is the model class of one infinitary sentence.
The López--Escobar characterization equivalently uses invariance under the natural permutation action on coded structures.
The class of coded well-orders is not a Borel set in the logic space.
A Borel equivalence relation on a Polish space with uncountably many classes has a continuous Cantor injection of pairwise inequivalent points.
A standard-Borel quotient has at most countably many classes or exactly continuum many classes.
Assuming the Silver--Burgess dichotomy, the number of isomorphism classes of coded countable models of an infinitary sentence is at most aleph-one or exactly the continuum.
Isomorphism among models of an infinitary sentence is Borel whenever their Scott heights have a common countable bound.
A coded-family presentation packages codes with their indexed decoding and a certificate for admissible infinitary formation.
A coded family packages a certified family code with an explicitly indexed decoding, made unique by the presentation's decoding law.
An admissible fragment is closed under exactly the coded infinitary families certified by its presentation.
The hereditarily finite fragment consists of the infinitary formulas whose syntax contains no infinitary connective.
The hereditarily finite fragment forms an admissible coded fragment without assuming compactness data.
Every finitely satisfiable theory contained in the first-order image fragment has a model.

projects.title: Infinite counterexamples to Connes's rigidity conjecture
projects.summary: Constructs one finitely generated property-(T) ICC group and an infinite family of finitely generated property-(T) ICC groups that are pairwise nonisomorphic and are each nonisomorphic to the first group, while all of their tracial group von Neumann algebras are normally star-isomorphic. This unconditional infinite-family result is independent of the pooled conditional two-group Connes-rigidity formalization.

source.title: Ten advances in mathematics and theoretical computer science

main_results.informal: Registry-friendly alias of the exact canonical infinite-family Connes-rigidity counterexample theorem below.

There exist a finitely generated property-(T) ICC group and an infinite sequence of finitely generated property-(T) ICC groups such that all their tracial group von Neumann algebras are normally star-isomorphic, although the sequence is pairwise nonisomorphic and none of its groups is isomorphic to the distinguished group.

projects.title: Inflation termination for classical pair-source networks
projects.summary: For finite binary pair-source networks without isolated vertices, classifies when the inflation hierarchy characterizes compatibility with finite latent alphabets: precisely forests of double stars, where order two suffices. Also proves triangle nontermination for arbitrary measurable latent probability spaces, quantitative obstructions, finite and measurable Finner inequalities, and graph witnesses.

main_results.informal: For finite binary pair-source graphs without isolated vertices, some finite order of the Navascués–Wolfe hierarchy characterizes compatibility with finite latent alphabets exactly for double-star forests; order two suffices there.
At every positive inflation order, a triangle law passes both the AI and NW tests but has no compatible model over any measurable latent probability spaces.

projects.title: Ordered resource algebras and the Iris recursive domain model
projects.summary: Constructs the algebraic core of the Iris proposition model from complete step-indexed spaces, ordered resource algebras, finite-support ghost maps, and monotone predicates. Proves guarded fixed-point unfolding and uniqueness, solves contractive mixed-variance domain equations, and constructs mutually inverse folding and unfolding maps for the recursive proposition model. Includes the October 2026 ordered-resource generalization and reusable morphism, product, optional-resource, and frame-preserving update infrastructure. The import is the mathematical dependency closure of IProp; it does not include the proof mode, HeapLang, program logics, or claims about their soundness.

source.title: Iris in Lean and the ordered resource algebra extension

main_results.informal: Every contractive endomorphism of an inhabited complete ordered family of equivalences has a constructed fixed point satisfying its unfolding equation.
Any fixed point of a contractive endomorphism of an inhabited complete ordered family of equivalences equals the constructed fixed point.

For a contractive mixed-variance functor preserving complete step-indexed spaces, with an inhabited value at the lifted unit space, folding after unfolding is the identity on its constructed recursive domain.
Under the same functor, completeness, and inhabitation hypotheses, unfolding after folding is the identity on the functor applied to the recursive domain.
For every family of contractive affine resource functors, folding after unfolding is the identity on the associated monotone proposition model.
For every such family of resource functors, unfolding after folding is the identity on the associated guarded recursive pre-proposition domain.

projects.title: Verified canonical labelling of finite graphs
projects.summary: Implements an individualisation-refinement canonical-labelling algorithm in the style of nauty and proves that its canonical adjacency form is invariant under vertex relabelling and classifies finite graphs up to isomorphism. The imported core includes the executable search, refinement, orbit-pruning and backjumping machinery together with its equivariance, termination, soundness and optimality proofs.

source.title: IsoGraph

main_results.informal: Two Boolean adjacency functions on Fin n have equal canonical forms exactly when one is a relabelling of the other by a vertex permutation.
Relabelling a finite graph by any permutation leaves its canonical adjacency form unchanged.
Equality of canonical adjacency forms yields an explicit permutation relating the original adjacency functions.

projects.title: Prekopa-Leindler, Brunn-Minkowski, and the isoperimetric inequality
projects.summary: Formalizes the Prekopa-Leindler inequality, Brunn-Minkowski inequality, and an isoperimetric inequality.

main_results.informal: Proves the Prekopa-Leindler inequality.
Proves the Brunn-Minkowski inequality.
Proves the isoperimetric inequality derived from Brunn-Minkowski.

projects.title: The transcendence of π
projects.summary: Formalizes a self-contained proof, following Niven's 1939 argument, that the real and complex number π is transcendental over the rationals.

main_results.informal: Proves that the complex number π is transcendental over ℚ.
Proves that the real number π is transcendental over ℚ.
Shows that if π is algebraic over ℚ then so is iπ.
Produces a monic rational polynomial vanishing at iπ when iπ is algebraic.

projects.title: Iwaniec's linear sieve and Jacobsthal's bound
projects.summary: Proves an absolute O((r log r)^2) bound for any run of consecutive integers covered by r distinct primes, using the Rosser-Iwaniec linear sieve at the sifting limit. Preserves the combinatorial sieve, delay-equation majorants, prime-sum estimates and the proved strong prime-number-theorem dependency. This imports the dependency closure of the Jacobsthal corollary, rather than claiming the upstream formalizations of both papers in full.

source.title: On the problem of Jacobsthal

main_results.informal: There is an absolute real constant C such that, for every finite set S of at least two primes and every interval of m consecutive integers each divisible by a prime in S, m is at most C times (|S| log |S|)^2.
Rosser's lower-bound sieve for the first r primes transfers to any set of r primes, bounding the number of integers avoiding all those primes.

At a fixed constant times z squared, Rosser's lower-bound sieve has main term bounded below by a positive constant times R(z)/log z and support bounded above by a constant times z squared divided by log squared z, for all sufficiently large z.

projects.title: The Jacobian of a Compact Riemann Surface
projects.summary: Constructs the Jacobian of a compact Riemann surface as the period-lattice quotient of the dual of holomorphic 1-forms, and proves the surrounding theory it needs: the genus as the dimension of the space of holomorphic 1-forms, discreteness and full rank 2g of the period lattice, the Abel-Jacobi map and its injectivity in positive genus, functoriality (pushforward, pullback, degree, and the projection formula), Riemann-Roch, Serre duality via Laurent tails, the residue theorem, the Dolbeault-Cech comparison, and finite dimensionality of the first cohomology by a Schwartz/Montel argument. The headline no-hack guard is that the genus vanishes exactly when the surface is homeomorphic to the sphere.

source.title: Jacobians of compact Riemann surfaces (AI challenge)

main_results.informal: A compact connected Riemann surface has genus zero if and only if it is homeomorphic to the 2-sphere.
The Abel-Jacobi map of a compact Riemann surface of positive genus is injective: two points with the same image coincide.
For a non-constant holomorphic map between compact Riemann surfaces, the pushforward composed with the pullback on Jacobians is multiplication by the degree of the map.

projects.title: The Johnson–Lindenstrauss Lemma and Quantized JL
projects.summary: Formalizes the Johnson–Lindenstrauss lemma end to end — a Gaussian random projection preserves pairwise distances of a finite point set up to a (1 ± ε) factor, so a distortion-ε embedding of any m-point set exists once k is logarithmic in m — together with the quantized JL (QJL) one-bit sign sketch: unbiasedness of the asymmetric 1-bit estimator and its sub-Gaussian distortion bound.

source.title: Extensions of Lipschitz mappings into a Hilbert space

main_results.informal: The abstract probabilistic-method union bound — if the summed per-pair distortion-failure probability is below one, a distortion-preserving map exists.
The end-to-end Johnson–Lindenstrauss lemma — a Gaussian random projection into k dimensions embeds any m-point set with (1 ± ε) distortion once k is logarithmic in m.
main_results.source_ref: S. Dasgupta, A. Gupta, An elementary proof of a theorem of Johnson and Lindenstrauss, Random Structures and Algorithms 22 (2003), 60-65, doi:10.1002/rsa.10073.

main_results.informal: The QJL asymmetric 1-bit estimator is unbiased for the normalized inner product between key and query.
main_results.source_ref: A. Zandieh, M. Daliri, I. Han, QJL: 1-Bit Quantized JL Transform for KV Cache Quantization with Zero Overhead, AAAI 2025, arXiv:2406.03482.

main_results.informal: Sub-Gaussian distortion bound for the QJL 1-bit estimator: deviation at least ε has probability at most 2·exp(-m·ε²/(π·‖q‖²)).
main_results.source_ref: A. Zandieh, M. Daliri, I. Han, QJL: 1-Bit Quantized JL Transform for KV Cache Quantization with Zero Overhead, AAAI 2025, arXiv:2406.03482.

projects.title: Kahn–Kalai expectation-threshold theorem
projects.summary: Formalizes Tran and Vu's short proof of the Park–Pham theorem resolving the Kahn–Kalai expectation-threshold conjecture. For an ℓ-bounded family of subsets of a finite ground set, it proves the strengthened covering theorem with the explicit constant L = 1000 and derives the threshold bound p_c(F) ≤ K q(F) log₂ ℓ with the explicit witness K = 100000. The supporting library develops finite-set cover cost, level-density, double-counting, binomial-tail, and numeric estimates.

source.title: A Short Proof of Kahn-Kalai Conjecture

main_results.informal: If ℓ ≤ N, p lies in [0, 1], and an ℓ-bounded family H has cover cost at least 1/2 - 2^(-(ℓ+2)), then its upset has at least (2/3 + 2^(-(ℓ+2))) choose(N, m) members of cardinality m, where m = floor(1000 p N log₂(ℓ+1)). For m ≤ N this is the corresponding level-density bound; for N < m both cardinalities are zero.
There is an absolute positive constant K such that every ℓ-bounded finite family with ℓ at least two satisfies p_c(F) ≤ K q(F) log₂ ℓ; the proof supplies K = 100000.

projects.title: Halving the Kalton-Roberts upper bound
projects.summary: Formalizes the paper-style Boolean-algebra theorem that every approximately additive real-valued set function is uniformly close to a finitely additive signed measure, proving the certified Kalton-Roberts constant bound below 19.838.

source.title: Halving the original Kalton-Roberts upper bound for nearly additive set functions

main_results.informal: Proves the headline certified bound that the Kalton-Roberts constant is strictly less than 9919/500, i.e. 19.838.
Proves the exact rational upper bound C₂ = 694198146664396294486127753 / 34994834677886019996000000 for the Kalton-Roberts constant.
States the paper-style set-algebra formulation, where every approximately additive function on a Boolean subalgebra of sets is within C₂ times the error of a finitely additive signed measure.

projects.title: Rank parity and complex structures on the Kalton–Peck space
projects.summary: Develops symplectic Fredholm theory and the real Kalton–Peck space to prove rank parity of finite-rank perturbations and rule out a complex structure on a hyperplane.

main_results.informal: The abstract symplectic Fredholm construction yields a rank-parity theorem.
On the real Kalton–Peck space, T² + 1 has even rank whenever its rank is finite.
A hyperplane of the real Kalton–Peck space cannot carry a complex structure.

projects.title: Carlet's Kasami cyclic-additive conjecture
projects.summary: Proves Carlet's cyclic-additive conjecture for the Kasami power function: over every finite field of characteristic two with cardinality 2^n and every k coprime to n, the normalized derivative image has the exact coefficient triple count 2^(2n-3) for all distinct nonzero slopes. The development combines the Müller--Cohen--Matthews permutation theorem, multiplicative character sums, Fourier inversion, and a Fermat-cubic Frobenius-kernel argument.

source.title: On a conjecture on the Kasami APN function

main_results.informal: For every finite field K of characteristic two with |K| = 2^n, every k coprime to n, and all distinct nonzero v₁ and v₂ in K, the coefficient triple count of the normalized Kasami derivative image is exactly 2^(2n-3).
In the normalized range 1 ≤ k < n, the same coefficient triple count is 2^(2n-3), assuming characteristic two, |K| = 2^n, coprimality, and distinct nonzero coefficients.
Under the normalized admissibility hypotheses, the image of the Kasami derivative has exactly half as many elements as the field.

projects.title: Kloosterman–Weil bounds via Carlitz and Stepanov
projects.summary: Proves the classical prime Kloosterman–Weil bound by extension-field recurrences and auxiliary-polynomial point counts. Develops exact CRT factorization, squarefree bounds with a unit first coefficient, and centered incomplete reciprocal-phase bounds at the reduced modulus.

source.title: Weil Bounds Toolkit

main_results.informal: For every prime p and nonzero coefficients m and n modulo p, the norm of the standard Kloosterman sum is at most twice the square root of p.
Kloosterman sums factor exactly over coprime nonzero moduli, with explicit Bezout-normalized coefficients.

For a positive squarefree modulus q, the mean-centered reciprocal phase defined at q divided by gcd(A,q) has interval sums bounded uniformly in interval length by its squarefree Weil constant times one plus log of that reduced modulus.
For every nonzero squarefree modulus q and unit first coefficient, the Kloosterman sum is bounded by 2 to the number of prime factors of q times the square root of q.

projects.title: Disproof of the Köthe conjecture (Krempa's matrix form)
projects.summary: Refutes Köthe's 1930 conjecture in Krempa's matrix form: there is a ring R (the unitization of a nil algebra of three weighted backward shifts over the algebraic closure of F_2) with a nil two-sided ideal I such that the matrix ideal M_2(I) contains a non-nilpotent matrix. The compared theorem is exactly the negation of the research-open statement `Koethe.KotherConjecture.variants.general_matrix` from Google DeepMind's Formal Conjectures, in every universe. The supporting library proves a multiprojective common-zero theorem via the Segre cone, the Nullstellensatz and Krull's height theorem, a mask-mortality theorem for one-row matrix pencils, a diagonal construction of universal mortal sequences, and a linearization theorem reducing nilness of a three-generator algebra to nilness of its root-row pencils.

source.title: A counterexample to Köthe's conjecture and a question of Rowen

main_results.informal: It is not the case that for every ring R, every nil two-sided ideal I of R and every finite index type n, the matrix ideal M_n(I) of M_n(R) is nil. This is the negation of Krempa's matrix form of Köthe's conjecture, stated verbatim as in Formal Conjectures.
In every universe there is a ring R with a nil two-sided ideal I such that some 2 x 2 matrix with entries in I is not nilpotent.
Over an algebraically closed field, at most 2N polynomials that are multihomogeneous of a common positive degree in each of N blocks of three variables have a common zero with no block equal to zero.

Over an algebraically closed field, every one-row matrix pencil and every periodic mask with more than half of its residues free admit a mask-compatible word of nonzero letters whose forward product is the zero matrix.
Over a countable field satisfying mask mortality there is a sequence of nonzero letter triples such that every pencil has all its windows of some fixed positive length equal to zero.
If every root-row pencil lifted along three elements of an algebra is nilpotent, then the non-unital subalgebra they generate is nil.

projects.title: The Komlós and Beck–Fiala bounds with constant 36
projects.summary: Proves that finitely many real vectors of Euclidean norm at most one admit signs whose sum has every coordinate bounded by 36, and deduces the Beck–Fiala discrepancy bound 36 times the square root of the maximum vertex degree for finite hypergraphs. The Karingula–Lovett splitting argument is supported by reusable finite-distribution, total-variation, transport, convex-hull, and matrix-discrepancy infrastructure. The near-invariant distribution uses discrete squared tent weights, and real vectors are handled by coordinatewise truncation toward zero.

source.title: An elementary proof of the Komlós conjecture

main_results.informal: For a real matrix with arbitrary finite row and column index types, if each column has sum of squared entries at most one, its minimum signed-column discrepancy is at most 36.
main_results.source_ref: Theorem 1.2, matrix form.

main_results.informal: Any finite family of vectors in a finite-dimensional real Euclidean space, each of norm at most one, admits signs in {-1, 1} whose signed sum has absolute value at most 36 in every coordinate.
main_results.source_ref: Theorem 1.2.

main_results.informal: If a hypergraph has finitely many vertices and each vertex belongs to at most t edges, there is a {-1, 1} colouring of all vertices whose sum on each edge has absolute value at most 36 times sqrt(t).
main_results.source_ref: Beck–Fiala consequence discussed in Section 1.

main_results.informal: For a finitely supported probability distribution on any real module and n vectors, if translation by six times each vector has total variation distance at most one third, some signed sum added to the mean belongs to the convex hull of the distribution's support.
main_results.source_ref: Lemma 1.4, generalized to arbitrary real modules.

main_results.informal: Every positive-denominator integer grid in finite-dimensional real coordinate space admits a finitely supported mean-zero probability distribution in [-6, 6]^d whose total variation distance under any grid translation of Euclidean norm at most one is at most one third.
main_results.source_ref: Lemma 1.5, using discrete squared tent weights.

projects.title: A Conditional Sieve Criterion for Twin Primes via Krafft Geometry
projects.summary: Introduces an original conditional sieve criterion for the Twin Prime Conjecture. Using a centered modular alignment (termed the Krafft alignment), proves that if the Rayleigh-Ritz quotient over the orthogonal unit sphere satisfies muMin < 1, then a twin prime pair must exist in the corresponding interval.

main_results.informal: Proves that muMin n < 1 is a sufficient condition for the existence of a twin prime pair in the corresponding interval.

If there are infinitely many intervals where the optimal multidimensional weight achieves a ratio strictly less than 1, then there are infinitely many twin primes. This is a conditional reduction; the hypothesis muMin n < 1 is not established here for any n.

projects.title: Aperiodic and simple-group wreath-division towers
projects.summary: Constructs a finite recursive wreath-division tower for every finite monoid in universe zero, with finite aperiodic or finite simple-group factors and every simple-group factor a monoid divisor of the original monoid. Implements a variant of the Diekert–Kufleitner–Steinberg local-divisor argument, with reusable monoid and semigroup division, local divisors, action coverings, wreath reassociation, and the Krasner–Kaloujnine group embedding. The endpoint permits arbitrary aperiodic factors and recursive intermediate bases; it does not assert the three-element flip-flop reduction, a single transformation-monoid strong division, or quantitative decomposition bounds.

source.title: Krohn–Rhodes formalization by Aditya Rao

main_results.informal: Every finite monoid M in universe zero admits a finite list of finite monoid factors, each witnessed to be aperiodic or a simple group, with DivTowerWreath M factors and every simple-group factor a monoid divisor of M. An empty tower means M divides the trivial monoid. At a nonempty step, M divides F wreath B for a finite action of a finite monoid B that itself has the tail tower.
main_results.source_ref: Upstream PrimeDecomposition.lean, completed September 28, 2026 at 07:36:52 UTC and publicly released at 08:48:24 UTC. Variant of Diekert–Kufleitner–Steinberg, arXiv:1111.1585, Sections 3–4, with left actions, the larger local divisor cM intersect Mc, arbitrary aperiodic factors, and recursive semigroup divisions. The stronger flip-flop and transformation-monoid claims of Theorem 4.1 are not asserted. Upstream CITATION.cff attributes the proofs primarily to Claude Code under Aditya Rao's direction.

main_results.informal: For any group G and normal subgroup N, the constructed monoid homomorphism from G to Mathlib's regular wreath product of N and G/N is injective. No finiteness assumption is required.
main_results.source_ref: Upstream Foundations/KrasnerKaloujnine.lean; the classical Krasner–Kaloujnine embedding theorem.

main_results.informal: For any monoid M and c in M, the local divisor on cM intersect Mc, with its twisted multiplication and identity c, is a quotient of a submonoid of M.
main_results.source_ref: Diekert–Kufleitner–Steinberg, arXiv:1111.1585, Section 2.5; uses the full local divisor rather than the smaller cMc union {c}.

projects.title: Finite-N Kuramoto Synchronization
projects.summary: Formalizes the finite-N Kuramoto model of coupled phase oscillators: the order parameter and its unit bound, the potential/force gradient identities, smoothness and local Lipschitz continuity of the vector field with ODE existence and uniqueness, Lyapunov descent along trajectories, pairwise and semicircle contraction estimates, Hebbian phase/weight dynamics, and full convergence to synchrony under all-to-all coupling from initial phases in an open semicircle.

source.title: Finite-N Kuramoto synchronization: order-parameter bounds and Lyapunov descent

main_results.informal: The Kuramoto order parameter has norm at most one for any phase configuration.
The weighted Kuramoto potential is non-increasing along the gradient flow, since the sum of force times potential-derivative over all oscillators is at most zero.
Under all-to-all coupling with positive strength and initial phases in an open semicircle, the order parameter norm tends to one, i.e. the oscillators synchronize.

projects.title: Kurosh and Schreier subgroup theorems via covering graphs
projects.summary: Proves the Kurosh subgroup theorem for arbitrary subgroups of indexed free products, with factors given by actual intersections with conjugates of the original factors and with the decomposition maps induced by their inclusions. The development constructs Bass–Serre trees, quotient graphs, graph-of-groups covers, path lifting, and normal forms. It also gives an explicit finite Schreier basis and classifies automorphisms of a finite regular Schreier action by its quotient group. The finite-graph basis infrastructure is reused from LeanPool.FiniteGraphFundamentalGroup.
authors: Ruy J. G. B. de Queiroz

source.title: Schreier and Kurosh subgroup theorems via covering graphs

main_results.informal: Every subgroup H of an arbitrary indexed free product admits a free product decomposition into a free group and subgroups of H that are intersections with conjugates of the original factors. The isomorphism to H is induced by the actual subgroup inclusions and a homomorphism from the free factor.
main_results.source_ref: Kurosh subgroup theorem; upstream inclusion-preserving statement.

main_results.informal: H is isomorphic to the free product of its nontrivial vertex stabilizers in the quotient Bass–Serre graph and the free group of that graph.

A finite-index subgroup H of a free group on any finite generator type of cardinality r has an explicit free basis of size d*r + 1 - d, where d is its index and subtraction is natural-number subtraction. This formulation also covers the empty generator type.
If the finite generator type is nonempty, the basis has the classical Schreier size 1 + d*(r - 1).
main_results.source_ref: Schreier index formula; DOI 10.1007/BF02952517.

main_results.informal: For a finite-index normal subgroup H of a group G, the automorphism group of the finite regular Schreier G-action is isomorphic to G/H by right translations. This is a theorem about the action, not a classification of general topological covers.
A subgroup with trivial stabilizers at every vertex of its quotient Bass–Serre graph is a free group.

projects.title: Finite witnesses and the width hierarchy for language generation
projects.summary: Characterizes generation in the limit for arbitrary families of infinite languages over any countably infinite universe by finite positive witnesses. Ordered-history generators admit a single set-driven normalization, chosen before the target language. The separation-width invariant takes every value 0, 1, 2, ..., omega, omega+1; generation is equivalent to width at most omega. Reusable infrastructure includes locking witnesses, positive separation, bounded diagonal capture over arbitrary universes, transport under equivalences, and finite-query normalization on natural numbers. The formalized scope is the semantic characterization and hierarchy, not the paper's additional density-one or Turing-computability results in Appendices D and E.

source.title: Characterizing Language Generation in the Limit: Finite Witnesses and a Separation-Width Hierarchy

main_results.informal: For any family H of infinite languages over a countably infinite universe, there exists one ordered-history generator that eventually outputs an unseen target element on every exact presentation of every target in H if and only if H admits a finite positive witness assignment whose nonempty active subfamilies always have infinite common intersection.

Every ordered-history generator over a countably infinite universe has one set-driven normalization that locks on every infinite target on which the original generator succeeds on all exact presentations. The normalization is chosen before the target.
A family of infinite languages over a countably infinite universe is generatable in the limit exactly when its separation width is at most omega.
Over every countably infinite universe, every value in WithTop (WithTop Nat), representing 0, 1, 2, ..., omega, omega+1, is the separation width of some family of infinite languages.

Over an arbitrary universe, every sequence of uniformly bounded finite sets has infinitely many terms contained in one set D such that D contains none of a prescribed countable list of infinite cores.

The finite-search normalization on natural numbers locks on every infinite language on which the supplied generator eventually succeeds on every exact presentation. This is a semantic correctness theorem for the defined procedure, without a formal Turing-computability claim.

projects.title: The smallest critical set in a Latin square
projects.summary: Proves that every partial Latin square of order n with fewer than floor(n²/4) filled cells has an even number of completions. Consequently every defining set has at least floor(n²/4) entries, and the two corner triangles in the cyclic square attain this bound as a critical set. Includes general results on matrix minors, square-zero ideals, and square-free polynomial coefficients.

main_results.informal: Every set of fewer than floor(n²/4) filled triples of an order-n partial Latin square has an even number of labelled Latin-square completions.
For every positive n, the smallest critical-set size among all Latin squares of order n, and the smallest critical-set size in the cyclic Latin square, both equal floor(n²/4).
Every defining set in every labelled Latin square of order n has at least floor(n²/4) cells.
For every positive n, the two opposite corner triangles form a critical set in the cyclic Latin square.

projects.title: On the paucity of lattice triangles
projects.summary: Formalizes an analytic lower bound used in the paucity theorem for lattice triangles.

main_results.informal: Proves the analytic-engine lower bound underlying the lattice-triangle result.

projects.title: Michal–Bastiani Calculus on Locally Convex Spaces
projects.summary: Develops real Michal–Bastiani calculus on Hausdorff locally convex spaces, with the chain rule, continuous symmetric higher differentials, and Taylor's formula in weak form. It proves equivalence with smooth Fréchet calculus on open subsets of normed spaces. Weak integrals exist for continuous curves in sequentially complete spaces and for continuously differentiable curves in Mackey complete spaces; Mackey completeness is characterized by weak integrability of Lipschitz curves. A smooth map from a Banach space to a normed space with derivative uniformly bounded below reflects finite differentiability of continuous maps from open locally convex domains.

source.title: Infinite-Dimensional Lie Groups

main_results.informal: Composing two real Michal–Bastiani C^k maps between open subsets of Hausdorff locally convex spaces preserves C^k regularity, provided the inner map takes the first domain into the second.
At every point of its open domain, the kth differential of a Michal–Bastiani C^k map is a continuous symmetric k-linear map.
On open subsets of real normed spaces, Michal–Bastiani smoothness is equivalent to Fréchet smoothness.
A continuous curve on the closed interval between any two real endpoints has a weak integral in every sequentially complete Hausdorff locally convex target space.

In a Hausdorff locally convex real space, convergence of Mackey–Cauchy sequences is equivalent to existence of weak integrals for all curves whose difference quotients form a bounded set on every nondegenerate compact real interval.

Let j be a smooth map from an open subset U of a real Banach space to a real normed space, with a fixed m > 0 such that every x in U and every vector v satisfy norm(dj(x)v) >= m * norm(v). If gamma maps an open locally convex domain continuously into U and j composed with gamma is C^k in the sense of Michal–Bastiani, then gamma is C^k.

projects.title: Analysis of Boolean functions in Lean
projects.summary: Walsh-Fourier analysis on Boolean functions, including Arrow's theorem and BLR linearity testing.

main_results.informal: Arrow's theorem for two-candidate Boolean voting rules.

projects.title: Carlson special functions and complex Dirichlet averages
projects.summary: Formalizes Carlson special functions through complex Dirichlet averages, with simplex measures, Gamma-regularized analytic continuation, Euler inversion, Euler–Poisson equations, and quadratic transformations. Includes the complete supporting several-complex-variable and special-function libraries.

main_results.informal: The Gamma-regularized Carlson R function satisfies the first quadratic transformation for complex exponent and Dirichlet parameters with positive-real-part unsquared variables.

For a holomorphic scalar function on a convex open domain D, its Gamma-regularized Dirichlet average extends jointly holomorphically to all complex Dirichlet parameters and all node vectors in D. The extension agrees with the regularized simplex integral when every parameter has positive real part; the ordinary normalized average differs by the factor Gamma of the parameter sum.

projects.title: Malliavin calculus and the Clark–Ocone representation
projects.summary: Constructs the Malliavin derivative, Gaussian integration by parts, closability, Wiener chaos, Brownian Itô integration and martingale representation. The Clark–Ocone endpoint uses a generating pre-Brownian process with continuous linear coordinates on a separable real Gaussian Banach space, its natural filtration, and pairs in the closed Malliavin graph; the conditional-expectation sections agree almost everywhere at positive times.

main_results.informal: For a generating pre-Brownian process on a separable real Gaussian Banach space whose coordinates are pointwise represented by continuous linear functionals, constructs a time realization of the Malliavin derivative and an Itô isometry for the natural filtration, with martingale representation for every terminal L² variable. For pairs in the closed Malliavin graph, the Clark–Ocone formula identifies the derivative's predictable projection with its conditional-expectation sections for almost every positive time.

projects.title: Formalizations of theorems related to model checking
projects.summary: Proves that every linear temporal logic formula has an equivalent finite-state nondeterministic Büchi automaton (via negation normal form, alternating Büchi automata, and the Miyano-Hayashi breakpoint construction), and that every linear-time property decomposes as the intersection of a safety property and a liveness property.

source.title: An Automata-Theoretic Approach to Linear Temporal Logic

main_results.informal: For any linear temporal logic formula there exists an equivalent finite-state nondeterministic Büchi automaton, i.e. one whose state type is finite, accepting the same language.
main_results.source_ref: M. Y. Vardi and P. Wolper, An automata-theoretic approach to automatic program verification, LICS 1986, 332-344; C. Baier and J.-P. Katoen, Principles of Model Checking, MIT Press, 2008, ISBN 978-0-262-02649-9, https://mitpress.mit.edu/9780262026499/principles-of-model-checking/

main_results.informal: The syntax of linear temporal logic formulas over a set of atomic propositions.
A nondeterministic Büchi automaton over a given alphabet of letters.
The Miyano-Hayashi breakpoint construction turns any alternating Büchi automaton over a finite state space into a nondeterministic Büchi automaton accepting the same language.
main_results.source_ref: S. Miyano and T. Hayashi, Alternating finite automata on omega-words, Theoretical Computer Science 32 (1984), 321-330, doi:10.1016/0304-3975(84)90049-5

main_results.informal: Every linear-time property is the intersection of a safety property and a liveness property.
main_results.source_ref: B. Alpern and F. B. Schneider, Defining liveness, Information Processing Letters 21 (1985), 181-185, doi:10.1016/0020-0190(85)90056-0

projects.title: Unitary dilation and the Crouzeix–Palencia bound
projects.summary: Proves unitary power dilation for Hilbert-space contractions, von Neumann’s polynomial inequality, and the Crouzeix–Palencia polynomial spectral-set estimate for the closed numerical range.

main_results.informal: Every contraction on a complex Hilbert space admits a unitary power dilation.
Polynomial evaluation on a contraction is bounded by the polynomial supremum on the closed unit disk.
The closure of the numerical range is a polynomial spectral set with constant 1 + √2.

projects.title: Polynomial ABC (Mason–Stothers) and its corollaries
projects.summary: Formalizes the Mason–Stothers theorem (the polynomial ABC theorem) and derives the polynomial Fermat's Last Theorem, the Fermat–Catalan inequality, Davenport's theorem, and a no-parametrization corollary.

source.title: Formalization of Polynomial ABC and FLT

main_results.informal: Mason–Stothers — for coprime non-constant polynomials with a+b=c, the max degree is below the degree of the radical of abc.
The polynomial Fermat's Last Theorem — no nontrivial coprime polynomial solutions of aⁿ+bⁿ=cⁿ for n ≥ 3.
The polynomial Fermat–Catalan inequality bounding solutions of aᵖ+bᵍ=cʳ.

projects.title: Lean-QuantumAlg
projects.summary: Provides a Mathlib-based library of formally verified quantum-algorithm definitions, primitives, and endpoints, including QFT, QSP, quantum kernels, amplitude amplification, Grover search, phase estimation, order finding, teleportation, and a Lie-algebraic barren-plateau witness.

source.title: Lean-QuantumAlg

main_results.informal: Proves the QFT action on computational-basis states and records exact circuit counts.
Characterizes reflection-based single-qubit QSP transforms in the Chebyshev basis.
Characterizes trigonometric single-qubit QSP transforms in the YZZYZ form.
Proves that fidelity quantum-kernel Gram matrices are positive semidefinite.
States the conditional quantum-kernel learning separation from discrete-log hardness.

Exhibits an exponentially vanishing loss-variance family for a fully controllable dynamical Lie algebra, conditional on the assumed Ragone second-moment variance law (the Haar/Weingarten averaging identity Var = P_g(rho)*P_g(O)/dim, taken as a hypothesis rather than derived from a circuit twirl).
Derives Grover search success probability from the amplitude-amplification closed form.

projects.title: A counterexample to Scottish Book Problem 155
projects.summary: A Lean proof that there are real Banach spaces X and Y and a bijection U from X to Y which preserves every pairwise distance on every closed ball of radius one quarter while failing to be a global isometry. This gives a counterexample to Scottish Book Problem 155.

main_results.informal: There exist real Banach spaces and a bijection between them that preserves all pairwise distances on each closed ball of radius one quarter but is not a global isometry.

projects.title: Classical several complex variables
projects.summary: Formalizes Cauchy and Taylor theory, Hartogs phenomena, removable singularities, analytic sets and germs, Weierstrass theory, holomorphic convexity, Cartan–Thullen and Bochner tube theorems, plurisubharmonic functions, Levi convexity, and elementary Runge-domain theory. Weierstrass preparation and coordinate-origin germ Noetherianity overlap LocalComplexGeometry; this development also supplies germ unique factorization and global extension and convexity results.

main_results.informal: Holomorphic functions on a polydisc satisfy the iterated Cauchy integral formula.
On an open subset of a finite complex coordinate space, a Banach-valued separately analytic map that is locally bounded is jointly analytic.
main_results.source_ref: Boas (2013), Section 2.7, Theorem 7 (the classical two-variable scalar case).

main_results.informal: Holomorphic functions on a connected domain that agree on a nonempty open subset agree throughout the domain.

projects.title: Pietsch s-numbers and the maximal difference theorem
projects.summary: Formalizes the five classical s-number sequences, their comparison inequalities, the maximal difference theorem, compact-operator singular value decomposition, John ellipsoids, entropy numbers, and compactness characterizations.

main_results.informal: For a bounded operator, its nth approximation number is at most e times (n+1) times its nth Hilbert number.
Every s-number sequence agrees with the approximation numbers on operators between Hilbert spaces.
In John position, the identity decomposes into a positive weighted sum of rank-one operators from contact points.

projects.title: lean-spectral-theory
projects.summary: The spectral theorem for possibly unbounded self-adjoint operators on complex Hilbert spaces, formalized through the Cayley transform and real projection-valued measures. The selected spectral theorem constructs a PVM whose scalar measures give the exact finite-second-moment domain and first-moment quadratic form, with measurable-set uniqueness, and is proved equivalent to equality with the unbounded coordinate spectral integral. The selected Stone theorem proves both that strongly continuous one-parameter unitary groups have self-adjoint generators and that every self-adjoint operator generates such a group.

main_results.informal: Every self-adjoint partial linear operator on a complex Hilbert space has a real projection-valued measure representing its domain and scalar moments, unique on Borel sets.
Every strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group has a self-adjoint generator, and every self-adjoint operator generates such a group.

projects.title: Square-function estimates from type IV superorthogonality
projects.summary: Proves the type IV superorthogonality square-function estimate for finite and countable index sets, including the pointwise combinatorial estimate and unconditional convergence in L^(2r).

main_results.informal: For an integer r >= 1, a countable type IV superorthogonal family in L^(2r), with almost-everywhere summable squared norms and square function in L^(2r), converges unconditionally in L^(2r) and satisfies the square-function bound with constant C(r).

projects.title: Craig Interpolation for Gödel-Löb logic via coalgebraic proofs
projects.summary: Formalizes a proof-theoretic Craig interpolation theorem for Gödel-Löb provability logic, built on a coalgebraic notion of circular proof.

main_results.informal: Proves the Craig interpolation theorem for Gödel-Löb provability logic.

projects.title: Coinductive Interaction Trees using QPFs
projects.summary: Formalizes coinductive interaction trees as the M-type of a polynomial functor (via Mathlib QPFs), proving the lawful functor and monad structure, a bisimulation equality coinciding with propositional equality, and iteration and effect-handler interpretation combinators, supported by a vendored parameterized-coinduction (Paco) library.
projects.notice: Copyright (c) 2025 the choice-tree authors (see the AUTHORS file)

main_results.informal: Defines the coinductive interaction tree as the final coalgebra (M-type) of the interaction-tree polynomial functor.
Defines bisimulation equality between interaction trees as a coinductive fixed point.
Proves that bisimulation equality of interaction trees coincides with propositional equality.
Proves associativity of monadic bind for interaction trees, part of the LawfulMonad instance.
Defines the iteration combinator producing an interaction tree from a step function.
Defines interpretation of an interaction tree against an effect handler into an arbitrary iterable monad.
Proves the accumulation principle for the parameterized least fixed point underlying the Paco coinduction library.
main_results.source_ref: C.-K. Hur, G. Neis, D. Dreyer, V. Vafeiadis, The Power of Parameterization in Coinductive Proof, POPL 2013, doi:10.1145/2429069.2429093.

projects.title: Formalized Complex Analysis in Lean
projects.summary: Formalizes Poisson integral formulas on the unit disc and arbitrary centered discs, Herglotz–Riesz representation, and Harnack's inequality on the unit disc, plus infrastructure for univalent function classes S and Σ.

main_results.informal: Proves the Poisson integral formula for harmonic functions on the unit disc.
Proves the Poisson integral formula for harmonic functions on arbitrary centered discs.
Proves that every positive harmonic function on the unit disc with value 1 at 0 has a unique Herglotz–Riesz representation by a probability measure on the unit circle.
Proves Harnack's inequality for positive harmonic functions on the unit disc.

projects.title: Modular forms and the generalized residue theorem
projects.summary: Formalizes the Hungerbühler-Wasem generalized residue theorem for Cauchy principal value integrals through poles and applies it to the valence formula for modular forms on the modular group.

main_results.informal: Proves the Hungerbühler-Wasem generalized residue theorem for piecewise-C1 curves through poles.
Specializes the generalized residue theorem to the simple-pole case.
Proves the valence formula for modular forms on the modular group.

projects.title: Lehmer's Polynomial and the E10 Coxeter Element
projects.summary: Proves that Lehmer's degree-10 polynomial — the integer polynomial of smallest known Mahler measure above 1 — is irreducible over the integers, and that it is the characteristic polynomial of a Coxeter element of the E10 Weyl group (the rank-10 instance of McMullen). Against Mathlib's Mahler-measure API it computes M(L) exactly as the Salem root with the unconditional bounds 1 < M(L) < 7/5, states Lehmer's conjecture as a defined Prop (never assumed) with the strong form implying the gap form, and contrasts the E8 Coxeter element (order exactly 30) with the E10 element (infinite order in GL(10,Z)): the E-series crosses from torsion to a Salem matrix at rank 10, and the crossing value is Lehmer's number.

main_results.informal: Lehmer's polynomial L(x) = x^10 + x^9 - x^7 - x^6 - x^5 - x^4 - x^3 + x + 1 is irreducible over the integers, and the characteristic polynomial of a Coxeter element of the E10 Weyl group equals L.
The Mahler measure of L equals its Salem root mu, with the unconditional bounds 1 < M(L) < 7/5.

projects.title: Lentil: Temporal Logic of Actions in Lean 4
projects.summary: A shallow embedding of Leslie Lamport's Temporal Logic of Actions (TLA) in Lean 4, with the temporal modalities, standard propositional and temporal proof rules, weak-fairness and leads-to reasoning, and an interactive proof mode for TLA judgments.

main_results.informal: Defines the TLA "always" (box) temporal modality, asserting a predicate holds on every suffix of an execution.
Defines the TLA "eventually" (diamond) temporal modality, asserting a predicate holds on some suffix of an execution.
The always-induction rule, equating `□ p` with `p` together with `□ (p → ◯ p)`.
The WF1 weak-fairness proof rule deriving a leads-to property from a next-state action under weak fairness.
Characterizes weak fairness of an action as a leads-to property between its enabledness and its occurrence.
Transitivity of the leads-to relation.

projects.title: Li's criterion for the Riemann Hypothesis
projects.summary: Li's criterion for the Riemann zeta function, formalized in Lean 4 over Mathlib: Mathlib's `RiemannHypothesis` holds if and only if every Li-Keiper coefficient of the completed xi function has nonnegative real part. The zero-indexed analytic coefficient at n is Li's classical lambda_(n+1), the n-th Taylor coefficient at 0 of the logarithmic derivative of s |-> xi(1/(1-s)).
