A second compared theorem identifies this analytic coefficient with Li's arithmetic coefficient, the symmetrized sum over the nontrivial zeros counted with multiplicity, and proves that symmetrized family summable so the sum is the genuine one. Both results are unconditional: the biconditional, the coefficient identification, the genus-1 Hadamard factorization of xi (with multiplicity), genus-1 summability of 1/|rho|^2, and the growth bound order(xi) <= 1 are all proved. This is a formalization of a classically known equivalence (X.-J. Li, 1997); it is not a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis, nor of the positivity of the coefficients.

main_results.informal: The Riemann hypothesis is equivalent to nonnegativity of every Li–Keiper coefficient.
The analytic Li–Keiper coefficients equal the symmetrically summed arithmetic coefficients over the nontrivial zeros.

projects.title: Lie–Trotter product formula with commutator scaling
projects.summary: Proves the Lie–Trotter product formula in a complete normed real algebra with norm-one unit, with an explicit error bound proportional to the commutator.

main_results.informal: For elements A and B of a complete normed real algebra with norm-one unit and every integer n at least one, the norm of the difference between (exp(A/n) exp(B/n))^n and exp(A+B) is at most norm(AB-BA) exp(norm(A)+norm(B))/(2n).
For any two elements of a complete normed real algebra with norm-one unit, (exp(A/n) exp(B/n))^n converges in norm to exp(A+B).

projects.title: Line-graph colourings and matching decompositions
projects.summary: Connects Mathlib line-graph colourings to palette-indexed partitions of actual graph edges into Mathlib matching subgraphs. Both conversions are inverse, preserve each matching exactly, and allow empty colours without a default colour or a finiteness assumption. An edge equivalence yields exact edge accounting: natural-number counts require only finite edges and a finite palette, while indexed cardinal counts allow arbitrary vertices, edges, and palettes. This is classical representation interoperability, not a new colouring bound or a claim of priority.

source.title: Original Lean Pool graph-colouring and matching adapters

main_results.informal: Proper colourings of the line graph on any palette are equivalent to partitions of the original edges into matching subgraphs indexed by that palette, with empty classes permitted.
main_results.source_ref: New adapter proved in GraphColouringMatching/Basic.lean, using Mathlib's existing lineGraph, Coloring and Subgraph.IsMatching.

main_results.informal: Converting a matching decomposition to a colouring and extracting one colour class returns exactly its original matching subgraph.
Original graph edges are in bijection with the disjoint union of the edge types of the palette-indexed matching subgraphs.
For a finite edge set and finite palette, the number of graph edges equals the sum of the numbers of edges in its matching classes, even when the vertex set is infinite.

Without any finiteness assumption on vertices, edges, or colours, the cardinality of the graph edge set equals the indexed cardinal sum of the matching-class edge cardinalities, with a universe lift on the graph edge cardinality when required.
main_results.source_ref: Cardinal.lean applies Mathlib's indexed cardinal sum to the existing edgeEquivSigma; no infinite graph-colouring theorem is assumed.

main_results.informal: The line graph is k-colourable if and only if the graph edges decompose into k matchings, allowing unused colours.

projects.title: Häggkvist–Janssen list edge colouring of complete graphs
projects.summary: Proves that arbitrary lists of at least n colours on the edges of a complete graph with n vertices admit a proper list edge colouring. The proof constructs and proves uniqueness of the local rank certificate, identifies a nonzero extended-star polynomial coefficient, and applies Mathlib's combinatorial Nullstellensatz. This is an alternative proof presentation, not a literal translation of the article's argument. The conclusion uses Mathlib's actual edge type and line-graph colouring, with no certificate hypothesis and no restriction on the colour universe. This formalizes a classical theorem, not a new bound or a solution of the general list-edge conjecture.

source.title: New Bounds on the List-Chromatic Index of the Complete Graph and Other Simple Graphs

main_results.informal: For every finite vertex type V, arbitrary colour type and finite list on each edge of the complete graph, if every list has cardinality at least the number of vertices, there is a proper colouring of the line graph choosing a colour from each list. This includes orders zero and one.
main_results.source_ref: Häggkvist–Janssen (1997), Theorems 1.1 and 3.1, complete-graph case.

projects.title: Foundational local complex-analytic geometry
projects.summary: Develops a common Lean foundation for several classical local theorems in several complex variables: complex-analytic Weierstrass preparation with full germ uniqueness, Noetherianity of holomorphic-germ rings, finite projection for hypersurface germs, the holomorphic constant-rank normal form, and the finite-family local analytic Nullstellensatz. The imported development also exposes the arbitrary-ideal Nullstellensatz and regular level-set, submersion, and immersion consequences.

source.title: Foundational theorems in local complex-analytic geometry

main_results.informal: If a finite family of functions analytic at the origin has common zero set locally contained in the zero set of another analytic function, then a positive power of the latter is locally an analytic linear combination of the family.
For every finite complex dimension, including dimension zero, the local ring of holomorphic germs at the origin is Noetherian.

A nonzero hypersurface germ vanishing at the origin admits a linear coordinate change whose local quotient is finite free over the base germ ring, together with an explicit prepared equation and a proper, surjective finite-fiber projection of the local zero set.
An analytic map of locally constant complex rank is locally equivalent, through analytic source and target coordinates, to the standard rank projection.

A complex-analytic germ of exact order in one distinguished variable factors uniquely into a nonvanishing analytic unit and a monic Weierstrass polynomial whose analytic coefficient germs vanish at the origin.
main_results.source_ref: BochaoKong/classical-complex-wpt, commit b4a7273fe5c9752753c52e10494097569089642d (2026-08-28).

main_results.informal: For every ideal of the local holomorphic-germ ring, the ideal of germs vanishing on its local zero set equals its radical.
Near a regular point, the level set of a holomorphic map admits an analytic parametrization with an analytic local inverse on the level set.

projects.title: Improved long gaps between consecutive primes
projects.summary: Formalizes the unconditional lower bound showing that, for all sufficiently large X, the largest gap between consecutive primes below X is at least a positive constant times log X (log log X)^2 log log log log X / (log log log X)^2. The development includes the short-translates sieve proposition, divisor coefficient estimates, truncated product weights, moment bounds, and the Erdos--Rankin covering argument used to derive the headline result.

source.title: Improved Long Gaps Between Primes

main_results.informal: There are a positive constant c and a real threshold X0 such that for every X at least X0, some pair of consecutive indexed primes below X has gap greater than c times log X (log log X)^2 log log log log X / (log log log X)^2.
For all sufficiently large X, there are consecutive primes p < q with q at most X and q - p at least a fixed positive multiple of the improved long-gap scale.

For all sufficiently large x, every sufficiently sparse subset S of an interval of length between x and x(log x)^2 has a translate b + Q(x)t + S consisting entirely of composite numbers, with 1 <= t <= exp x.

projects.title: Gradient-only acceleration for generalized-smooth convex optimization
projects.summary: A damped accelerated method minimizes convex functions on real Hilbert spaces whose differentiable gradients satisfy the Hessian-growth bound norm(D gradient f x) <= L0 + L1 * norm(gradient f x). The development proves an explicit gradient-query budget for any positive accuracy, initial distance bound and initial objective-gap bound, with an attained minimum. It retains the oracle execution model, ordinary gradient descent, energy dissipation, charging arguments and two complementary convergence bounds. No objective value or line-search oracle is assumed.

main_results.informal: For positive L0, R, Delta and epsilon and nonnegative L1, a single damped accelerated algorithm returns a point of objective gap at most epsilon for every admissible convex objective with an attained minimum within distance R and initial objective gap at most Delta. Its exact gradient-query budget is zero when Delta <= epsilon; otherwise it is twice the natural ceiling of 4096 times (1 + sqrt(L0*R^2/epsilon) + min(ceil((L1*R)^(2/3))*D, D + (L1*R*D)^(2/3))), where D = log(4 + 4*Delta/epsilon).
Under the same convexity, gradient, Hessian-growth and initialization hypotheses, N accelerated steps reach objective gap epsilon whenever N >= 4096*(1 + sqrt(L0*R^2/epsilon) + D + (L1*R*D)^(2/3)).
Execution with any admissible exact-gradient oracle and a budget of 2*N gradient queries equals the N-step accelerated iterate, for every seed.

For L > 0, R >= 0 and epsilon > 0, a convex function with an exact L-Lipschitz gradient and initial distance at most R from a comparison point, ordinary gradient descent reaches objective gap epsilon after max(1, ceil(L*R^2/(2*epsilon))) queries.

projects.title: Low-weight Pauli dynamics and truncation error
projects.summary: Derives a normalized Pauli 2-norm truncation-error bound for concrete circuits of disjoint-support Hermitian Pauli rotations, with explicit locality, angle, step-count, and cutoff hypotheses. Develops a faithful matrix representation, Pauli coefficient reconstruction, finite Schur bounds, and reusable scalar multi-jump ladder estimates. Also proves a combinatorial light-cone bound and exact counterexamples showing why repeated product-formula layers must count toward the layer exponent. This is the norm-level analysis, not a formalization of expectation-value accuracy, Hamiltonian approximation, or the paper's full algorithm.

source.title: Classical Simulation of Noiseless Quantum Dynamics without Randomness

main_results.informal: For an observable supported on Pauli weights at most ko, a block of Γ positive-many disjoint-support layers of Hermitian rotations of weight at most kh, kh ≥ 2, and |sin θ| ≤ a ≤ αt/r with α > 0 and t ≥ 0, truncation to weight ko + m(kh - 1) after each of r blocks has Pauli 2-norm error at most (2Γ(kh - 1)αt)^(m+1) (e(m+1))^(ko/(kh-1)) times the input norm. The conditions include m ≥ 1, r ≥ 5, m ≤ r, rΓ ≥ 8(m+1)^2, and r ≥ 8e^2(ko+kh-1)αt. Γ counts every layer of the actual block, including repeated product-formula layers.
main_results.source_ref: Upstream STATEMENTS.md and Pauli/LayerError.lean at the pinned commit; norm-level counterpart of the revised supplement's truncation bound.

main_results.informal: A finite rectangular matrix over any RCLike field, with absolute row sums bounded by nonnegative R and absolute column sums bounded by nonnegative C, has Euclidean operator norm at most sqrt(RC).
main_results.source_ref: Upstream Schur.lean, finite-dimensional Schur test.

main_results.informal: Every Pauli string reachable through a list of disjoint-support kh-local layers, kh ≥ 1, has weight at most its initial weight times kh raised to the number of layers. Reachability is combinatorial; this theorem does not assert that a reachable coefficient is nonzero.
main_results.source_ref: Upstream Pauli/LayerWitness.lean, effective-layer light cone.

main_results.informal: For the explicit eight-qubit second-order word L1,L2,L2,L1 and angles 0 < θ < π/2, truncating the evolved weight-one input at weight one discards a nonzero coefficient of weight greater than four. Thus the two distinct layer types give an invalid bound 1*2^2; repetitions must be counted.
main_results.source_ref: Upstream Pauli/LayerCounterexample.lean, exact symbolic witness.

projects.title: Classification of low-dimensional solvable Lie algebras
projects.summary: Formalises the classification of solvable Lie algebras up to dimension three.

source.title: Classification and Identification of Lie Algebras

main_results.informal: Classifies three-dimensional solvable Lie algebras over arbitrary fields.

projects.title: The ten minimum universal collections of MacMahon cubes
projects.summary: Classifies all minimum universal inventories of six-coloured MacMahon cubes. A universal inventory can build a two-by-two-by-two model of every cube variety, with matching exterior faces and eight distinct physical copies. The minimum inventory size is twelve, exactly ten labelled inventories attain it, and they are precisely the two-triangle collections in Conway's tableau. Natural-number multiplicities are allowed; every minimum inventory has no repeated variety. The tableau has zero diagonal; its thirty off-diagonal entries are the varieties. The development also verifies all proper signed-axis rotations, the thirty varieties, all six-colour face assignments, and the equivalence of corner matching with physical face matching. This resolves Johnson and Roldán's Conjectures 4 and 8 (arXiv:2407.13208v1), with a stronger multiset conclusion.

main_results.informal: Twelve is the attained minimum size of a universal physical inventory.
Every universal physical inventory has at least twelve cubes.
Exactly ten labelled universal physical inventories have size twelve.

An inventory of twelve cubes is physically universal exactly when its Conway tableau is the two disjoint triangles of a partition of the six labels into two triples, with one copy of each directed edge.
Every variety has multiplicity at most one in a minimum universal inventory.
The rotation table contains precisely all proper signed-axis rotations.
The outward faces at each of the eight positions obey the coordinate sign rule.
Every off-diagonal tableau entry assigns the six distinct nonzero colours.
Every assignment of six distinct nonzero colours is a rotated tableau variety.
The variety and proper rotation representing a face assignment are unique.

projects.title: The main theorem of polytopes
projects.summary: Formalizes the Minkowski–Weyl theorem — the equivalence between V-polytopes (convex hulls of finite point sets) and bounded H-polytopes (finite intersections of half-spaces) in a finite-dimensional real vector space.

source.title: Main theorem of polytopes

main_results.informal: The Minkowski–Weyl theorem — a set is a V-polytope iff it is a bounded H-polytope.
main_results.source_ref: G. M. Ziegler, Lectures on Polytopes, GTM 152, Springer, 1995, Theorem 1.1.

main_results.informal: Every bounded H-polytope (finite intersection of half-spaces) is the convex hull of a finite point set.

projects.title: Markoff mod p
projects.summary: Lean 4 formalization of strong approximation for the Markoff surface modulo sufficiently large primes. The primary source is Bourgain-Gamburd-Sarnak.

main_results.informal: For primes exceeding the explicit bound, reduction of integral Markoff points to the Markoff surface modulo p is surjective as specified by the theorem.

projects.title: MarkovProcess
projects.summary: A Lean formalization of continuous-path Markov processes associated with conservative Feller transition semigroups on nonempty locally compact Polish spaces. A uniform Kolmogorov displacement-moment bound yields a unique measurable kernel from each starting point to continuous-path space, with the prescribed finite-dimensional distributions. The library also develops strong Markov properties, generators and resolvents, stopping and killing, and Brownian motion as an example.

main_results.informal: A conservative Feller transition semigroup on a nonempty locally compact Polish space satisfying the Kolmogorov moment criterion determines a unique continuous-path Markov kernel with its prescribed finite-dimensional distributions.

projects.title: Marshall Hall's theorem through finite cores
projects.summary: Formalizes Marshall Hall's finite-index free-factor theorem for finitely generated subgroups of finite-rank free groups. The proof extracts the finitely many suffix states of a subgroup generating set, completes the resulting partial generator actions to permutations of a finite state set, identifies the connected orbit with a finite core, and extends a geodesic spanning tree to obtain an inclusion-compatible free-product decomposition. It also exposes an explicit finite permutation separator for every finitely generated subgroup and element outside it, yielding the LERF consequence. The repository also proves binary and finite-indexed free-group instances of Grushko--Neumann rank additivity, and the arbitrary-factor binary theorem. The arbitrary-factor proof is carried by a finite labelled-graph fold, source-unfold, and monochromatic-vertex contraction reduction.
authors: Ruy J. G. B. de Queiroz

main_results.informal: Every finitely generated subgroup of a finite-rank free group is an inclusion-compatible free factor of a finite-index subgroup.
Every element outside a finitely generated subgroup of a finite-rank free group can be separated by an explicit finite permutation action.
The rank of a free product of finitely generated groups is the sum of their ranks.

projects.title: Global completeness of one-sorted definedness-free matching logic
projects.summary: Formalizes the one-sorted case of Chen and Roșu's global-completeness argument and independently discharges its local-completeness oracle by mechanizing the canonical-model construction from their 2019 Matching μ-Logic technical report (Theorem 73, Lemmas 80–81, and strong local completeness Theorem 83). The resulting theorem supplies both local completeness and soundness for countably infinite variable types.

source.title: Completeness and incompleteness of basic matching logic; Matching μ-Logic (2019 technical report)

main_results.informal: For a backward-closed subset of a matching-logic model, two valuations that agree inside the subset and both stay outside it otherwise give identical denotations after restriction to that subset.
The double-cover model over a nonempty backward-closed proper subset has exactly the denotation predicted by each of its two projections back to the original model.
For a closed theory and closed conclusion, global semantic consequence is equivalent to local consequence from the localized theory.
One-sorted basic matching logic has strong local completeness over an arbitrary one-sorted finitary signature when the element-variable type is countably infinite.

For a one-sorted finitary signature, closed premises and conclusion, and a countably infinite element-variable type, global semantic consequence is equivalent to derivability, with both soundness and local completeness discharged.

projects.title: Matrix multiplication exponent at most 9/4 over every field
projects.summary: The arithmetic exponent of square matrix multiplication is at most 9/4 over every field. The proof preserves a general tensor-rank and arithmetic-program library, extends Fourier separation to positive characteristic, and descends finite tensor decompositions through algebraic extensions. For every positive epsilon it constructs correct division-free programs of cost at most C n^(9/4 + epsilon), with C uniform in the matrix size.

main_results.informal: For every field F, the infimum of admissible arithmetic matrix multiplication exponents is at most 9/4.

Over every field F and for every epsilon > 0, a positive constant C bounds the cost of a correct division-free straight-line program for n by n matrix multiplication by C n^(9/4 + epsilon) for every n >= 1.
The bound is realized by correct arithmetic programs at every positive matrix size, with a constant depending on the field and epsilon but not the size.
A rank-R decomposition over a finite extension E/P of degree m descends to a rank at most m^3 R decomposition over P.

projects.title: Improved asymptotic bounds for binary and spherical codes
projects.summary: Formalizes asymptotic coding bounds obtained from multilevel harmonic analysis, branching rules, and spectral decompositions. The development proves a binary-code exponent strictly below the MRRW rate, constructs a strict hierarchy of spherical-code bounds, and derives the published 0.39661 asymptotic kissing-number exponent. This import incorporates substantial proof and performance optimizations by Dean Cureton.

source.title: Ten Advances in Mathematics and Theoretical Computer Science

main_results.informal: For every relative distance strictly between zero and one half, the combined variational upper bound on the asymptotic binary-code rate is valid and is strictly smaller than the MRRW rate.
Every feasible finite interlacing certificate gives an eventual exponential upper bound for spherical codes, while the spherical-code rate is bounded by the closed hierarchy's variational rate.

At every angle parameter strictly between zero and one, successive levels of both the global and localized hierarchies improve strictly, with the localized hierarchy also strictly improving the row and classical bounds.
In all sufficiently large dimensions, the kissing number is at most 2 raised to 0.39661 times the dimension.

projects.title: Microwave network synthesis and power-of-two DFT implementation
projects.summary: Characterizes the complex transmission matrices synthesized from phase shifters and permutations, with or without hybrid couplers, using series and parallel composition. Phase-only networks are permuted phase-diagonal matrices; networks with hybrid couplers are products of permutation and phase-parametrized block-diagonal layers. Proves that the normalized DFT of every power-of-two size is implementable, with reusable finite-type reindexing, independent row and column permutations, and block-diagonal composition infrastructure. Uses the reciprocal matched network matrix model of the source paper; no general scattering-physics theorem is claimed.

source.title: Toward a Lean Formalization of Analog Computing with Microwaves

main_results.informal: A finite phase-only network is implementable exactly when its matrix is a permutation matrix times a diagonal matrix of complex phases.
main_results.source_ref: Upstream PhaseShifters.lean.

main_results.informal: A finite network is implementable with hybrid couplers and phase shifters exactly when its matrix is an initial permutation preceded by finitely many permutation and phase-parametrized block-diagonal layers.
main_results.source_ref: Theorem 1 and Section IV of arXiv:2610.04774.

main_results.informal: For every natural L, the normalized DFT matrix of size 2^L can be implemented by hybrid couplers, phase shifters, and permutation networks.
main_results.source_ref: Section V of arXiv:2610.04774.

projects.title: Minimum modulus for the unique multiset-sum problem
projects.summary: Formalizes the exact minimum modulus `N_min(n) = 2^n - 2^{floor(log_2 n)}` for the unique multiset-sum problem on the super-increasing residue set `{2^i - 1 : 0 <= i < n}`, and proves the sharp elementary-abelian-2-group lower bound `k >= n - 1` for unique multiset sums in `(Z/2Z)^k`.

source.title: Minimum modulus for the unique multiset-sum problem, with an application to computing the permanent

main_results.informal: Proves that among moduli `N >= 2` the least one making the super-increasing residue set `{2^i - 1 : 0 <= i < n}` valid for the unique multiset-sum problem is `2^n - 2^{floor(log_2 n)}`, for every `n >= 2` (stated as `IsLeast`).
Proves that if `g_0, ..., g_{n-1}` in `(Z/2Z)^k` have unique multiset sums, then `k >= n - 1`: an elementary abelian 2-group admitting such a family has order at least `2^(n - 1)`.

projects.title: BKLO simultaneous perfect matchings and spread matchings
projects.summary: Formalizes the r = 2 specialization of the simultaneous factor-selection step in BKLO Lemma 10.7: under quantitative parity, minimum-degree, codegree, and incidence hypotheses, a linearly sized, overlapping family of neighbourhood graphs admits perfect matchings whose edge sets are pairwise disjoint. The proof replaces the published randomized greedy process by a deterministic pessimistic-estimator sweep. Supporting results develop perfect, near-perfect, edge-disjoint, and quantitatively weighted spread matchings from sharp minimum-degree hypotheses.

source.title: Edge-decompositions of graphs with high minimum degree

main_results.informal: Specializes BKLO Lemma 10.7 to r = 2 in its apex-neighbourhood configuration: for every sufficiently large admissible configuration, all indexed neighbourhood graphs admit perfect matchings whose edge sets are pairwise disjoint. The proof is deterministic.
Every finite simple graph of even order whose minimum degree is at least half its order has a perfect matching.
Every finite simple graph of odd order n and minimum degree at least (n - 1) / 2 has a matching whose vertex set is the complement of a singleton.

If every vertex of a finite even vertex set has at least half the set size plus t neighbors inside the set, then the graph contains t + 1 pairwise edge-disjoint perfect matchings of that set, represented by an indexed family of partner involutions. These involutions are pairwise distinct when the vertex set is nonempty.

Under the same minimum-degree condition with slack t, every nonnegative edge-weight function admits a perfect matching whose weight is at most 1 / (t + 1) times the total weight over ordered pairs in the vertex set.

projects.title: Perfect multilinear local T(b) theorems
projects.summary: Proves the perfect multilinear local T(1) and T(b) theorems with interdependent testing families. Develops dyadic stopping times, pruning, outer-measure interpolation and Carleson embedding. Also proves a global variant for locally dyadic testing functions with scale-normalized weak boundedness and finite-Hardy-norm BMO testing.

source.title: A local T(b) theorem for perfect multilinear Calderón–Zygmund operators

main_results.informal: In positive dimension, a perfect multilinear Calderón–Zygmund form satisfying the local T(1) testing bound obeys a uniform Hölder bound on all dyadic test tuples, with a constant depending only on dimension, arity, exponents and testing bound.

In positive dimension, admissible collections of paths and testing functions satisfying the support, mean, norm, interdependence and local testing conditions imply the uniform Hölder bound, for every path length between one and the arity.

In positive dimension, locally dyadic, bounded pseudo-accretive testing functions satisfying scale-normalized weak boundedness and BMO testing on functions with integrable dyadic square function imply a uniform Hölder bound for the perfect form.
In positive dimension, dyadic martingale averages and differences satisfy outer Lp bounds for every finite exponent greater than one, with constants depending only on the dimension and exponent.

projects.title: Misere combinatorial games
projects.summary: Formalizes a combinatorial game theory library for misere play, including comparison modulo universes, p-free forms, outcome-stability, Property X, and concrete rulesets such as Hackenbush.

source.title: misere-games

main_results.informal: Shows that comparison modulo a universe is characterized by the maintenance-proviso test.
Proves that Property X makes the sum of two short p-free games p-free in an outcome-stable, hereditary, integer-invertible monoid.
Proves that universal closure gives a bijection from bounded end-like seeds to universes.

projects.title: Monlib4 Operator-Algebra and Quantum-Set Core
projects.summary: Formalizes monlib4's finite matrix-algebra inner-automorphism theorem, unitary inner automorphisms, star-preserving linear maps, the structural core of quantum sets, the core Schur-product definition of quantum graphs, and a self-contained digit-sum divisibility theorem.

main_results.informal: Shows that any automorphism of a finite nontrivial matrix algebra is implemented by an invertible intertwining matrix.
Packages matrix-algebra automorphisms as inner automorphisms induced by a linear equivalence of the underlying coordinate space.
Packages matrix-algebra automorphisms as conjugation by an element of `GL n 𝕜`.
Proves that automorphisms of finite matrix algebras preserve trace.
Defines the linear map induced by conjugation with a unitary matrix.
Proves that unitary inner automorphisms preserve matrix trace.
Proves that unitary inner automorphisms preserve the spectrum of the associated linear operator.
Defines star-preserving, or real, function-like maps.
Defines the star-conjugate involution on linear maps.
Defines the monlib4 quantum-set structure with modular automorphisms and a fixed orthonormal basis.
Instantiates the complex numbers as the base quantum set.
Defines the Schur product of linear maps using multiplication, tensoring, and coalgebra comultiplication.
Defines quantum graphs as Schur-idempotent endomorphisms.
Defines real quantum graphs as Schur-idempotent, star-preserving endomorphisms.
Proves that the value represented by digits in base `a + 1` has the same remainder modulo `a` as the sum of those digits.
Proves the generalized digit-sum divisibility criterion for base `a + 1` modulo `a`.

projects.title: Monsky's Theorem
projects.summary: Formalizes Monsky's theorem that a square can be dissected into n triangles of equal area if and only if n is nonzero and even, via a 2-adic valuation, a three-coloring of the unit square, and a rainbow-triangle argument.

source.title: On dividing a square into triangles

main_results.informal: Proves that the unit square admits a dissection into n equal-area triangles if and only if n is nonzero and even.

projects.title: Geometric Four-Colorings of the Moser Lattice and Ring
projects.summary: Formalizes the two explicit parity colorings from Dúcz's 2026 note on the Moser lattice. The development derives the exact quadratic norm formula, proves that the integer-coordinate embedding is faithful, proves both colorings proper and geometric on the entire lattice, and descends them through localization by powers of three to the Moser ring. As a structural corollary, every unit-distance graph realized entirely in the Moser ring is four-colorable. The uniqueness classification of geometric four-colorings and the chromatic number of the full Euclidean plane are not claimed.

source.title: A note on geometric colorings of the Moser lattice

main_results.informal: The two parity maps defined by Dúcz descend to proper four-colorings of the full Moser ring, and equality of colors for each map depends only on Euclidean distance.
main_results.source_ref: Theorem 3.1 and the Moser-ring extension following it.

main_results.informal: Every abstract graph with a realization in the Moser ring that sends each edge to a unit-distance pair is four-colorable.
main_results.source_ref: Corollary of the geometric four-coloring of the Moser ring.

projects.title: Optimality of Gerver's sofa
projects.summary: Formalizes Baek's solution of the moving sofa problem: Gerver's sofa attains the supremum of the areas of closed connected shapes that can move continuously around a right-angled corner in a unit-width hallway. Includes certified Gerver parameters, admissibility, convex cap geometry, Stieltjes curve area, Jordan separation, polygon approximation, and the concave quadratic upper bound.

source.title: Optimality of Gerver's Sofa

main_results.informal: The supremum, in extended nonnegative real numbers, of the areas of all admissible moving sofas equals the area of the explicitly defined Gerver sofa.
main_results.source_ref: Baek, Optimality of Gerver's Sofa, Theorem 1.1. Upstream Lean completion a0753860f1d2b4424e059c35e64ad611be71a415 (2026-09-20 10:55:24 UTC), announced 2026-09-20 18:42:40 UTC at https://x.com/deancureton/status/2101743865392926967. The imported commit has identical Lean sources; its later change is documentation only.

main_results.informal: Gerver's four defining equations have exactly one quadruple of parameters with A and B nonnegative and 0 ≤ φ ≤ θ ≤ π/4.
main_results.source_ref: Romik, Differential equations and exact solutions in the moving sofa problem, equations (1)-(4), arXiv:1606.08111. The GerverSofaLean v1.1.0 release archive (MIT, Dawid Trela) has SHA-256 7c496150f709ac709ae01f4836e9a702a18f752450efa69f15cf44264c0c2f77.

main_results.informal: Gerver's sofa is closed and connected and admits a continuous rigid motion from the horizontal arm to the vertical arm, starting at the identity and remaining within the unit-width hallway throughout.

projects.title: MRiscX
projects.summary: A Hoare logic for verifying unstructured RISC-V-like assembly in Lean, following Lundberg et al. (SEFM 2020), with a certified interpreter, proved structural Hoare rules, per-instruction specifications, custom elaborators and tactics, and a complete One-Time-Pad correctness proof.

main_results.informal: Defines the MRiscX Hoare triple, asserting that from any state satisfying the precondition the code reaches a successor state satisfying the postcondition while respecting the line whitelist and blacklist.
main_results.source_ref: D. Lundberg, R. Guanciale, A. Lindner, M. Dam, Hoare-Style Logic for Unstructured Programs, SEFM 2020, doi:10.1007/978-3-030-58768-0_11.

main_results.informal: Proves the sequencing Hoare rule, peeling off the last instruction of a code block.
main_results.source_ref: D. Lundberg, R. Guanciale, A. Lindner, M. Dam, Hoare-Style Logic for Unstructured Programs, SEFM 2020, doi:10.1007/978-3-030-58768-0_11.

main_results.informal: Proves the precondition-strengthening rule for MRiscX Hoare triples.
Proves the postcondition-weakening rule for MRiscX Hoare triples.
Proves the per-instruction Hoare specification of the load-immediate instruction.
Proves the full correctness of a One-Time-Pad implementation written in MRiscX assembly.

projects.title: Superexponential lower bounds for multicolor triangle Ramsey numbers
projects.summary: Resolves Erdős problem 183 by proving that the k-color triangle Ramsey number has a k-th root tending to infinity. The development constructs saturated palette families and recursive edge colorings, derives an explicit superexponential lower bound, and proves matching order-of-growth bounds for the logarithm of the Ramsey number.

source.title: Ten Advances in Mathematics and Theoretical Computer Science

main_results.informal: The k-th root of the k-color triangle Ramsey number tends to infinity, resolving Erdős problem 183.
For every k at least two, the k-color triangle Ramsey number is at least ((k^(1/3))/(6 exp(38) log k))^k, and its k-th root tends to infinity.
The logarithm of the k-color triangle Ramsey number has order k log k.

projects.title: Nagata's prime-generated factoriality theorem
projects.summary: Nagata’s factoriality criterion for noetherian domains localized at prime-generated multiplicative sets, with concrete and abstract localization interfaces and applications to polynomial rings through Laurent and fraction-field localizations.
authors: Ruy J. G. B. de Queiroz
projects.provenance_note: Inferred from explicit Copilot coauthor trailers in the pinned upstream history: 83.5% of surviving noncomment Lean code lines, including 94.8% of the core localization lemmas and 96.6% of the theorem module, trace to those commits. Commits 5b1698879b05fc76597723347544cb0b02c268c4 and ef73ee27e4b0a8d1260350801c6915bfb56b6658 add substantial new proofs, including prime-generated descent and the fraction-field polynomial application. Coauthorship records support this classification but do not identify who wrote each individual line.

main_results.informal: A noetherian integral domain is a unique factorization domain when localization at a prime-generated multiplicative set is a unique factorization domain.

projects.title: Nair–Tenenbaum short sums of arithmetic functions
projects.summary: Uniform upper bounds for arithmetic functions at polynomial values in short intervals, including prime arguments, arithmetic progressions, Hooley moments, smooth values and Goldbach upper bounds. Preserves the sieve, polynomial-root, number-field counting and lattice-discrepancy infrastructure. Includes a counterexample to the printed Lemma 1, replacement comparisons used by the main proofs, and the nonconstant-coordinate restriction for Corollary 6.

source.title: Short sums of certain arithmetic functions

main_results.informal: For an integer polynomial family of positive total degree with no fixed prime divisor, short sums of admissible nonnegative arithmetic functions satisfy the Nair–Tenenbaum sieve bound in its degree-dependent interval range. The height threshold is independent of the coefficients and discriminant; the bound constant depends on the restricted discriminant. Factorization data are constructed from the original family.

For any nonconstant irreducible integer polynomial Q and integer k greater than its degree, the greatest prime factor of the product of its values over (x, x + y], with y = x^(degree(Q)/k), eventually exceeds y times exp((log x)^alpha), for each alpha < 2 - log 4.

Under the same family and growth hypotheses, with nonzero constant term of the product polynomial, the corresponding bound holds at prime arguments. The constant-term correction is explicit and factorization data are constructed from the original family.
The smooth-weight tail estimate holds for general scalar class-M weights, with the stated cutoff, convergent series and uniform constant.

projects.title: Nash-Williams–Tutte tree packing and arboricity
projects.summary: A finite simple graph on a nonempty vertex type has k edge-disjoint spanning trees exactly when every partition into m nonempty parts has at least k(m − 1) crossing edges. The development also proves the Nash-Williams characterization of covering the edges by k forests, and that every finite nonempty 2k-edge-connected simple graph has k edge-disjoint spanning trees. It preserves the general forest exchange lemma and supporting reachability and edge-counting infrastructure, using Mathlib's graph definitions.

source.title: Edge-disjoint spanning trees of finite graphs

main_results.informal: A finite simple graph on a nonempty vertex type has k pairwise edge-disjoint spanning trees if and only if every vertex partition into m nonempty parts has at least k(m − 1) crossing edges.
A finite simple graph is the union of k forests if and only if every nonempty finite vertex set S induces at most k(|S| − 1) edges.
Every finite simple graph on a nonempty vertex type that remains connected after deletion of fewer than 2k edges has k pairwise edge-disjoint spanning trees.

Every finite simple graph G contains k pairwise edge-disjoint forests and a subgraph H such that intersecting each forest with H preserves the connected components of H, and the forests cover every edge of G outside H.

projects.title: Nash-Williams fronts and 2-better-quasi-orders
projects.summary: Formalizes Nash-Williams fronts through their well-founded prefix trees and ordinal ranks, proves the finite-color Nash-Williams theorem, and derives the infinite Ramsey theorem for arbitrary finite arity. The order-theoretic development proves that 2-better-quasi-orders are well-quasi-orders and establishes closure under finite products, lexicographic sums, domination of subsets, and pointwise embedding of sequences. Throughout, TwoBQO r is the good-triple property of an arbitrary binary relation r (every pair-sequence has m < n < l with f(m,n) related to f(n,l)); it assumes no reflexivity or transitivity of r.

source.title: Towards better: A motivated introduction to better-quasi-orders

main_results.informal: Every two-coloring of a Nash-Williams front on an infinite set has an infinite restriction whose front is monochromatic.
Every finite coloring of a Nash-Williams front has an infinite restriction whose front is monochromatic.
Every finite coloring of the r-element subsets of an infinite set of natural numbers is constant on all r-element subsets of some infinite subset.
Every 2-better-quasi-order is a well-quasi-order.

The 2-BQO good-triple property is preserved by lexicographic sums: if the index relation and every fibre relation have it, so does the lexicographic-sum relation on the sigma type. This asserts nothing about reflexivity or transitivity of the sum; those are proved separately (LexSumRelQO.refl and LexSumRelQO.trans) under the corresponding order hypotheses on the index and fibres.
If a preorder is a 2-better-quasi-order, then its infinite sequences are well-quasi-ordered by the relation admitting a strictly monotone reindexing along which corresponding terms are related.

projects.title: Nash's smooth isometric embedding theorem
projects.summary: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Nash's C^∞ isometric embedding theorem for closed manifolds: every compact smooth manifold without boundary, equipped with a smooth Riemannian metric, admits a smooth injective map into some Euclidean space ℝ^q whose differential pulls the Euclidean inner product back to the given metric. The proof formalized is Günther's (1989), which replaces the Nash-Moser iteration by an elliptic fixed-point argument, following the presentation in A. J. Wassermann's Cambridge Part III lecture notes as the primary source. The development has two layers. The first proves the theorem for the flat torus: a self-contained Sobolev toolkit on 𝕋ⁿ (weighted ℓ² Sobolev spaces on ℤⁿ, Rellich compactness, the Sobolev sup bound, three multiplication theorems, mollifiers, periodization, Fourier inversion and Parseval), the approximation of smooth metrics by realizable ones, Günther's perturbation theorem proved by a contraction in Hˢ, and their assembly into the statement that every smooth 2π-periodic positive-definite matrix field on ℝⁿ is the pullback metric of a smooth periodic immersion that is injective modulo 2πℤⁿ. The second layer reduces the closed-manifold case to the torus: a Whitney embedding from Mathlib is extended to the ambient space, the metric is extended by a pseudo-inverse construction, cut off, symmetrized and periodized, and the torus theorem is applied. No bound on the embedding dimension is claimed. Concrete instances (round spheres of every dimension, products of spheres, the flat torus 𝕊¹ × 𝕊¹) are derived, and the flat-torus instance is shown to reproduce the torus theorem's conclusion, tying the two layers together. Nothing here is claimed to be new.

main_results.informal: Every compact smooth boundaryless manifold with a smooth Riemannian metric admits a smooth isometric embedding in some finite-dimensional Euclidean space.

projects.title: Square-difference-free polynomials beyond Naslund's conjectured bound
projects.summary: Constructs square-difference-free subsets of polynomials over the field with three elements that refute Naslund's Conjecture 13 at every degree bound divisible by four and at least eight. An explicit degree-eight lift multiplies cardinality by 810 and yields a lower bound of 16/21 for the lower limiting normalized logarithmic growth rate.

source.title: Square-difference-free sets in F_3[T] past the conjectured bound

main_results.informal: There is a square-difference-free set of 810 polynomials over F_3 with degree less than eight.
The upper bound 3^6 = 729 in Naslund's Conjecture 13 fails for square differences over F_3 at degree bound eight.
For every positive integer e, there is a square-difference-free set of 810^e polynomials over F_3 with degree less than 8e.
For every natural number e, there is a square-difference-free set of 27 times 810^e polynomials over F_3 with degree less than 8e + 4.
For every n divisible by four with n at least eight, there is a square-difference-free set of polynomials over F_3 of degree less than n whose cardinality exceeds 3^(3n/4).
If D(n) is the largest cardinality of a square-difference-free set of polynomials over F_3 of degree less than n, then the lower limit of log D(n) divided by n log 3 is at least 16/21.

projects.title: Finite-time breakdown for Navier–Stokes and Euler
projects.summary: Formalizes forced three-dimensional Navier–Stokes breakdown on Euclidean space and the periodic torus for every positive viscosity, and finite-time singularity formation for unforced Euler from smooth, compactly supported, divergence-free initial data. The Euler result specifies maximal Sobolev lifespan, divergence of the velocity C¹ norm, and divergence of the time integral of the vorticity norm.

source.title: Finite time blowup for Navier–Stokes and Finite time blowup for the Euler equation

main_results.informal: For every positive viscosity, there are smooth divergence-free initial data and smooth forcing on ℝ³, with the prescribed spatial and temporal decay, admitting no global smooth Navier–Stokes solution with uniformly bounded kinetic energy.

For every positive viscosity, there are smooth periodic divergence-free initial data and smooth periodic forcing with the prescribed temporal decay, admitting no global smooth periodic Navier–Stokes solution.

There exist smooth divergence-free initial data on ℝ³ whose spatial derivatives decay faster than every polynomial and which admit no global smooth unforced Euler solution with uniformly bounded kinetic energy.

There exist nonzero smooth compactly supported divergence-free initial data, a maximal time 0 < Tstar ≤ 1, and an unforced Euler solution on [0, Tstar) in the all-order Sobolev class with bounded kinetic energy. Smooth Sobolev solutions on [0, T] exist exactly when T < Tstar. The velocity C¹ norm has infinite left limsup at Tstar, and the time integral of the spatial supremum of the vorticity norm diverges.

projects.title: Nemytskii operators on Lebesgue spaces
projects.summary: Develops superposition operators induced by Caratheodory functions: measurability, Lp-to-Lq growth bounds and sequential continuity, Lipschitz estimates, monotonicity and coercivity, and Frechet remainder estimates. For Lebesgue measure on the real line and finite-dimensional real fibers, characterizes when every Lp input has an Lq output by the standard integrable-envelope growth condition, for 1 <= p,q < infinity. First-order remainder estimates on arbitrary measure spaces assume a Caratheodory derivative with the stated Holder-compatible growth. The integral-functional result bounds the integrated remainder and proves integrability of the linearized integrand; it does not assert integrability of the original integrand without its separate growth hypotheses. Caratheodory here requires strongly measurable sections and almost-everywhere continuity in the fiber variable.

source.title: Nemytskii operators on Lebesgue spaces

projects.provenance_note: Upstream credits the four listed authors. Its README and available commit history contain no AI disclosure; this is evidence under the repository's human-provenance rubric, not proof of tool non-use. The imported version includes substantial AI-assisted Mathlib porting and proof refactoring by OpenAI Codex, so it is recorded as mixed.

main_results.informal: For f from R times R^m to R^k with strongly measurable sections and almost-everywhere continuous fibers, and 1 <= p,q < infinity, every Lp input gives an Lq output if and only if there exist an Lq real envelope a and a nonnegative constant C such that almost everywhere, simultaneously for every fiber vector xi, norm(f(x,xi)) <= abs(a(x)) + C * norm(xi)^(p/q).
main_results.source_ref: Upstream NemytskiiLebesgue/ConverseImplication.lean.

main_results.informal: On any measure space, the same Caratheodory and growth assumptions imply that a sequence of Lp functions converging in Lp to an Lp function has superposition images converging in Lq, for finite exponents p,q at least one and finite-dimensional real fibers.
main_results.source_ref: Upstream NemytskiiLebesgue/Continuity.lean.

main_results.informal: On a measure space, suppose f and its fiber derivative f' are Caratheodory, f' is the Frechet derivative at every fiber point almost everywhere, p,r >= 1 satisfy 1/q = 1/r + 1/p, and f' is bounded by b + C * norm(xi)^(p/r) with nonnegative b in Lr and C > 0. At each Lp function u, the Lq integral quantity (a quasi-norm when q < 1) of the first-order remainder is at most epsilon times the Lp norm of l whenever l is in Lp and its Lp norm is sufficiently small.
main_results.source_ref: Upstream NemytskiiLebesgue/Frechet.lean; generalized in this port by removing an unused finite-measure assumption.

main_results.informal: On a measure space with finite-dimensional real inputs, under Caratheodory assumptions on f and its fiber derivative f', conjugate exponents p,q, and derivative growth b + C*norm(xi)^(p-1) with nonnegative b in Lq and C > 0, the linearized integrand is integrable for every Lp perturbation. The norm of the integral of the first-order remainder is at most epsilon times the Lp norm of the perturbation when that norm is sufficiently small.
main_results.source_ref: Upstream NemytskiiLebesgue/IntegralFunctional.lean; generalized in this port by removing an unused finite-measure assumption.

projects.title: Neukirch's Algebraic Number Theory: Hilbert ramification theory
projects.summary: Formalizes Hilbert's ramification theory for Galois extensions of number fields, including the fundamental identity and the decomposition and inertia groups, ported from the jjdishere/neukirch project.

main_results.informal: Proves the fundamental identity g·e·f = [L : K] for a Galois extension of number fields.
Shows that when P is the unique prime over p, the degree [L : K] equals the ramification index times the inertia degree.
Proves the Galois group acts transitively on the primes lying over a fixed prime.
Computes the order of the decomposition group as the product of the ramification index and inertia degree.
Identifies the Galois group of the inertia field over K with the Galois group of the residue field extension.
Computes the order of the inertia group as the ramification index of p in L.
Proves multiplicativity of the ramification index in a tower of Dedekind domains.
Proves multiplicativity of the inertia degree in a tower of Dedekind domains.

projects.title: New Foundations refutes the Weak Partition Principle
projects.summary: Constructs a formal first-order derivation of the negation of the Weak Partition Principle from New Foundations, with extensionality and the full integer-stratified comprehension schema. Proves full deductive equivalence with Metamath's Hailperin-derived finite presentation, including its added singleton axiom. Replays the source proof through nominal syntax, explicit freshness certificates, and a de Bruijn calculus. Includes reusable first-order soundness and completeness, stratification, lowering, and proof-translation infrastructure. This is a derivability theorem; it does not assert the consistency of New Foundations.

source.title: NF proves not-WPP, source-complete Lean formalization

main_results.informal: Standard New Foundations formally derives the negation of WPP. WPP says that, for all sets x and y, if a function maps y onto x and an injective function maps y into x, then an injective function maps x into y.
main_results.source_ref: Upstream Proof/NFStandard/NotWPP.lean and the exact source formulation documented in README.md at the pinned commit. main_results.informal: Extensionality together with every integer-stratified comprehension instance and Metamath's Hailperin-derived finite first-order presentation, including its added singleton axiom, derive exactly the same sentences.
main_results.source_ref: Upstream Proof/NFStandard/Equivalence.lean at the pinned commit. Metamath's ax-sn entry credits the singleton addition to SF on 2015-01-12 and distinguishes it from Hailperin's original presentation: https://us.metamath.org/nfeuni/ax-sn.html.

projects.title: The sharp finite-field Nikodym exponent
projects.summary: Proves a lower bound for Nikodym sets over arbitrary finite fields and a matching exponent upper construction over sufficiently large prime fields, using interpolation, algebraic degree bounds, and multiquadratic constructions.

main_results.informal: Every Nikodym set in dimension d ≥ 2 over a finite field of size q has size at least q^d − (8d²+1)q^(d−2^(1−d)).
For every positive ε and dimension d ≥ 2, sufficiently large prime fields admit a Nikodym set of size at most q^d − q^(d−2^(1−d)−ε).

projects.title: Nivat's conjecture
projects.summary: Formalizes the proof of Nivat's conjecture found by GPT-6 Pro. A configuration on the integer lattice over a finite alphabet whose number of distinct patterns on some m-by-n rectangle is at most m times n has a nonzero period. Develops rational alphabet labelings, the Laurent-polynomial shift action and its annihilator ideals, the exact line ideal of a half-plane-supported difference of orbit-closure points, complexity descent to a smaller rectangle, and Szabados's two-factor theorem for finite-range configurations.

source.title: Pattern complexity and Nivat's conjecture
source.notes: The proof and manuscript were produced by GPT-6 Pro and the Lean development by GPT-6 Astra in Codex, both prompted and directed by Boon Suan Ho, who claims no human mathematical authorship. The manuscript ships in the upstream repository as paper/nivat.tex. The Lean sources are identical to the commit archived by Palomar on 2026-09-14 (0d94547e); later upstream commits only touched the README and the paper's abstract. No human expert review is claimed upstream; Bryna Kra's guest post on Terence Tao's blog (2026-09-13) discusses the arrival of AI proofs of the conjecture. The upstream MIT copyright and permission notice is retained in every imported file.

main_results.informal: For every finite alphabet A and configuration c from the integer lattice to A, if for some positive m and n the number of distinct patterns of c on the m-by-n rectangle, counted over all integer translations, is at most m times n, then there is a nonzero lattice vector h with c(z + h) = c(z) for every z.

The same statement written with Mathlib vocabulary only, as registered with Palomar. The pattern set is the range of the restriction of translates of c to the product of the integer intervals [0, m) and [0, n), its natural cardinality is at most m times n, and the conclusion is a lattice vector h different from (0, 0) with c(z + h) = c(z) for all z.

A finite-range rational-valued configuration whose pattern count on some m-by-n rectangle with m, n positive is at most m times n is periodic. This is proved by strong induction on the area of the rectangle.

If a finite-range rational configuration has pattern count at most m times n on an m-by-n rectangle with m, n positive and is annihilated by the product of two difference operators in nonzero directions h and t, then it is periodic.

If two pointwise limits x and y of translates of a finite-range rational configuration c have nonzero difference whose Laurent annihilator ideal is generated by a nonzero polynomial, and c has pattern count at most m times n on an m-by-n rectangle, then applying that polynomial to c yields a configuration with pattern count at most its area on some rectangle of strictly smaller positive area.

A nonzero rational configuration that vanishes on the open lower half-plane of a lattice basis and is periodic with positive period q along the first basis direction has Laurent annihilator ideal generated by a single line-supported polynomial, obtained from a monic divisor of X^q - 1 of positive degree.

projects.title: Existence of a finitely presented non-sofic group
projects.summary: Constructs a finitely presented group that is not sofic, resolving the question whether every group admits arbitrarily accurate finite permutation approximations. The development combines an explicit elementary group with property T, a finite-table construction of a finitely presented group, finite-model expansion, and a local obstruction to sofic approximation.

source.title: Ten Advances in Mathematics and Theoretical Computer Science

main_results.informal: There exists a group admitting a finite presentation but no sofic approximation.

projects.title: Equal-area and equal-perimeter convex partitions
projects.summary: Formalizes the Akopyan–Avvakumov–Karasev theorem that every planar convex body can be partitioned into any prescribed positive number of convex pieces with equal area and equal perimeter. Area is Lebesgue measure and perimeter is Hausdorff measure of the boundary.

main_results.informal: Every compact convex planar set with nonempty interior admits a convex partition into any positive number of pieces whose areas and perimeters are all equal.

projects.title: Exact odd-prime distributions of central-binomial valuations
projects.summary: Formalizes the exact distribution of the p-adic valuation of the central binomial coefficient binom(2n,n) over every complete block 0 <= n < p^k for every odd prime p. The development proves Kummer correctness for padded digit words, constructs the two-state doubling carry enumerator, identifies it with the arithmetic valuation polynomial, derives its second-order recurrence, proves the rational bivariate generating function, and obtains closed formulas for valuations zero and one.

source.title: Über die Ergänzungssätze zu den allgemeinen Reciprocitätsgesetzen

main_results.informal: For every odd prime p = 2h+1, proves the denominator-cleared identity for the bivariate series whose coefficient of T^k X^r counts n < p^k with nu_p(binomial(2n,n)) = r; equivalently the series is (1-XT)/(1-(h+1)(1+X)T+pXT^2).
main_results.source_ref: A. Straub, V. H. Moll, T. Amdeberhan, The p-adic valuation of k-central binomial coefficients, Acta Arith. 140 (2009), 31-42.

main_results.informal: Proves that the exact valuation polynomials satisfy F_{k+2}(X)+pX F_k(X)=(h+1)(1+X)F_{k+1}(X), with F_0=1 and F_1=(h+1)+hX.
Proves Kummer correctness for every valid padded base-p word: the p-adic valuation of its central binomial coefficient equals the number of carries produced by doubling the word.
Gives a closed formula for the number of n below p^(k+2) whose central binomial coefficient has p-adic valuation exactly one.

projects.title: Poitou's Explicit Odlyzko Bound for Root Discriminants
projects.summary: Formalizes the unconditional explicit-formula argument for a lower bound on root discriminants of totally complex number fields. Develops the completed Dedekind zeta function and its functional equation, Poitou's explicit formula, the Tartar test function, and a certified numerical estimate proving that degree at least 18 forces root discriminant at least 8.25.

source.title: Sur les petits discriminants

main_results.informal: Proves that every totally complex number field of degree at least 18 has absolute discriminant at least 8.25 raised to its degree.
main_results.source_ref: Georges Poitou, Sur les petits discriminants, equation (26) and the table on p. 17; Lean source adapted from ImperialCollegeLondon/FLT commit 01370b013e55c83f1994af814cd31cb8fb2ef653.

projects.title: Order closure, order adherence and Fatou norms
projects.summary: Formalizes order and unbounded-order adherence in vector lattices, the Gao-Leung characterization of order-continuous norms on sigma-order-complete Banach lattices, and the Solovay/Stone-space construction of order-complete C(K) spaces with arbitrarily large density and norm-closed separable sublattices whose only order-closed vector-sublattice extension is the whole C(K) space. Constructs solid sets with a prescribed infinite number kappa of solid generators whose adherence towers are strict below any ordinal at most kappa's successor cardinal. Constructs a complete weakly Fatou lattice norm with constant 2 that is not equivalent to any Fatou lattice norm. Includes reusable vector-lattice, net-convergence, sublattice, seminorm, Boolean-algebra and transfinite-iteration infrastructure.

source.title: Order closure, order adherence and Fatou norms

main_results.informal: For a sigma-order-complete Banach lattice X, the following are equivalent: every vector sublattice has order-closed order adherence; every vector sublattice has equal order and unbounded-order adherence; and the norm of X is order continuous.
main_results.source_ref: Paper Theorem 1.1, recalling Gao-Leung Theorem 2.7.

main_results.informal: For every cardinal kappa there is a compact Hausdorff space K such that C(K, R) is order complete and has density at least kappa, with a norm-closed separable vector sublattice Y whose only order-closed vector-sublattice extension is all of C(K, R).
main_results.source_ref: Paper Proposition 2.1, via the Solovay Boolean algebra.

main_results.informal: For every infinite cardinal kappa and ordinal xi at most the initial ordinal of kappa's successor cardinal, there is a vector lattice and a solid set with solid generator number kappa whose order-adherence tower has a proper step at every stage below xi. The witness and cardinal/ordinal parameters are lifted one universe in Lean.
main_results.source_ref: Paper Theorem 2.6, with its explicit infinite-cardinal hypothesis. Lean strengthens the stated size-kappa generating-set conclusion to minimum solid generator number exactly kappa; this exact-minimum conclusion is proved in the formalization, not stated in the paper.

main_results.informal: There is a real vector lattice with a complete lattice norm p satisfying the weak Fatou property with constant 2, such that no lattice norm q with the Fatou property is equivalent to p. Norms, completeness and equivalence are represented explicitly by PaperLatticeNorm, IsCompleteFor and EquivalentNorms.
main_results.source_ref: Paper Theorem 3.1; self-contained construction of the result previously announced by Anthony Wickstead and credited to Michael Elliott. The paper credits Jaume de Dios Pont for an earlier Lean formalization of this result.

projects.title: Classification of groups of order p * q
projects.summary: Classification of noncyclic finite groups of order p*q, including the prime-square direct-product case and the p<q semidirect-product normal form.

main_results.informal: There exists a noncyclic group of order p*q exactly when p=q, p divides q-1, or q divides p-1.
Any two noncyclic groups of order p*q are isomorphic.
If p<q, every group of order p*q is isomorphic to a semidirect product of MulZMod q by MulZMod p.

projects.title: Osterwalder-Schrader Axioms for the Gaussian Free Field
projects.summary: Formalizes Osterwalder-Schrader axioms for the massive Gaussian free field using Minlos, covariance, and reflection-positivity infrastructure.

main_results.informal: Proves that the massive Gaussian free field satisfies the OS0-OS4 Osterwalder-Schrader axioms.

projects.title: Clique trees, subtree representations and chordal treewidth
projects.summary: Develops rooted clique forests with the running-intersection property, constructs them from perfect elimination orders of finite chordal graphs, characterizes chordality by their existence, and obtains maximal-clique, separator, and counting results. Also characterizes chordality under retained-clique gluing of induced pieces, with exact vertex and edge inclusion-exclusion identities. The original library was extracted as a reusable byproduct of the published Paper IV formalization of the chordal-graph case of Erdős problem #81; this library is not by itself a proof of that paper's partition bound. Gavril's characterization supplies exact finite-tree subtree representations and the converse to chordality. Finite subtree Helly places every finite clique in a bag of any tree decomposition and gives optimal chordal treewidth. The supplied representation includes an empty connector; no minimal-host or runtime bound is claimed.

source.title: Clique partitions with rooted simplicial defect: quantitative stability and sharp eventual bounds

main_results.informal: Every finite chordal graph admits a perfect elimination order.
A finite graph is chordal if and only if it has a rooted clique tree.
A nonempty finite chordal graph has a clique tree whose distinct bags are precisely its maximal cliques, with no more bags than vertices.
In a clique tree, each minimal separator of two reachable vertices is the intersection of two adjacent bags.
The total bag size minus the total parent-child bag intersection size equals the number of graph vertices.

A finite rooted clique forest gives nonempty connected vertex sets of a finite host tree, with adjacency of distinct source vertices exactly equivalent to intersection of their assigned sets. Empty and disconnected source graphs are supported through one empty connector node.
main_results.source_ref: Gavril, JCT B 16 (1974), 47–56, doi:10.1016/0095-8956(74)90094-X; constructor using the PR 579 adapter.

main_results.informal: A finite graph on a vertex type in Type is chordal if and only if it has an exact representation by nonempty connected vertex sets of a finite tree.
A finite pairwise-intersecting family of nonempty connected vertex sets of a finite tree has a common vertex; the empty family is also allowed.
Every finite clique is contained in one bag of any tree decomposition.
For every finite nonempty chordal graph on a vertex type in Type, its natural treewidth plus one equals its clique number.
A finite nonempty chordal graph admits a tree decomposition whose width plus one is its clique number.
If two induced pieces cover a finite graph, their overlap is a clique, and no edge joins their exclusive parts, the graph is chordal exactly when both pieces are chordal. Overlap edges are retained.
main_results.source_ref: New Lean Pool extension proved here using the existing Dirac and simplicial-elimination interfaces; not a claim from the frozen paper.

main_results.informal: The vertex count of the graph plus the overlap size equals the sum of the vertex counts of the two covering pieces.
main_results.source_ref: New Lean Pool extension; finite-set inclusion-exclusion.

main_results.informal: The graph edge count plus the number of pairs in the retained clique overlap equals the sum of the induced pieces' edge counts.
main_results.source_ref: New Lean Pool extension; induced-edge inclusion-exclusion.

projects.title: Independence of Playfair's axiom via Euclidean and Klein models
projects.summary: Constructs Euclidean and Klein models of a synthetic Hilbert plane, proving that Playfair's axiom is independent of incidence, Pasch order, and congruence axioms, even with Archimedes and Dedekind continuity. Develops reusable coordinate geometry over ordered fields, projective motions, Klein angles and metric, smooth-path length and distance, congruence constructions, and a coordinate curvature calculation. Dedekind continuity replaces Hilbert's maximal completeness axiom; their equivalence is not formalized. Curvature uses Brioschi's formula, and distance uses C1 paths; no identification with Mathlib's Riemannian distance or connection curvature is asserted.

source.title: ParallelPostulate formalization by Richard Sutton

main_results.informal: There exists a Hilbert plane satisfying Archimedes and Dedekind continuity and Playfair's axiom, and there exists another satisfying the same continuity axioms and the negation of Playfair's axiom. The models use real coordinate planes with bounds zero and minus one.
main_results.source_ref: Upstream Hilbert/Independence.lean. First publicly announced 2026-09-30 01:08:53 UTC at https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/583339-AI-authored-projects/topic/Independence.20Parallel.20Postulate/near/627942879. The author's follow-up discloses mostly AI-written proofs. Pasch order and Dedekind continuity are the stated variants; equivalence to plane separation and maximal completeness is not proved.

main_results.informal: Over any linearly ordered field, for every negative bound and every line in the bounded coordinate plane, infinitely many distinct lines pass through any point of the plane outside that line without meeting it.

For every negative real bound and every pair of points in its plane, the infimum of C1-path lengths in Klein's coordinate metric equals arsinh of the square root of minus the bound times apart, divided by the square root of minus the bound.
For every real bound, Brioschi's coordinate curvature formula applied to the three coefficients of Klein's metric equals that bound at every point of its coordinate plane.

projects.title: Parameter-Free Gradient Minimization in l_p Geometry
projects.summary: Exact value-gradient query-complexity results for convex differentiable objectives on finite-dimensional real l_p spaces with attained minima and a positive global primal-to-dual Lipschitz-gradient bound. For finite real p > 1, the development proves strict-local scale-identification impossibility at LR/epsilon = 4 and a deterministic method family with three post-secant-initialization query-rate regimes. For p > 2 it also proves deterministic known-parameter upper and lower query exponents p/(p+2), with explicit horizon and dimension restrictions on the lower bound.

main_results.informal: For finite real p > 1 and positive epsilon, measurable strict-local exact value-gradient methods satisfy scale-identification lower bounds on convex smooth one-dimensional objectives with unique minimizers, even at LR/epsilon = 4. The result includes deterministic and randomized finite-horizon statements and infinite worst-case expected queried-or-returned hitting time.

For finite real p > 2 and convex differentiable objectives with attained minima and a positive global primal-to-dual Lipschitz-gradient bound, deterministic known-parameter exact value-gradient methods have upper query exponent p/(p+2). The matching lower exponent concerns the first T queries, requires d >= 2 and 1 <= T <= d, and retains the explicit min(p, log d) dependence.

For convex differentiable objectives with attained minima and positive global L-Lipschitz gradients from l_p to its dual, one deterministic family works for every finite real p > 1 and positive epsilon after supplied nondegenerate secant initialization with 0 < M0 <= L. It returns a queried point with dual gradient norm at most epsilon. Writing R for distance to the minimizer set, the post-initialization oracle-call bound has polynomial dependence on max(1, LR/epsilon) with exponent 1/2 for 1 < p < 2 and p = 2, and p/(p+2) for p > 2, plus additive log(e + L/M0) calibration cost. Constants depend only on p, with a universal constant at p = 2; discovering the secant pair is outside the count.

projects.title: Partial Combinatory Algebras
projects.summary: Formalises partial combinatory algebras with the K/S combinators, programming combinators, the free combinatory algebra, and the graph model.

source.title: Realizability: An Introduction to its Categorical Side

main_results.informal: Defines the class of partial combinatory algebras (PCAs) with K and S combinators.
Defines total combinatory algebras and exhibits every total combinatory algebra as a PCA.
Constructs the free total combinatory algebra as a quotient of formal expressions.
Constructs the graph-model combinatory algebra on the powerset of any Listing-typed carrier.

projects.title: Almost all primes are partially regular
projects.summary: Formalizes an asymptotic theorem about partial regularity of primes via Bernoulli-number irregularity.

main_results.informal: Proves the asymptotic big-O bound behind the partial-regularity theorem.

projects.title: PCF Theory
projects.summary: Formalizes foundational results from Shelah's Possible Cofinality theory, including the existence of club-guessing sequences.
