main_results.informal: Proves the existence of a club-guessing sequence on a stationary set whose elements share a common uncountable cofinality bounded by the cofinality of the ambient ordinal.

projects.title: Craig interpolation and Beth definability for propositional dynamic logic
projects.summary: Proves Craig interpolation for full propositional dynamic logic, including tests and Kleene star, by constructing interpolants from uniform cyclic tableaux. Interpolants use only atomic propositions and atomic programs common to the two formulas. The development also proves the local Beth definability property for a propositional letter, and supplies reusable syntax, Kripke semantics, Fischer-Ladner closure, tableau soundness and completeness, finite reachability and game-theoretic infrastructure. The results assert existence; no executable extraction algorithm or complexity bound is claimed. Human contributors and Aristotle jointly developed the formalization. The completeness modules reuse the finite game determinacy theorem already pooled in `LeanPool.Lean4GlCoalgebras` instead of duplicating it.

source.title: Propositional Dynamic Logic has Craig Interpolation: a tableau-based proof

main_results.informal: If the implication from PDL formula phi to psi is valid in every Kripke model, there exists a PDL formula theta whose atomic proposition and program vocabulary is contained in the intersection of theirs, such that phi implies theta and theta implies psi in every model.

If a PDL formula phi implicitly determines a propositional letter p (all two-letter substitutions agree wherever both substituted formulas hold), there is a formula psi using only phi's vocabulary other than p such that phi entails that p is equivalent to psi.
A free sequent is tableau-consistent if and only if it is satisfiable in a Kripke model.

projects.title: Optimal Pebbling Number of the Hypercube
projects.summary: Formalizes that the optimal pebbling number of the n-dimensional hypercube Q_n is Theta((4/3)^n).  Builds a weight-function lower bound of (4/3)^n and a probabilistic recursive upper bound C * (4/3)^n with an explicit constant, combining them into a two-sided big-Theta witness.

source.title: Optimal pebbling number of the hypercube

main_results.informal: The optimal pebbling number of Q_n has order (4/3)^n: there is a positive constant C with (4/3)^n <= o(Q_n) <= C * (4/3)^n for all n.
The optimal pebbling number of Q_n is at least (4/3)^n, proved by a weight-function argument summing one-pebble weights over the cube.
The optimal pebbling number of Q_n is at most C * (4/3)^n for an explicit constant C, via a probabilistic recursive splitting construction.

projects.title: Euler's pentagonal number theorem, two independent proofs, and the Jacobi triple product
projects.summary: Two independent proofs of Euler's pentagonal number theorem that share no lemmas, so each confirms the result on its own. The primary development is combinatorial: Franklin's sign-reversing involution on partitions into distinct parts, giving p_e(n) - p_o(n) = (-1)^|k| when n is the generalized pentagonal number k(3k-1)/2 and 0 otherwise, stated under a single integer index, together with the identification of that signed count with the coefficient of X^n in the truncated product over ℤ⟦X⟧. It builds on Mathlib's Nat.Partition.genFun. The second route develops q-Pochhammer symbols, the Gaussian binomial coefficient, Euler's two identities and the Cauchy identity, proves the Jacobi triple product both as a formal power series identity in (LaurentPolynomial ℂ)⟦X⟧ and analytically over ℂ for ‖q‖ < 1, and reaches the same theorem for the infinite product by specialization. The Lean proofs in both routes were largely generated by Aristotle; the Franklin route additionally has an author-written blueprint that the formalization follows lemma by lemma, and carries substantially more manual intervention and review, whereas the q-series route is machine-generated blueprint and all. The Franklin route and the analytic pentagonal number theorem overlap the pooled `pentagonal-number-theorem` development, which states its analytic form over RCLike fields rather than only over the complex numbers; the q-Pochhammer, Gaussian binomial and Euler identity definitions overlap arXiv:2607.01544. The project's distinct contribution is the complex-analytic layer: an analytic Jacobi triple product over the complex numbers for norm q < 1, its extension to the punctured disc, the analytic Cauchy identity, and the summability and locally-uniform-convergence machinery they require. Neither the pooled entry nor the non-archimedean development of arXiv:2607.01544 covers that setting.

source.title: Pentagonal Number Theorem

main_results.informal: The primary result. For every n, either n is a generalized pentagonal number k(3k-1)/2 for some integer k, in which case the number of partitions of n into an even number of distinct parts exceeds the number with an odd number of distinct parts by exactly (-1)^|k|; or n is not of that form, in which case the two counts are equal. Proved by Franklin's sign-reversing involution.

The coefficient of X^n in the truncated product ∏_{k=1}^{n}(1 - X^k) over ℤ⟦X⟧ equals p_e(n) - p_o(n), the signed count of partitions of n into distinct parts. Truncating at n is harmless because the omitted factors are ≡ 1 mod X^{n+1}.
For ‖q‖ < 1, ‖z‖ < 1 and z ≠ 0, the product (q;q)_∞ (-z;q)_∞ (-q/z;q)_∞ equals the bilateral theta series ∑_{k ∈ ℤ} z^k q^{k(k-1)/2}.

For ‖q‖ < 1, the infinite product (q;q)_∞ equals ∑_{k ∈ ℤ} (-1)^k q^{ω(k)} over the generalized pentagonal numbers ω(k) = k(3k-1)/2, written as two one-sided sums. Obtained from the Jacobi triple product by specialization.

The Jacobi triple product as an identity of formal power series in (LaurentPolynomial ℂ)-coefficient power series, with no convergence hypothesis: the product of q-Pochhammer symbols equals the bilateral theta series coefficientwise.

projects.title: Euler's pentagonal number theorem
projects.summary: Formalizes Euler's pentagonal number theorem as a generating-function identity for power series and for real/complex numbers, with a partition-recurrence corollary and a self-contained Franklin-style combinatorial proof.

main_results.informal: Proves Euler's pentagonal number theorem as a formal power series identity ∏(1-xⁿ) = Σ(-1)ᵏ x^(k(3k-1)/2).
Proves the analytic version of the pentagonal number theorem for real or complex numbers of norm less than one.
Derives Euler's pentagonal recurrence for the partition function from the pentagonal number theorem.

projects.title: Quartic-over-logarithmic lower bound for rational permanent formulas
projects.summary: Proves that every valid rational arithmetic formula over the complex numbers computing the n-by-n permanent, for n at least 32, has at least n^4 / (192 log_2 n) variable leaves. The development derives the bound through coefficient-field transcendence degree, Jacobian minors, matching-polynomial identities, and a cyclic block decomposition.

source.title: Ten Advances in Mathematics and Theoretical Computer Science

main_results.informal: For n at least 32, every valid rational formula over the complex numbers that computes the n-by-n permanent has at least n^4 / (192 log_2 n) variable leaves.
The same quartic-over-logarithmic lower bound controls variable leaves, total leaves, and vertices, and half that bound controls internal gates.

projects.title: Persistent failure of quartic sum-of-squares exactness
projects.summary: Constructs explicit rational cubics in fourteen real variables whose Euclidean quartic regularizations have a strict ordinary sum-of-squares gap for every positive regularization, quadratic, and cubic parameter. A companion construction has a unique global minimizer and a positive-definite Hessian there. Exact moment certificates and a general SOS degree bridge certify the gap for arbitrary finite sums of squares of real polynomials.

source.title: Persistent SOS failure with an explicit unique global minimizer

main_results.informal: For every positive sigma, a, and b, the explicit fourteen-variable quartic sigma/4 times the Euclidean norm to the fourth power minus a/2 times the squared norm minus b times the displayed cubic has the stated attained global minimum, and subtracting that minimum is not an ordinary finite sum of squares of real polynomials.

For all three positive parameters, the companion quartic has exactly one global minimizer, its actual polynomial Hessian is positive definite there, and its shift by the attained minimum is not an ordinary sum of squares.

For positive sigma and a and any real b, every ordinary sum-of-squares lower bound is at most the stated minimum-value expression minus b times 753357629/500000000000 times the cube of the stated radius. When b is positive, that expression is the attained global minimum.

An explicit linear functional on real polynomials has normalized radial moments, is nonnegative on all quadratic squares, annihilates the quadratic sphere localizers, and evaluates the cubic to 500753357629/500000000000, strictly above its sphere maximum of one.

projects.title: Stable phase retrieval for Hermite-Fock expansions
projects.summary: Formalizes stable phase retrieval for finite Hermite-Fock polynomials and their Gaussian L2 closure in d complex dimensions, together with the quantitative one-dimensional Fock-space local stability estimate that underlies it.

source.title: Stable phase retrieval for Hermite-Fock expansions

main_results.informal: Proves stable phase retrieval for the Gaussian L2 closure of finite d-dimensional Hermite-Fock polynomials at a fixed level, giving a uniform stability constant bounding the phase-aligned L2 distance by the L2 distance of magnitudes.
main_results.source_ref: R. Balan, P. Casazza, D. Edidin, On signal reconstruction without phase, Appl. Comput. Harmon. Anal. 20 (2006), 345-356, doi:10.1016/j.acha.2005.07.001.

main_results.informal: Proves the phase-aligned one-dimensional Fock-space local stability estimate, producing a unit phase for which the L2 distance to one is controlled by the magnitude defect.
Proves the quantitative centered core estimate bounding the Gaussian Fock norm of a polynomial with small norm by the magnitude defect against one.
Proves the local Fock-space stable phase retrieval coercivity estimate for centered polynomials.

Defines the Gaussian L2 closure of finite Hermite-Fock polynomials at a fixed level.

projects.title: Planar Euclidean dual-geodesic midpoint rigidity
projects.summary: Complementary canonical local midpoints for two Euclidean dual torsion-free connections force their symmetric cubic tensor to be constant on a connected open planar domain. The proof constructs the local geodesic germs and derives the fourth-order obstruction, including its exceptional tensors. A differential strengthening needs only differentiability; five fixed direction tests suffice.

source.notes: The upstream MIT-licensed original proof settles the dimension-two case of Nielsen–Okamura Conjecture 9.1 (v2, Section 9); the cited paper poses the general-dimensional conjecture and does not contain this planar necessity proof. Public completed source was released on 2026-10-08. Proofs and mathematical arguments were produced by OpenAI Codex agents under JD Jones's supervision.

main_results.informal: On an open preconnected Euclidean planar domain, a smooth symmetric cubic tensor field whose canonical local dual geodesic midpoints sum to the endpoints is constant.
The geometric midpoint rigidity theorem already holds for C2 coefficient fields.
A differentiable planar cubic coefficient field is constant if its quartic midpoint obstruction vanishes at every point and in every direction.
The differential obstruction criterion needs only the five directions (j, 1) for j = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 at every point.

projects.title: Poincaré's Nonintegrability Theorem for the Restricted Three-Body Problem
projects.summary: Formalizes Poincaré's classical parameter-analytic nonintegrability theorem for the planar circular restricted three-body problem. The development defines the rotating-frame Hamiltonian on its collision-free domain, proves logarithmic blow-up of the resonant disturbing average at an apoapsis collision boundary, and analytically propagates the resulting dense resonant obstruction to exclude an additional analytic first integral. The final statement is the fixed-coordinate, global uniform-domain special case of the planar part of Yagasaki's Theorem 1.1; his local meromorphic resonant-orbit obstruction is Theorem 3.1.

source.title: A new proof of Poincaré's result on the restricted three-body problem

main_results.source_ref: Kazuyuki Yagasaki, "A new proof of Poincaré's result on the restricted three-body problem," Theorem 1.1 (p. 2), planar case; compare the precise local meromorphic obstruction near resonant unperturbed elliptic orbits in Theorem 3.1 (p. 8). The Lean result is the fixed-coordinate global uniform-domain special case: a global real-analytic family restricts and complexifies on the local neighborhoods used in the source theorem.

main_results.informal: If the first homological equation holds and its perturbing Fourier coefficient is nonzero at every positive rational Kepler resonance, then the leading differential of a putative analytic first integral is nowhere independent of the unperturbed Hamiltonian frequency.

At a resonant action in two degrees of freedom, a nonzero perturbing Fourier mode and the first homological equation force the unperturbed frequency and the differential of a putative leading first-integral coefficient to be linearly dependent.
If the resonant obstruction holds on a dense set of actions and the frequency and differential vary continuously, then they are linearly dependent at every action.

projects.title: Pointwise provable equality and the failure of composition
projects.summary: For every consistent recursively enumerable extension of Peano arithmetic, pointwise provable equality of unary programs fails to respect composition. Separate productive-set and Goedel incompleteness proofs establish the obstruction. For consistent extensions, compatibility is equivalent to Pi-one completeness. For every extension, the generated composition congruence is extensional equality in the Sigma-one sound case and universal otherwise. The development also proves weak-totality and range obstructions and identifies the sound generated quotient with actual unary partial recursive functions. Its coherent dependency closure preserves the concrete evaluator, arithmetization, first-order syntax, semantics and provability infrastructure. Main-result proofs were produced by AI agents under Florian Lengyel's direction; the Foundation dependency includes substantial human formalization by the Formalized Formal Logic contributors.

For every Sigma-one sound extension of Peano arithmetic, the generated quotient is a monoid isomorphic to actual unary partial recursive functions with partial-function composition.

projects.title: The polynomial Freiman–Ruzsa conjecture
projects.summary: Formalizes Marton's polynomial Freiman–Ruzsa conjecture by the entropy method, including the characteristic-two bounds with exponents twelve and nine, the bounded-torsion theorem with an explicit exponent, and quantitative consequences for affine dimension and approximate homomorphisms. The supporting development builds entropic Ruzsa distance, multidistance, conditional entropy, and additive-energy machinery. This optimized import reuses the pooled Zhang–Yeung entropy and kernel library in place of duplicate upstream modules while preserving all six closed headline statements.

source.title: Marton's conjecture (the polynomial Freiman–Ruzsa conjecture)

main_results.informal: A nonempty finite set A of doubling at most K in an abelian group of exponent two is covered by fewer than 2 K^12 cosets of a finite subgroup no larger than A.
Strengthens the characteristic-two covering theorem to fewer than 2 K^9 cosets of a finite subgroup no larger than A.
In an abelian group of exponent m at least two, a nonempty finite set of doubling at most K is covered by fewer than m K^(256 m^3 + 1) cosets of a subgroup no larger than A.
A nonempty finite set of doubling at most K in a finite-rank free abelian group has a subset of relative size at least K^(-34) and affine dimension at most (80 / log 2) log K.
A map between finite abelian groups of exponent two whose additive defects lie in S differs from a homomorphism by a map taking at most |S|^10 values.
A map between finite abelian groups of exponent two that is additive on at least a 1/K fraction of pairs agrees with a homomorphism on at least (|G| / (2^144 K^122) - 1) / 2 points.

projects.title: Puiseux's theorem
projects.summary: Constructs Puiseux series as the bounded-denominator subfield of rational-exponent Hahn series. Proves that this field is algebraic over Laurent series over any coefficient field, and is an algebraic closure when the coefficient field is algebraically closed of characteristic zero. The Newton-Puiseux proof includes reusable Hensel splitting and polynomial translation lemmas. Dean Cureton directed the AI formalization and subsequently simplified its proofs.

source.title: Puiseux's theorem in Lean 4

main_results.informal: For an algebraically closed field K of characteristic zero, the field of Puiseux series over K is an algebraic closure of the Laurent series field K((t)).
Over any field K, the Puiseux series field is algebraic over the Laurent series field.
A rational-exponent Hahn series belongs to the Puiseux subfield if and only if its support lies in (1/n) times the integers for some positive integer n.
A monic degree-m polynomial over K[[t]] whose reduction has a root of multiplicity k, with 0 < k < m, factors into monic polynomials of degrees k and m-k.

projects.title: Pure Nock semantics, trace certificates, and polynomial fingerprints
projects.summary: Formalizes Pure Nock nouns with natural-number leaves, operational semantics, evaluator soundness and completeness, verifiable crash behavior, modular evaluation and guarded natural-number bridges, execution trace certificates, and polynomial fingerprints over arbitrary finite fields. Distinct field-valued noun data have bounded fingerprint collision probability, with a union bound for tables sharing one random evaluation point. A computable Horner evaluator agrees with the polynomial fingerprint. The language and fingerprint closure excludes the framework's zkVM, AIR, RAP, table security theorem, and concrete Goldilocks field. Manuscript line references concern the upstream bundled draft v0.1.6, rather than the posted ePrint revision.

main_results.informal: A subject and formula evaluate to a result under the small-step program machine with some finite fuel if and only if the derived paper evaluator produces that result with some finite fuel.

Every successfully emitted program trace is consistent and complete, every adjacent transition passes the Nock checker, and the final state is either terminal or has a crash edge accepted by the checker.

For a modulus greater than one and inputs whose atoms are below the modulus, successful guarded evaluation produces the same bounded result under natural-number paper evaluation, modular paper evaluation, the full modular evaluator, the natural-number reference evaluator, and the small-step program machine with some finite fuel.

For nouns with at most Lambda leaves and distinct field-valued coefficient data or tree shapes, a uniformly selected point of a finite field makes their polynomial fingerprints coincide with probability at most 2 times (2 Lambda minus 1) divided by the field cardinality.
The computable Horner fingerprint of every noun at every field evaluation point equals its polynomial fingerprint.
The three-valued evaluator reports a crash at some finite fuel exactly when the initial verb has a complete trace ending at a stuck nonterminal state.

For a finite table of bounded-length nouns evaluated at one shared random field point, the probability that some pair with distinct field-valued data collides is at most the single-pair error times k times (k minus 1) divided by 2.

Converts the positive parametrization to an unrestricted sixteen-integer-parameter parametrization using the four-square theorem.

projects.title: Quantum code certificates and hypergraph-product theory
projects.summary: Formalizes general binary row reduction, kernel bases and rank certificates; quantum-code distance bounds from witnesses and exhaustive low-weight enumeration; arbitrary-matrix hypergraph-product dimension and X/Z cleaning bounds; and CSS orthogonality of lifted products over finite groups. Includes a Pauli expression translation modulo global phase, a Boolean encoding with proved soundness and model extension, and sound checking of RUP additions in LRAT certificates, bridged to matrix-level distance bounds. Concrete code-family datasets, large certificate replays and measurement protocols are outside this import.

source.title: Quantum code parameters, checkable by a certificate of provable size

main_results.informal: For arbitrary finite binary matrices A and B, the number of columns of their hypergraph product minus its X and Z ranks equals nullity(A) times nullity(B) plus nullity(transpose A) times nullity(transpose B), expressed with natural-number rank differences.

main_results.informal: If a binary vector is killed by the hypergraph-product X check and is outside the Z row space, its Hamming weight is at least the minimum of supplied lower bounds for nonzero vectors in the kernels of the first input and the transpose of the second input.
Dually, a vector killed by the Z check and outside the X row space has weight at least the minimum of supplied lower bounds for the kernels of the transpose of the first input and the second input.
For arbitrary matrices of binary-valued functions on a finite group, the left/right regular expansion gives lifted-product X and Z checks whose every pair of rows has zero binary dot product.
The rank of a finite binary matrix equals the length of the verified row-reduction output for its list of rows.

For two binary matrices, if d is at most the number of columns, exhaustive enumeration finds no vector of weight below d in the first kernel outside the second row space, and a supplied vector has those membership properties and weight d, then the minimum such weight is d. The empty-set distance convention is the number of columns plus one.

Acceptance by the RUP certificate checker implies unsatisfiability of the original CNF. No correctness assumption on an external SAT solver is needed; the clause-database interface carries proved soundness laws.

For a positive number n of input bits and nonempty row supports within that range, a Boolean assignment satisfying the parity constraints, odd bilinear pairing and weight bound extends to a model of buildPair while agreeing on all 2n input variables. The complementary soundness theorem extracts those constraints from every model.

projects.title: Galois groups of quadratic polynomial iterates
projects.summary: Formalizes Stoll's criterion for when the Galois group of the n-th iterate of X² + a over the rationals is the full n-fold iterated wreath product of C₂. It proves the criterion in terms of two-independence of a signed critical-orbit sequence and its pairwise-coprime Möbius factors, and derives the paper's congruence families for which maximality holds at every level. The supporting library develops reusable multiquadratic-extension, iterated wreath-product, Möbius-factor, and valuation results.

source.title: Galois groups over ℚ of some iterated polynomials

main_results.informal: For each n, assuming -a is not a rational square, the Galois group of the n-th iterate of X² + a is the full n-fold iterated wreath product of C₂ exactly when either the first n terms of the signed sequence c₁ = -a, cₖ = fₖ(0) for k ≥ 2, or the first n integer Möbius factors of that sequence are independent modulo rational squares.
If -a is not a rational square and none of the absolute Möbius factors from levels 2 through n is a rational square, then the n-th iterate has the full iterated-wreath-product Galois group.
The Galois group is the full iterated wreath product at every positive level when a is positive and congruent to 1 or 2 modulo 4, or when a is negative and divisible by 4 with -a nonsquare.

projects.title: Quantum parallel repetition
projects.summary: Proves a quantitative parallel-repetition theorem for finite two-player quantum games: whenever the entangled value is below one, the entangled values of parallel repetitions decay exponentially, with an explicit universal exponent in the game gap and answer-alphabet sizes.

source.title: Ten Advances in Mathematics and Theoretical Computer Science

main_results.informal: There is a universal positive constant giving an explicit exponential upper bound on the repeated entangled value of every finite game with positive gap and nonempty answer alphabets.
Every finite two-player game whose entangled value is below one has exponentially decaying entangled value under parallel repetition.

projects.title: Adversary bounds and the polynomial method for quantum queries
projects.summary: Develops finite quantum query algorithms, real adversary primal and dual programs, strong duality, exact Boolean block composition, explicit constant-factor bounded-error query characterizations, and degree bounds for output-probability polynomials. Query models include idle and blank sectors; bounds count queries, not gate complexity or running time. Uniform algorithm extraction assumes a supplied dual certificate.

main_results.informal: For every total Boolean function on a finite Boolean input cube, the all-pairs real adversary dual infimum equals the real symmetric primal supremum.
The negative-weight adversary value of total Boolean functions composed on disjoint blocks equals the product of their adversary values, including constant functions and empty index types.

For a total Boolean function at error one third, quantum value-query complexity lies between ADV±/36 and 2^14 ADV±. The value oracle swaps a blank answer with the queried letter and includes an idle query index.
For the Boolean XOR oracle with idle and blank sectors, query complexity at error one third lies between ADV±/72 and 2^15 ADV±.

A supplied all-pairs real dual certificate of nonnegative cost c gives a finite quantum algorithm using at most 8192(1+c) value queries at error one third, for any finite promise domain and nonempty decidable output type.
Each output probability of a q-query value-oracle algorithm on Boolean inputs agrees on the Boolean cube with a real polynomial of total degree at most 2q.
Each output probability of a q-query Boolean XOR algorithm agrees on the Boolean cube with a real polynomial of total degree at most 2q.

projects.title: Quasi-Borel Spaces
projects.summary: Formalizes quasi-Borel spaces and quasi-Borel pre-domains, a category for higher-order probability theory.

main_results.informal: Defines a quasi-Borel space as a type with a set of random variables closed under constants, measurable precomposition, and gluing.
Defines morphisms of quasi-Borel spaces as maps that preserve random variables under precomposition.
Combines the quasi-Borel and ω-complete partial order structures with the compatibility axiom of Vakar-Kammar-Staton.
Defines the probability-measure monad on quasi-Borel spaces by quotienting pre-probability measures by integral equivalence.

projects.title: Radó's theorem for Riemann surfaces
projects.summary: Proves that every connected Hausdorff one-dimensional complex manifold is second countable. The development constructs a nonconstant harmonic function by Perron's method, builds the étale space of its harmonic-conjugate germs, and applies a formalized Poincaré-Volterra lemma to its discrete-fiber evaluation map.

source.title: Radó's theorem for Riemann surfaces

main_results.informal: Every connected Hausdorff topological space carrying the structure of a one-dimensional complex manifold has a second-countable topology.

A connected Hausdorff, locally compact, locally connected and locally second-countable space is second countable whenever it admits a continuous, locally injective map into a second-countable Hausdorff space.

Every continuous real-valued function on a Euclidean circle extends continuously to its closed disk and harmonically to the open disk; unlike the existing LeanComplexAnalysis Poisson theorems, this constructs the harmonic function rather than assuming one.
The pointwise upper envelope of a Perron family of surface subharmonic functions is harmonic on its open domain.

projects.title: The Ramanujan-Nagell theorem
projects.summary: Formalizes the Ramanujan-Nagell theorem, proving that the Diophantine equation x^2 + 7 = 2^n has exactly the five positive-integer solutions (|x|, n) = (1, 3), (3, 4), (5, 5), (11, 7), (181, 15).

main_results.informal: Proves that the integer solutions of x^2 + 7 = 2^n are exactly (x, n) = (+/-1, 3), (+/-3, 4), (+/-5, 5), (+/-11, 7), (+/-181, 15).
main_results.source_ref: T. Nagell, The Diophantine equation x^2 + 7 = 2^n, Ark. Mat. 4 (1961), 185-187; L. J. Mordell, Diophantine Equations, Academic Press, 1969, Ch. 20.

projects.title: ABC implies that Ramanujan's tau function misses almost all primes
projects.summary: Formalizes the ABC-conditional proof that Ramanujan's tau function takes prime values only rarely.

main_results.informal: ABC implies that Ramanujan's tau function misses almost all primes.
Reduces the main prime-value statement to the key analytic estimates.
ABC-bound input for the Eisenstein-series term E2.
ABC-bound input for the Eisenstein-series term E4.

projects.title: Rare subtree patterns in conditioned Bienaymé trees
projects.summary: Proves marked Poisson approximation, root declumping, maximal complete non-fringe r-ary height and maximum leaf-height for critical Bienaymé trees conditioned on their size, under the stated stable-domain, marking, cutoff and non-clustering hypotheses. Periodic offspring laws are included through admissible-size limits. Single-point phase refinements are formulated along phase-separated admissible subsequences. The dependency closure preserves tree coding, Chen–Stein bounds, regular variation, stable densities and lattice local limit estimates, with concrete offspring examples and direct consequences.

main_results.informal: Under the critical stable-domain assumption, microscopicity and non-clustering with a common sublinear divergent cutoff give Poisson approximation for bounded expected marked counts, and a law of large numbers when the expected count diverges, along admissible tree sizes.

For a root-degree set B with positive finite weight c_B, structural microscopicity of the original marks and non-clustering of the root-declumped marks yield Poisson approximation with the c_B-adjusted parameter when expected counts are bounded, and divergence in probability when they grow, along admissible tree sizes.

For critical offspring laws in a stable domain, the maximum non-fringe complete r-ary height has a lattice-Gumbel law for unary strings and two-point localization for r at least two, with the stated offspring probabilities and single-point refinements along phase-separated admissible subsequences.

The maximum leaf-height has the stated lattice-Gumbel behavior when the unary offspring probability is positive, and the two-point behavior when it is zero, with single-point refinements along phase-separated admissible subsequences and the stated nondegeneracy and stable-domain conditions.

projects.title: Improved Lower Bounds for Strong n-Conjectures
projects.summary: Formalizes the disproof of Ramaekers's conjecture, constructing tuple families whose abc-style quality stays bounded above 1, and proves Browkin-Brzezinski lower bounds on the quality of the n-conjecture tuples.

source.title: Improved Lower Bounds for Strong n-Conjectures

main_results.informal: Defines Ramaekers's conjecture for fixed n as the statement that the quality of the relevant tuple set equals 1.
Proves Ramaekers's conjecture fails for every n at least 6 (the general case, Theorem 1.14).
Proves Ramaekers's conjecture fails for every odd n at least 5 (the odd case via Pell equations, Theorem 1.13).
Proves Ramaekers's conjecture fails for n equal to 5 (the Konyagin prelude bound).
Proves the Browkin-Brzezinski 1994 lower bound 2n-5 on the quality of the n-conjecture tuples (Theorem 1.3).

projects.title: A proof of the Regts–Sevenster conjecture, formalized
projects.summary: A Lean 4 proof of the Regts–Sevenster conjecture. A complex-valued graph parameter, normalized at the empty graph and invariant under isomorphism, has exponentially bounded edge-connection rank if and only if it is a mixed partition function. For a natural rank base R, a representing model can be chosen with k even and 2ℓ odd colours satisfying k + 2ℓ ≤ R. The development also proves the even connection-rank growth limit, minimum total colour dimension, minimal parity formulas and prescribed-dimension criterion. Schrijver's factorial argument supplies nilpotent-trace vanishing; semisimplicity and Deligne's fibre-functor theorem give the model; a polynomial commutant estimate gives the sharp colour budget. Deligne's theorem and the required symmetric-group character theory are proved within the development. The appendix's trace-zeta results give rationality and degree bounds, with an independent proof of nilpotent-trace vanishing. The theorems of record use only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound, checked by pinned audits.

main_results.informal: Normalized isomorphism-invariant complex graph parameters with exponentially bounded edge-connection ranks are precisely mixed partition functions.
A natural rank bound R admits a representing mixed model with total color dimension at most R.
The development proves its stated Deligne fiber-functor theorem for the symmetric tensor categories used in the representation.

projects.title: Rellich–Kondrachov compact embedding theorem
projects.summary: Formalizes the Rellich–Kondrachov compact embedding theorem: the Sobolev embedding H¹ → L² is a compact operator on compact Riemannian manifolds. The proof builds the Euclidean core (compactness of the H¹ → L² inclusion on a fixed compact support via the Fréchet–Kolmogorov criterion and the H¹ translation estimate ‖τₐu − u‖₂ ≤ ‖a‖ · ‖∇u‖₂), glues chart contributions over a finite atlas, and specializes to the Levi-Civita Riemannian volume measure.

source.title: Rellich–Kondrachov compact Sobolev embedding theorem

main_results.informal: On a compact Riemannian manifold, the Sobolev inclusion H¹ → L² for the Levi-Civita volume measure is a compact operator.
Euclidean Rellich–Kondrachov compactness: on a fixed compact support K, the H¹ → L² inclusion restricted to functions supported in K is a compact operator.
On a compact Riemannian manifold there exists finite chart data equipped with explicit Lipschitz neighborhoods and a subordinate partition of unity, the input to the manifold Rellich glue.

projects.title: Riemann Mapping Theorem
projects.summary: Formalizes a proof of the Riemann mapping theorem for proper simply connected plane domains with primitives.

main_results.informal: Proves the Riemann mapping theorem for the project's domain hypotheses.
Constructs a conformal map from a good domain onto the unit disk.
Proves a Montel compactness theorem for uniformly bounded holomorphic families.
Proves the Hurwitz theorem used to preserve injectivity under limits.

projects.title: Riemann–Roch for algebraic function fields
projects.summary: Formalizes the Riemann–Roch theorem for algebraic function fields of one variable through the adelic route. Divisors are indexed by intrinsic places (discrete rank-one valuation subrings containing the constants), with an equivalence to a two-chart coordinate model via Ostrowski's theorem. The development builds Riemann–Roch spaces, the genus, an intrinsic adele space, Weil differentials and the canonical class, and proves Riemann's inequality, the duality theorem, Riemann–Roch, Clifford's inequality, and the standard corollaries. As an application it shows that a Weierstrass elliptic curve has genus one and identifies its degree-one places with the class group of the coordinate ring compatibly with the group law.

source.title: Riemann–Roch for function fields, in Lean 4

main_results.informal: For a function field K over its full constant field k, a canonical divisor W, and any divisor D indexed by intrinsic places, ℓ(D) = deg D + 1 − g + ℓ(W − D).
For a canonical divisor W and any divisor D, ℓ(W − D) equals the index of specialty i(D), the codimension of L(D) plus K inside the adele space.
Riemann's inequality ℓ(D) ≥ deg D + 1 − g holds for every divisor D.

Clifford's inequality 2(ℓ(D) − 1) ≤ deg D holds for every divisor D with 0 ≤ deg D ≤ 2g − 2, ℓ(D) > 0, and ℓ(W − D) > 0 for a canonical divisor W. The degree bounds are not needed for the inequality and are dropped in FunctionField.clifford_of_ell_pos.
Every function field admits a canonical divisor, namely the divisor of a nonzero Weil differential.
The function field of a Weierstrass elliptic curve over a field k that is its full constant field (for example any algebraically closed k, in any characteristic) has genus one.
The bijection between degree-one places of an elliptic function field and the class group of the coordinate ring is compatible with the elliptic group law.

projects.title: RL Theory in Lean
projects.summary: Develops probability, Markov-chain, and stochastic-matrix infrastructure for reinforcement-learning theory.

main_results.informal: Proves existence of a stationary distribution for a stochastic matrix.

projects.title: Explicit type Aₙ and BCₙ root pairings
projects.summary: Constructs the type Aₙ and BCₙ root pairings explicitly over ℤ — from signed intervals on Fin n and from the reflective vectors of the standard dot product — proves the pairing and reflection identities exhibiting them as Mathlib `RootPairing`s, and identifies the BCₙ roots with the classical set {±eᵢ, ±2eᵢ, ±eᵢ ± eⱼ}.

source.title: Introduction to Lie Algebras and Representation Theory

main_results.informal: Constructs the type Aₙ root pairing over the integers from signed intervals on Fin n, with finiteness, reducedness, and crystallographic properties.
main_results.source_ref: N. Bourbaki, Lie Groups and Lie Algebras, Chapters 4-6, Springer, 2002; J. E. Humphreys, Introduction to Lie Algebras and Representation Theory, GTM 9, Springer, 1972, Ch. III.

main_results.informal: Constructs the type BCₙ root pairing from the reflective vectors of the standard dot product on ℤⁿ via a symmetric nondegenerate form.
Characterizes the reflective vectors of the standard dot product on ℤⁿ as exactly the classical type BCₙ roots ±eᵢ, ±2eᵢ, and ±eᵢ ± eⱼ for i ≠ j.
Identifies the root set of the type BCₙ root pairing with the classical type BCₙ root set.

projects.title: The nonmeagre lower bound for the rearrangement number
projects.summary: Formalizes the inequality non(M) ≤ rr in ZFC via relational systems, category and slalom bounds, finite-vector constructions, and rearrangements of conditionally convergent real series. The reverse inequality from the accompanying manuscript is outside the upstream Lean formalization.

main_results.informal: The uniformity of the meagre ideal is at most the rearrangement number.

projects.title: Certified Runge-Kutta Order Conditions
projects.summary: Certifies Runge-Kutta order conditions over planar rooted trees, including RK4 order four, Dormand-Prince order five, and Gauss-Legendre order six.

source.title: What Order a Method Knows

main_results.informal: Reduces order-p Runge-Kutta conditions to a finite catalogue check over rooted trees.
Certifies that classical RK4 satisfies all planar rooted-tree order conditions through order four.
Shows that RK4 fails a fifth-order condition, pinning its order exactly.
Proves order conditions are invariant under permutations of a node's children.
Certifies the Dormand-Prince RK45 fifth-order tableau through order five.
Certifies the Gauss-Legendre three-stage tableau through order four over Q(sqrt(15)).
Certifies the denominator-cleared (360-scaled) integer Z(sqrt(15)) Gauss-Legendre tableau through order six, the scaled certificate feeding the homogeneity bridge.
Certifies the Gauss-Legendre s=3 tableau through order six over Q(sqrt(15)), via the formalized homogeneity bridge from the 360-scaled integer certificate.

projects.title: Sharp asymptotic bounds for runs of multiples in finite sets
projects.summary: For a finite set S of n positive integers, let k(S,a) be the least positive integer k for which k*a is outside S. Proves an upper bound for every such S and a matching positive lower bound attained by some set of every sufficiently large cardinality n, establishing the extremal order n log n log log n. Contains entropy and chain-compression upper bounds and two lower-bound constructions, sharing definitions, prime estimates and padding. Preserves prime-weighted entropy estimates, smooth-number constructions and abstract cardinality-preserving compression lemmas.

source.title: Runs of multiples in a finite set of integers
authors: Claude Opus 5.5 (AI; published by Jason Hoelscher-Obermaier)

main_results.informal: Every sufficiently large finite set S of positive integers has sum of its first missing multiple indices at most C*n*log(n)*log(log(n)); for every sufficiently large n, a set of exactly n positive integers attains at least c*n*log(n)*log(log(n)), for a fixed c>0. This proof uses entropy and smooth numbers.
The identical sharp asymptotic statement, proved using compression to divisor-closed, prime-shift-closed sets and a box-times-simplex construction.

projects.title: The Rupert Problem for convex polyhedra
projects.summary: Formalizes the Rupert property for the cube, the regular tetrahedron, and the triakis tetrahedron, exhibiting for each an explicit straight-through hole admitting a congruent copy.

main_results.informal: Proves that the cube has the Rupert property.
Proves that the regular tetrahedron has the Rupert property.
Proves that the triakis tetrahedron has the Rupert property.

projects.title: Sabidussi's compatibility conjecture for Eulerian multigraphs
projects.summary: Formalizes Sabidussi's compatibility conjecture for finite labelled endpoint multigraphs with loops and parallel edges, where a loop contributes two half-edge incidences to the degree of its vertex. Given an Euler tour and minimum degree at least four, the main theorem constructs a partition of all edges into nonempty, edge-connected, 2-regular ordinary circuits such that consecutive edges of the Euler tour never lie in the same circuit. The proof runs a four-colour (F_2^2) algebra over the cyclic transition word, uses an odd balancing parity lemma to choose compatible local frames, and transports the resulting colouring back to a compatible ordinary circuit decomposition.

source.title: Graph Puzzles III.1: A proof of Sabidussi's compatibility conjecture

main_results.informal: For any finite endpoint multigraph with an Euler tour and minimum degree at least four, the edges partition into ordinary, nonempty, connected, 2-regular circuits that are compatible with the tour: no circuit contains two consecutive tour edges.
The same compatibility statement phrased with the intrinsic even-edge-set circuit decomposition, from which the ordinary-circuit form is derived.

projects.title: Every Pisot number is a two-sided limit of Salem numbers
projects.summary: Proves Salem’s two-sided approximation theorem for Pisot numbers, preserving both the polynomial reciprocal-family construction and the exceptional quadratic-unit construction.

main_results.informal: Every Pisot number is approached by Salem numbers from both below and above.
For the nondegenerate Pisot polynomial pattern, reciprocal-family polynomials have Salem roots arbitrarily near the Pisot root from either side.
The quadratic-unit family supplies Salem roots approaching each reciprocal quadratic Pisot unit from either side.

projects.title: Moreira's version of Sard's theorem
projects.summary: Formalizes Moreira's strengthening of Sard's theorem, bounding the Hausdorff dimension of critical-value images of C^{k+alpha} maps.

main_results.informal: Proves Hausdorff-measure nullity for images of points where the derivative rank is bounded by p, at Moreira's Sard bound.
main_results.source_ref: Moreira 2001, http://dmle.icmat.es/pdf/PUBLICACIONSMATEMATIQUES_2001_45_01_06.pdf

main_results.informal: Converts the measure-null theorem into the headline Hausdorff-dimension upper bound for critical-value images.
main_results.source_ref: Moreira 2001, http://dmle.icmat.es/pdf/PUBLICACIONSMATEMATIQUES_2001_45_01_06.pdf

projects.title: Jordan–Schönflies theorem
projects.summary: Formalizes the Jordan curve theorem and the extension of every homeomorphism between Jordan curves to a plane homeomorphism.

source.title: The Jordan–Schönflies theorem in Lean

main_results.informal: Every homeomorphism between two Jordan curves in the plane extends to a self-homeomorphism of the plane.
A homeomorphism between Jordan curves extends to a global homeomorphism agreeing with it on the source curve.
Every Jordan curve separates the plane into an inside and an outside region.

projects.title: Scott's measurement representation theorems
projects.summary: Formalizes all eight numbered finite representation theorems of Dana Scott's 1964 Measurement Structures and Linear Inequalities. Develops a shared finite separation and rational-cancellation engine, unit-threshold semiorder representations, additive utility on pairs, ordered utility differences, and normalized finitely additive probabilities on finite Boolean algebras. Includes the Kraft-Pratt-Seidenberg five-atom counterexample to de Finetti's weaker axioms and local real embeddings of finite subsets of ordered abelian groups. A separately labelled modern infinite analogue assumes a generalized Kelley condition: strict-comparison vectors have a countable cover by closed convex upper sets avoiding zero above the weak-comparison cone. It is neither a countably additive measure theorem nor an attribution of Scott's unpublished infinite theorem. The infinite construction uses universal probability evaluation vectors, with a proved faithful Stone representation and probability-state correspondence. The upstream proofs were produced primarily by AI agents under Lars Warren Ericson's direction and review.

source.title: Measurement Structures and Linear Inequalities

main_results.informal: For a finite symmetric subset X of a finite-dimensional real normed space, membership in an arbitrary set N on X is represented by nonnegativity of a linear functional if and only if every x in X has x or -x in N and every zero sum of positively real-weighted vectors from X intersect N has all their negatives in N.

For a finite symmetric set of rational-valued vectors on a finite coordinate type, the same linear realizability criterion uses unweighted zero sums, with repetitions allowed, instead of arbitrary positive real weights.

A relation on a finite set of rational-valued vectors on a finite coordinate type is represented exactly by comparison of one real linear functional if and only if it is complete and, whenever two equally indexed finite lists have equal sums and every left vector is related to its right partner, all the reverse comparisons also hold.

A relation on a finite rational vector set is represented by one real linear functional if and only if it extends to its zero-inclusive additive submonoid closure as a complete relation preserving addition and satisfying Scott's cancellation axiom.

On any finite set (allowing the empty case, unlike the source), a relation P admits real scores with P x y exactly when the score of x is at least the score of y plus one if and only if P is irreflexive and satisfies Scott's two four-alternative semiorder axioms.

On the product of any two finite sets (also allowing empty coordinate types), a relation admits an additive representation f(x)+g(x') exactly when it is total and satisfies Scott's cancellation scheme for independent permutations of the two coordinates.

On any finite set (also allowing the empty case), a quaternary relation D is represented exactly by comparisons f(x)-f(y) >= f(z)-f(w) for one real utility f if and only if D is total and satisfies permutation cancellation and reversal.

A relation on a finite Boolean algebra is represented exactly by a nonnegative normalized finitely additive real probability if and only if the certain event is strictly above null, every event is at least null, comparisons are total, and Scott's cancellation scheme holds whenever two finite lists have equal sums of atom characteristic vectors.

Every finite subset of a linearly ordered abelian group has a real-valued map reflecting its order and preserving every addition equation whose three terms lie in the subset; this asserts a local map, not an embedding of the entire group.

The explicit Kraft-Pratt-Seidenberg order on the 32 events of five atoms satisfies de Finetti's five qualitative-probability axioms but has no normalized finitely additive real probability representing all comparisons.

On an arbitrary Boolean algebra, a relation admits an exact normalized finitely additive real probability representation if and only if it is nontrivial, nonnegative relative to null, total, and satisfies the stated generalized Kelley cover condition on its universal event-span comparison vectors. This is a modern analogue with an explicit extra analytic condition.

Finitely additive probabilities on an arbitrary Boolean algebra are canonically equivalent to positive normalized continuous linear functionals on the real span of its universal probability-evaluation vectors, equipped with the inherited supremum norm.

projects.title: Selberg Sieve
projects.summary: Formalizes the Selberg sieve with applications to prime-counting bounds and a Brun-Titchmarsh-style estimate.

source.title: Sieve Methods

main_results.informal: Proves the simple Selberg sieve upper-bound theorem.
Derives the asymptotic prime-counting upper bound.
Gives an eventual explicit constant upper bound for the prime-counting function.
Bounds the number of primes in an interval using the sieve estimate.

projects.title: Genus-Zero Pairings and Catalan Numbers
projects.summary: Formalizes the finite combinatorics behind the genus-zero term of the Wigner semicircle law: a pairing of Fin (2n), viewed as a fixed-point-free involution, has genus zero (total cycle count of the rotation product maximal) exactly when it is noncrossing, and these genus-zero pairings are counted by the Catalan number Cₙ. The Catalan recurrence is obtained from an explicit equivalence decomposing a noncrossing pairing by the partner of vertex 0 into independent inside and outside pairings.

source.title: semicircle-catalan: genus-zero pairings and the Catalan moments of the Wigner semicircle law

main_results.informal: The number of noncrossing pairings on 2n points equals the Catalan number catalan n.
The number of genus-zero pairings of Fin (2n) equals the Catalan number catalan n.
A pairing has genus zero if and only if it is noncrossing.

projects.title: Wigner Semicircle Distribution
projects.summary: Defines the real Wigner semicircle distribution, its normalized density, affine transformations, and finite-moment integrability.

main_results.informal: Defines the real-valued density of the semicircle distribution with mean μ and variance v.
Defines the ℝ≥0∞-valued density of the semicircle distribution.
Proves that the real-valued semicircle density integrates to one for nonzero variance.
Defines the semicircle measure on ℝ, equal to a Dirac mass when the variance is zero.
Shows that translating a semicircle measure translates its mean parameter.
Shows that scaling by a nonzero constant scales the mean and variance parameters.
Shows that the identity has all finite Lp moments under a semicircle distribution.

projects.title: Sendov's conjecture and the Phelps–Rodriguez conjecture
projects.summary: Proves Sendov's conjecture in full generality: if every zero of a complex polynomial of degree at least two lies in the closed unit disk, then every zero has a critical point within distance one. Also proves the Phelps–Rodriguez strengthening, with strict inequality unless the zero lies on the unit circle and the polynomial is a scalar multiple of z^n - a^n, and recovers Rubinstein's boundary theorem. Formalizes Tao's digestion of Lech Mazur's proof: the problem is reduced to a numerical inequality in the degree and one real parameter, settled by exact rational Bernstein certificates for degrees up to one hundred and by an analytic large-degree reduction beyond. Includes the top case of Maclaurin's inequality and multiset AM–GM, a defect inequality on the closed unit disk, a sharp bound on log(sinh h / h), kernel-checked polynomial certificate infrastructure, and a packed-exponentiation bridge for exact moment integrals.

source.title: Sendov's conjecture in Lean
source.mathematical_source: T. Tao, A digestion of the proof of Sendov's conjecture, blog post, 12 August 2026, digesting Lech Mazur's AI-assisted proof; the boundary case follows Q. Tang and T. Zhang, arXiv:2508.10341, equation (5.1) and Remark 5.1.

projects.provenance_note: The upstream README states that essentially all Lean source was written by Claude Opus 5 in Claude Code under the direction and review of Terence Tao, who set the targets, supplied the informal proof and staged plans, and made the mathematical decisions.

main_results.informal: For every natural number n at least two and every complex polynomial p of degree n all of whose roots have norm at most one, every root a of p admits a root of the derivative of p within distance at most one of a.
main_results.source_ref: Sendov's conjecture (1962); Tao's blog post of 12 August 2026, Conjecture 1, following Mazur's proof; upstream Sendov/Conjecture.lean. First publicly announced 2026-08-12 23:10:54 UTC in that post, with the Lean repository completed the same day.

main_results.informal: Under the same hypotheses, either some root of the derivative lies at distance strictly less than one from a, or a has norm one and p equals a nonzero scalar multiple of X^n - a^n.
main_results.source_ref: Phelps–Rodriguez conjecture; Tao's blog post, Conjecture 2; upstream Sendov/Conjecture.lean. The equality case is Rubinstein's 1968 theorem.

main_results.informal: The same statement in the Mathlib-only form of the upstream statement of record: for every complex polynomial p of degree at least two such that every complex w with p(w) = 0 has norm at most one, every zero a of p admits a root of the derivative within distance at most one of a.
main_results.source_ref: Upstream Solution.lean, the declaration checked by the upstream comparator setup.

main_results.informal: If a polynomial of degree n at least two with all roots in the closed unit disk vanishes at one, then either its derivative has a root within distance strictly less than one of the point one, or the polynomial equals its leading coefficient times X^n - 1.
main_results.source_ref: Rubinstein's theorem; Tang–Zhang arXiv:2508.10341, equation (5.1) and Remark 5.1, run to equality; upstream Sendov/Boundary.lean.

main_results.informal: For every degree n at least five and every real parameter alpha between zero and seventeen satisfying the feasibility constraint c^2 ≤ A, the quantity R n alpha of the blog post's equation stat is strictly less than one.
main_results.source_ref: Equation (stat) of Tao's blog post; degrees five to one hundred by Bernstein certificates (upstream Sendov/FiniteRange), degrees at least 101 by the analytic reduction (upstream Sendov/LargeDegree).

main_results.informal: For a nonempty multiset of nonnegative reals of cardinality m, the (m-1)-st elementary symmetric function is at most m times the (m-1)-st power of the mean.
main_results.source_ref: Maclaurin's inequality, top case; upstream Sendov/Analytic/Maclaurin.lean.

main_results.informal: The product of a multiset of nonnegative reals is at most the mean raised to the cardinality.
main_results.source_ref: Multiset AM–GM inequality; upstream Sendov/Analytic/Maclaurin.lean.

main_results.informal: For a multiset of complex numbers in the closed unit disk, the product of the norms times the sum of the norms of 1/z minus the conjugate of z is at most one minus the square of that product.
main_results.source_ref: The defect lemma; upstream Sendov/Analytic/Defect.lean.

main_results.informal: For every positive real h, the logarithm of sinh h divided by h is at most the square root of h^2 + 9 minus three.
main_results.source_ref: Upstream Sendov/Common/Sinh.lean; the crux of the beta-bound step.

main_results.informal: If the Bernstein expansion of an integer coefficient list on an interval from zero to p/q equals p^d times a polynomial P and every Bernstein coefficient is positive, then P is positive on that interval.
main_results.source_ref: Lean Pool port infrastructure replacing the upstream per-certificate ring identities; LeanPool/Sendov/FiniteRange/Certificate.lean.

projects.title: Sensitivity Conjecture: sqrt(deg) <= sensitivity
projects.summary: Formalizes the quantitative Nisan-Szegedy/Huang sensitivity theorem for Boolean functions.

main_results.informal: Proves that the square root of multilinear degree is bounded above by sensitivity.
Derives the degree bound by the square of sensitivity.

projects.title: Serre's mass formula for totally ramified local-field extensions
projects.summary: Proves both of Serre's mass formulas for totally ramified separable extensions of a nonarchimedean local field of any positive degree, together with the discriminant bound, tame-ramification criterion, finiteness dichotomy, convergence, and automorphism-weighted orbit count. The proof develops Eisenstein monogenicity, quantitative Newton-Hensel lifting, local constancy of root counts, and Haar measures of lattices over discrete valuation rings.

source.title: Une «formule de masse» pour les extensions totalement ramifiées de degré donné d'un corps local

main_results.informal: For every nonarchimedean local field K with residue-field cardinality q and every positive integer n, the sum of q^(-c(L)) over the totally ramified degree-n subextensions L of a separable closure of K is n, where c(L) is the discriminant exponent minus n plus one.
For every nonarchimedean local field K, positive n, and set of representatives of K-isomorphism classes of totally ramified separable degree-n extensions, the sum of 1/(|Aut_K(L)| q^c(L)) is one.
For positive n, the set of totally ramified separable degree-n subextensions is infinite exactly when K and its residue field have the same characteristic p and p divides n.
For positive n, the discriminant exponent of a totally ramified degree-n extension is at least n-1.
For positive n and a totally ramified degree-n extension, the wild discriminant exponent vanishes exactly when the residue characteristic does not divide n.
For positive n, the real-valued series of the unweighted mass terms is summable.

For a nonarchimedean local field K and a totally ramified separable extension L of positive degree n, the number of K-isomorphic copies of L inside a separable closure, multiplied by |Aut_K(L)|, is n.

projects.title: The Kunen inconsistency theorem
projects.summary: Formalizes elementary embeddings of models of ZF set theory and proves the Kunen inconsistency theorem, that there is no nontrivial elementary embedding of the set-theoretic universe into itself.

source.title: Elementary embeddings and infinitary combinatorics

main_results.informal: Proves the Kunen inconsistency theorem, that every elementary embedding of the von Neumann universe V into itself is the identity.
Proves the Kunen inconsistency theorem for von Neumann levels V_μ at a successor-limit ordinal, computing the supremum of the critical-point iterates.
Defines the critical point of a nontrivial elementary embedding as the least ordinal it moves.
Defines a nontrivial elementary embedding of a model of ZF into itself.

projects.title: Shannon Entropy Characterization
projects.summary: Formalizes Shannon's finite-alphabet characterization theorem for entropy from the 1948 paper.
projects.notice:
The upstream MIT LICENSE file gives the copyright line as
