"SamuelSchlesinger".

main_results.informal: Proves that any finite-alphabet uncertainty functional satisfying Shannon's conditions equals natural-log entropy up to a positive scale.
Restates the characterization for any logarithm base greater than one.
Proves the converse, showing that Shannon entropy satisfies the formal condition bundle.
Proves the finite joint-entropy chain rule.
Proves subadditivity of finite joint entropy.

projects.title: Shelah's bound for the Hales–Jewett numbers
projects.summary: Proves the Hales–Jewett theorem with Shelah's primitive recursive bound. The proof is by induction on the alphabet; to add a letter it finds a subspace on which the coloring is insensitive to replacing the new letter by an old one, building each dimension of the subspace from a line given by the pigeonhole principle. This gives an explicit recursion shelahBound k r for the dimension, which is proved to be below the fifth level of the Ackermann function, so every r-coloring of the words of length n ≥ A(5, 2k + r) over k ≥ 1 letters has a monochromatic combinatorial line.

source.title: Primitive recursive bounds for van der Waerden numbers

main_results.informal: Over a nonempty finite alphabet α, every coloring with κ colors of the words indexed by a finite type ι has a monochromatic combinatorial line when |ι| ≥ shelahBound |α| |κ|.
main_results.source_ref: The Hales–Jewett theorem with Shelah's bound.

main_results.informal: For letters a and b and a finite type η, in a cube of dimension insensitiveBound every coloring has an η-dimensional subspace on which replacing a by b in any coordinates does not change the color.
main_results.source_ref: Shelah's insensitivity lemma.

main_results.informal: shelahBound k r < A(5, 2k + r), where A is the Ackermann function.
Over a nonempty finite alphabet of k letters, every coloring with r colors of the words of length n ≥ A(5, 2k + r) has a monochromatic combinatorial line.

projects.title: Exact adaptive single-copy stabilizer learning
projects.summary: Exact recovery of pure qubit stabilizer states from adaptive single-copy measurements, with explicit confidence, copy and elementary gate upper bounds.

main_results.informal: For every normalized pure qubit stabilizer state and failure parameter 0 < delta <= 1, the physical learner returns a finite circuit and readout that decode to the input up to global phase with probability at least 1 - delta. Every supported execution uses exactly 2T + 1 copies and at most (n + 1)T^2 elementary gate applications at the stated round budget T.
For n >= 1, every supported output at the confidence budget consumes fewer than 136(n + log(1 / delta)) input copies.

projects.title: Quadratic-order prime classification
projects.summary: Formalizes foundational algebra for quadratic orders associated to discriminants, including their power basis, norm and discriminant identities, odd-prime splitting/ramification/inertness criteria via Legendre symbols, and root-counting results for quadratic congruences modulo odd prime powers.

source.title: Singular Moduli and the Ideal Class Group

main_results.informal: Proves that for an odd rational prime p and a valid discriminant d, the ideal (p) is maximal in the quadratic order O_d exactly when the Legendre symbol (d/p) is -1.
main_results.source_ref: C. Geiger, Singular Moduli and the Ideal Class Group, Section 3.2, Proposition 3.2.1.

main_results.informal: Proves that for an odd rational prime p and a valid discriminant d, the ideal (p) is not radical in O_d exactly when p divides d.
main_results.source_ref: C. Geiger, Singular Moduli and the Ideal Class Group, Section 3.2, Proposition 3.2.1.

main_results.informal: Proves that for an odd rational prime p and a valid discriminant d, the ideal (p) is radical but not maximal exactly when the Legendre symbol (d/p) is 1.
main_results.source_ref: C. Geiger, Singular Moduli and the Ideal Class Group, Section 3.2, Proposition 3.2.1.

main_results.informal: Counts roots of x^2 = c modulo p^n for odd prime p and p not dividing c, giving two roots when the Legendre symbol is 1 and none otherwise.
main_results.source_ref: C. Geiger, Singular Moduli and the Ideal Class Group, Section 3.1.

main_results.informal: Counts roots of x^2 = p^(2r) u modulo p^n for odd prime p, p not dividing u, and 2r < n, reducing to the coprime case and multiplying by p^r.
main_results.source_ref: C. Geiger, Singular Moduli and the Ideal Class Group, Section 3.1.

main_results.informal: Proves the discriminant identity (tau - tauConj)^2 = d for valid quadratic-order discriminants d congruent to 0 or 1 modulo 4.
main_results.source_ref: C. Geiger, Singular Moduli and the Ideal Class Group, Section 2.

projects.title: Small undecidable groups and effective Adian–Rabin families
projects.summary: Proves the existence of a finitely presented group with three generator slots and nine relator slots whose word problem is undecidable, and effective families with undecidable triviality having respectively four generators and eleven relators, and two generators and ten relators. The dependency closure includes computable machine-to-Thue reductions, synchronized rewriting, Borisov’s group simulator, injective HNN and Tietze compression, and general Miller–Tancer and Gordon constructions. Formalizes the algebraic results of the cited paper; its four-manifold consequences are outside this project.

source.title: Small undecidable groups and unrecognizable 4-manifolds

main_results.informal: There is a finite presentation with three generator slots and nine relator slots whose word problem is not a computable predicate.
main_results.source_ref: arXiv:2609.10461v1, Theorem 1.1.

main_results.informal: There is a uniformly computable family of finite presentations with four generator slots and eleven relator slots for which the set of indices presenting the trivial group is not computable.
main_results.source_ref: arXiv:2609.10461v1, Theorem 1.3.

main_results.informal: There is a uniformly computable family of finite presentations with two generator slots and ten relator slots for which the set of indices presenting the trivial group is not computable.
main_results.source_ref: arXiv:2609.10461v1, Theorem 1.4.

main_results.informal: The three small-presentation bounds hold together: an undecidable word problem with three generators and nine relators, and effective families with undecidable triviality with four generators and eleven relators and with two generators and ten relators.
main_results.source_ref: arXiv:2609.10461v1, Theorems 1.1, 1.3, and 1.4.

projects.title: Spectral positivity
projects.summary: Perron-Frobenius theory, Jentzsch's theorem, and matrix/operator positivity in Lean 4. At the matrix level it proves that nonnegative matrices have nonnegative powers, the Metzler decomposition and positivity of the matrix exponential of a Metzler matrix, M-matrix inverse positivity, and the Perron-Frobenius theorem for irreducible nonnegative matrices (a positive dominant eigenvalue with a strictly positive eigenvector). At the operator level it proves Jentzsch's theorem for compact self-adjoint positivity-improving operators on L2 — a simple, strictly positive ground state with a spectral gap — together with a kernel positivity criterion.

source.title: spectral-positivity: Perron-Frobenius, Jentzsch, and matrix positivity in Lean 4

main_results.informal: A matrix with all strictly positive entries has a positive eigenvalue with a strictly positive eigenvector (Perron-Frobenius for positive matrices, via the Collatz-Wielandt characterization).
An irreducible (primitive) nonnegative matrix has a positive eigenvalue with a strictly positive eigenvector.
The ground eigenfunction of a compact self-adjoint positivity-improving operator on L2 is strictly positive almost everywhere (Jentzsch).
The inverse of a nonsingular irreducible M-matrix is entrywise strictly positive.

projects.title: Sharp asymptotic upper bounds for sphere packing
projects.summary: Formalizes the sharp high-dimensional asymptotics of the unrestricted Cohn--Elkies linear program and bridges them to sphere-packing density. The development constructs radial test functions through Mellin, saddle-point, and harmonic analysis, proves radialization preserves the unrestricted optimum, and certifies the exact natural- and base-two exponential rates.

source.title: Ten Advances in Mathematics and Theoretical Computer Science

main_results.informal: The d-th root of the unrestricted Cohn--Elkies linear-program bound converges to the sharp constant sqrt(e / (2 pi)).
The base-two logarithm of the unrestricted linear-program bound, divided by dimension, converges to -1/2 log_2(2 pi / e).
There is a vanishing error sequence such that, in every positive dimension, sphere-packing density is at most (sqrt(e / (2 pi)) plus that error) to the dimension.

Packages the complete sharp asymptotic conclusions for the unrestricted program, including quotient-root, natural-logarithmic, and base-two limits, vanishing-error formulas, a universal bound for all admissible functions, and a certified decimal exponent interval.

projects.title: Stability of matter and the kinetic Lieb–Thirring inequality
projects.summary: Formalizes stability of non-relativistic fermionic Coulomb matter in three dimensions, the kinetic Lieb–Thirring inequality with Rumin's explicit coefficient, Baxter's electrostatic inequality with its positive nuclear correction, and real quadratic-form stability with Coulomb finiteness. Preserves the Fourier, Pauli-occupation, Hardy and Voronoi infrastructure in the 184-module dependency closure of these results. The separate ionization, thermodynamic-limit and Thomas–Fermi developments are outside the imported scope.

main_results.informal: For each positive spin multiplicity and nonnegative maximum nuclear charge, one positive constant bounds electron–nucleus attraction by kinetic energy, electron and nuclear repulsion, and the total particle count, uniformly over normalized antisymmetric L² states, charges and nuclear positions, in nonnegative extended-energy form.

With distinct nuclear positions and finite kinetic energy, Coulomb expectations and nuclear repulsion are finite and the real quadratic energy is bounded below by a negative constant times the total particle count, with the constant depending only on spin and maximum charge.

Every normalized antisymmetric L² state with positive spin multiplicity q has kinetic energy at least Rumin's coefficient times q to the power minus two thirds times the integral of the density to the power five thirds, including states of infinite kinetic energy.

For equal nonnegative nuclear charges, attraction plus the positive nearest-other-nucleus correction is bounded by electron and nuclear repulsion plus nearest-nucleus control, including collisions and empty configurations in nonnegative extended arithmetic.
The Fourier kinetic energy of a spin-valued Schwartz state equals the sum of the squared classical spatial derivative integrals, with the physical minus-Laplacian normalization.

projects.title: Stafford 3.8
projects.summary: Lean formalization of Stafford's Conjecture 3.8 for every characteristic-zero field and every Weyl-algebra rank, proving that each nonzero d admits F, R, and S with 1 = d*R + F*d*S. The development also proves an exact Bernstein-degree fixed-source strengthening and derived localization, adjoint, and evolutionary results.

main_results.informal: For every characteristic-zero field, every Weyl algebra rank, and every nonzero d, there are F, R, S with 1 = d*R + F*d*S.
The stated fixed-source strengthening holds with its exact Bernstein-degree bound.

projects.title: Verified Stallings folding for finitely generated subgroups of F2
projects.summary: Constructs a finite inverse automaton recognizing the subgroup generated by any finite list of signed words in the rank-two free group. Proves exact subgroup preservation and correctness of canonical reduced-word membership testing. Reusable infrastructure includes inverse-automaton walks, reduction-compatible traversal, finite fold congruences, coset potentials, flower graphs, and basis roses. Folding uses exhaustive finite search over Boolean relations; no complexity bound, core pruning, subgroup basis, intersection, or index algorithm is claimed.

source.title: Verified finite automata for finitely generated subgroups of F2
source.mathematical_source: John R. Stallings, Topology of Finite Graphs, Inventiones Mathematicae 71 (1983), 551-565, doi:10.1007/BF02095993. This is the rank-two finite-recognizer special case, implemented through least congruences rather than a sequence of local folds.
source.background: Ilya Kapovich and Alexei Myasnikov, Stallings Foldings and Subgroups of Free Groups, Journal of Algebra 248 (2002), 608-668, doi:10.1006/jabr.2001.9033.

projects.provenance_note: Upstream formalization.yaml records human-directed GPT-6 Codex proof development. Lean Pool porting, cleanup, and optimization were also performed by OpenAI Codex. Author attribution follows upstream.

main_results.informal: For every finite list S of signed words on two generators, there exist a finite type of states, a base state, and a partial transition table with inverse-labelled reverse edges, such that traversing the canonical reduced word of any g in FreeGroup (Fin 2) returns to the base exactly when g lies in the subgroup generated by the word values in S. The witness is the computed flower-graph fold.
main_results.source_ref: Upstream Solution.lean, completeStatement and folded_recognizer_exists.

main_results.informal: For every finite input list of signed words in the rank-two free group, the based-loop subgroup of the computed folded flower graph equals the subgroup generated by the input words.
main_results.source_ref: Upstream Stallings/Flower.lean.

main_results.informal: For any finite generating list S and any rank-two free-group element g, the executable folded-automaton test returns true if and only if g belongs to the subgroup generated by S. There is no efficiency guarantee for constructing the automaton.
main_results.source_ref: Upstream Stallings/Flower.lean.

projects.title: Monotonicity Formula for Stationary Harmonic Maps
projects.summary: Formalizes the monotonicity formula for stationary `W^{1,2}_{loc}` maps with Euclidean target. The proof is target independent: it uses only the displayed weak gradient and a vanishing domain first variation, so no target-manifold structure enters the argument. From a bundled stationary Sobolev witness `StationaryW12LocMap u Omega` it proves, for `0 < s <= r < R0`, that the normalized energy `Theta(Du, a, rho) = rho^(2-n) * integral over B(a, rho) of |Du|^2` is monotone: `weakTheta Du a s <= weakTheta Du a r`, together with the exact increment formula `weakTheta Du a r - weakTheta Du a s = weakMonotonicityRhs Du a s r`. The Sobolev layer is project-defined from Mathlib's `MemLp`, weak-derivative identities, Bochner integration, and Euclidean measure theory, following the De Giorgi-Nash-Moser engineering choice; the internal proof routes through a radial vector-field first variation, a coarea/Radon-Nikodym radius representation, smooth radial cutoffs, and an absolute-continuity boundary step.

source.title: Theorems on Regularity and Singularity of Energy Minimizing Maps

main_results.informal: The public input package: a domain-variation stationary `W^{1,2}_{loc}` Sobolev map bundling a chosen weak gradient (`W12LocMapWitness`) with the vanishing domain first-variation identity. This is the object users construct to invoke the monotonicity theorem.

Witness-style monotonicity: from a stationary `W^{1,2}_{loc}` map package, the normalized weak energy `weakTheta` is monotone in the radius, `weakTheta Du a s <= weakTheta Du a r` for `0 < s <= r < R0`.

Witness-style monotonicity formula: the increment of `weakTheta` equals the nonnegative annular radial-energy term, `weakTheta Du a r - weakTheta Du a s = weakMonotonicityRhs Du a s r` for `0 < s < r < R0`.

Componentwise convenience wrapper: the same monotonicity inequality stated directly from the local `L^2`, measurability, weak-gradient, and first-variation hypotheses, without first constructing the witness package.

projects.title: Split, cograph and threshold graph structures
projects.summary: Connects split partitions, cotrees and threshold creation sequences on Mathlib SimpleGraph. Proves the finite forbidden-induced-subgraph characterizations, split iff chordal and co-chordal, and completeness of cotrees and creation sequences. Supplies certificate-preserving operations, twins and nonempty union/join decompositions for cographs, maximum-clique split partitions, and induced/isomorphic transport of existing chordal elimination orders and clique trees. Classical graph theory is formalized; no new mathematical theorem, canonical certificate or recognition-time bound is claimed.

source.title: Structural graph classes, original Lean development checkpoint

main_results.informal: A finite graph is split iff it contains no induced 2K2, C4 or C5.
main_results.source_ref: Földes and Hammer, Split graphs (1977).

main_results.informal: A finite graph is split iff both it and its complement are chordal.
main_results.source_ref: Földes and Hammer, Split graphs (1977).

main_results.informal: A finite graph is P4-free iff it is isomorphic to the graph of a cotree, whose constructors are empty, singleton, disjoint union and join.
main_results.source_ref: Seinsche (1974), doi:10.1016/0095-8956(74)90063-X; Corneil, Lerchs and Stewart Burlingham (1981), doi:10.1016/0166-218X(81)90013-5.

main_results.informal: A graph has a split partition with nested independent-side neighbourhoods iff it is both split and P4-free. No finiteness is required.
main_results.source_ref: Classical threshold characterization; local Threshold.lean and Cotree.lean.

main_results.informal: A finite graph is threshold iff it contains no induced 2K2, C4 or P4.
A finite graph is threshold iff it is isomorphic to a graph constructed from the empty graph by successively adding an isolated or universal vertex.
main_results.source_ref: Classical threshold creation characterization; local ThresholdCreation.lean.

main_results.informal: A finite cograph with at least two vertices has two distinct vertices with identical adjacency outside their pair, whether adjacent or not.
main_results.source_ref: Cotree induction in CographTwins.lean; classical cograph structure.

main_results.informal: A finite cograph that is not preconnected admits a cotree representation with a union root and two nonempty children. This is an existence claim, not a claim about every unreduced cotree.
main_results.source_ref: Seinsche decomposition and CotreeRepresentation constructors.

main_results.informal: A preconnected finite cograph with at least two vertices admits a cotree representation with a join root and two nonempty children.
main_results.source_ref: Seinsche decomposition and CotreeRepresentation constructors.

main_results.informal: Every finite split graph admits a split partition whose clique part has maximum cardinality. Such a partition need not be unique.
main_results.source_ref: Direct finite maximization argument in SplitDecomposition.lean.

projects.title: The optimal exponent relating sumsets and difference sets
projects.summary: For a finite integer set A with at least two elements, proves that C(A) = log(|A+A|/|A|) / log(|A-A|/|A|) is strictly below 2, while explicit finite sets have exponents tending to 2. Thus 2 is the supremum and is never attained. Also gives an explicit witness within 10^(-999) of 2. This imports the upstream base-39 row-and-column variant, not the paper's base-12 automaton construction or its quantitative cardinality estimates. Supporting infrastructure includes injective digit expansions and the strict Pluennecke-Petridis equality argument for finite integer sets.

source.title: Settling the Optimal Exponent Relating Sumsets and Difference Sets

main_results.informal: For every finite set A of integers with at least two elements, log(|A+A|/|A|) / log(|A-A|/|A|) is strictly less than 2.
The growth exponents of the explicit finite integer sets approximatingSet l converge to 2 as l tends to infinity; these sets have at least two elements whenever l is positive.
The number 2 is the least upper bound of the growth exponents of all finite integer sets with at least two elements.
The supremum of the growth exponents of all finite integer sets with at least two elements equals 2.
No finite integer set with at least two elements has growth exponent equal to 2.
The explicitly defined finite integer set quantitativeSet has growth exponent strictly between 2 - 10^(-999) and 2.

projects.title: Sum of sets in several dimensions
projects.summary: Proves Ruzsa's lower bound for sumsets in R^D. If A and B are finite with B nonempty, |B| ≤ |A| and A + B of affine dimension d, then |A + B| ≥ |A| + Σ_{t=1}^{|B|-1} min(d, |A| - t), and this bound is attained in R^d whenever d ≥ 1 and |A| ≥ d + 1, so it is the exact minimum. Derives the asymmetric form of Freiman's lemma, |A + B| ≥ |A| + d|B| - d(d+1)/2. Defines the Freiman dimension of a finite subset of a commutative monoid, transfers the bound to sets with a Freiman model in R^r, and shows that a set X with |X + X| ≤ κ|X| has Freiman dimension at most 2κ - 1 and at most κ - 1 + κ(2κ - 1)/|X|.

source.title: Sum of sets in several dimensions

main_results.informal: For finite A, B ⊆ R^D with B nonempty and |B| ≤ |A|, if the differences of A + B span a space of dimension d, then |A| + Σ_{t=1}^{|B|-1} min(d, |A| - t) ≤ |A + B|.
main_results.source_ref: Theorem 1.

main_results.informal: For finite A, B ⊆ R^D with B nonempty and |B| ≤ |A|, and every d at most the dimension of the span of the differences of A + B, |A| + d|B| ≤ |A + B| + d(d+1)/2.
main_results.source_ref: Corollary 1.1.

main_results.informal: For d ≥ 1, 1 ≤ m ≤ n and n ≥ d + 1, the least size of A + B over A, B ⊆ R^d with |A| = m, |B| = n and A + B of affine dimension d is n + Σ_{j=1}^{m-1} min(d, n - j).
main_results.source_ref: Theorem 2, F_d(m, n) = G_d(m, n).

main_results.informal: The same minimum n + Σ_{j=1}^{m-1} min(d, n - j) holds when only B is required to have affine dimension d.
main_results.source_ref: Theorem 2, F'_d(m, n) = G_d(m, n).

main_results.informal: A nonempty finite subset X of a cancellative commutative monoid with |X + X| ≤ κ|X|, for a real κ, has Freiman dimension at most 2κ - 1.
Under the same hypotheses, the Freiman dimension of X is at most κ - 1 + κ(2κ - 1)/|X|.
Ruzsa's lower bound holds for finite A, B in a commutative monoid with B nonempty and |B| ≤ |A|, with d replaced by r - 1, where r ≥ 1 is the Freiman dimension of A ∪ B.

projects.title: Sums of Three Squares
projects.summary: Formalizes a blueprint step in the three-squares theorem using quadratic forms and geometry of numbers.

main_results.informal: Proves the mod-8-equals-3 blueprint case for the three-squares theorem.
main_results.source_ref: H. Davenport, The geometry of numbers, The Mathematical Gazette 31 (1947), 206-210, doi:10.2307/3608159.

projects.title: Sundog certificates
projects.summary: A referee-free, axiom-clean Lean development of coding-theory certificates: syndrome decoding soundness and lossiness bounds for GF(2) parity-check schemes (with a Reed–Solomon evaluation-dual variant), and a fully machine-checked correctness proof of the Karp reduction chain 3SAT ≤ 3DM ≤ X3C ≤ bounded-weight syndrome decoding. Only the logical iff of each reduction is formalized; polynomial-time bounds, NP classes, and Cook–Levin are unformalized external inputs, so NP-hardness of decoding is conditional on those standard facts.

source.title: Sundog certificates

main_results.informal: The end-to-end reduction correctness: a formula is satisfiable iff its image under the composed 3SAT-to-decoding reduction is a yes-instance of bounded-weight syndrome decoding.
The 3-dimensional matching instance has a perfect matching iff the reduced exact-cover-by-3-sets instance has an exact cover, both directions machine-checked.
Soundness of the cheap syndrome-decoding verifier when it accepts: an exhibited light same-syndrome witness certifies the body is safe within the decoding radius.
Soundness of the verifier when it rejects: a sound column-weight lower bound on the minimum same-syndrome weight rules out every light witness, so the body is genuinely unsafe.

projects.title: Superdiffusion and anomalous regularization in self-similar random flows
projects.summary: Proves quenched displacement-moment estimates, quantitative generator renormalization and anomalous large-scale elliptic regularity for random incompressible flows satisfying the ABK shell-law assumptions. The shell carrier has continuous second derivatives, a stronger qualitative regularity assumption than the paper's local C^{1,1} assumption. The model hypotheses are explicit; the Gaussian example is not constructed. Preserves the production dependency closure, including sensitivity, diffusivity recursion, concentration and divergence-form process theory. Reuses the pooled homogenization and Markov-process libraries. A public companion theorem proves finiteness of the first and second displacement observables used in the superdiffusivity statement. Additional proofs establish measurable dependence of the transition law and quenched displacement expectations on the environment.

main_results.informal: For dimensions at least two, one positive small-coupling threshold simultaneously gives the full quantitative superdiffusivity bounds and almost-sure integrability of both displacement observables at every positive time.

For each dimension and positive nondegeneracy constant, sufficiently small coupling gives annealed moment bounds for the quenched second displacement moment about the intrinsic superdiffusive scale and for the squared quenched mean displacement, uniformly at all positive times and throughout the stated coupling-dependent moment range.

At every triadic scale, the effective diffusivity tracks the predicted superdiffusive profile. One measurable random error with quantitative moment bounds controls both the essential uniform difference and the energy difference between random and homogenized Dirichlet solutions for all admissible forcing and boundary data.

At every scale and admissible Hölder exponent, a random minimal scale with an exponential tail yields large-scale excess-decay estimates for Dirichlet solutions, uniformly in molecular diffusivity, with the boundary-data term absent in the interior subcube.

For dimensions at least two and sufficiently small coupling, at every positive time the first and second displacement observables of the constructed process are integrable for almost every environment.
The first and second quenched displacement expectations of the constructed process are measurable functions of the environment.

projects.title: Synthetic Euclidean geometry: Euclid's Elements Book I
projects.summary: Formalizes Book I of Euclid's Elements via an axiomatic synthetic-geometry system (incidence, betweenness, congruence, and area), culminating in the Pythagorean theorem and its converse.

source.title: A formal system for Euclid's Elements

main_results.informal: The axiomatic class of synthetic Euclidean geometry, bundling points, lines, circles, and the incidence, betweenness, congruence, and area primitives with Euclid's axioms.
Constructs a square on a given segment off a given line.
Constructs the three squares and parallelograms on the sides of a triangle used in the proof of the Pythagorean theorem.
Euclid I.47, the Pythagorean theorem, that the square on the hypotenuse of a right triangle equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides.
Euclid I.48, the converse of the Pythagorean theorem, that a triangle whose square areas satisfy the Pythagorean relation has a right angle.

projects.title: The Three-Gap (Steinhaus) Theorem
projects.summary: Formalizes the three-gap (Steinhaus, three-distance) theorem: for every real `a` and every `N`, the `N`-point orbit `{i·a mod 1 : i < N}` partitions `[0,1)` into gaps taking at most three distinct lengths, and when exactly three occur the largest is the sum of the other two. The proof works in `[0,1)` via `Int.fract` (not `AddCircle`) through the two first-return times `η⁺` and `η⁻`, and is uniform in the rotation number, covering rational and irrational `a` with no case split.

source.title: The Three Gap Theorem (Steinhaus Conjecture)

main_results.informal: For every real `a` and natural `N`, the gaps of the orbit `{i·a mod 1 : i < N}` take at most three distinct lengths.
When the gaps take exactly three distinct lengths, those lengths are precisely the two first returns `η⁺`, `η⁻`, and their sum `η⁺ + η⁻`; in particular the largest gap is the sum of the other two.

projects.title: Boundedness of the trilinear Hilbert transform
projects.summary: Proves the L³ × L³ × L³ to L¹ bound for the principal-value trilinear Hilbert transform on Schwartz functions, together with its unique bounded extension to L³. Preserves the finite inverse theorem, quantitative quadratic charts, dyadic stopping and projection estimates used by the proof.

source.title: Formalization of boundedness of the trilinear Hilbert transform

main_results.informal: There is an absolute real constant C such that the L¹ norm of the principal-value integral of f₁(x+t) f₂(x+2t) f₃(x+3t)/t is at most C times the product of the L³ norms, for all complex Schwartz functions.

The truncations converge pointwise for Schwartz inputs, and the transform has a unique bounded complex trilinear extension from three copies of L³ to L¹, agreeing almost everywhere with the Schwartz transform.

projects.title: Turán's theorem (the "Book" weighting proof)
projects.summary: Formalizes the weighting/optimization proof of Turán's theorem from Proofs from THE BOOK, bounding the number of edges of a p-clique-free simple graph by (1/2)(1 - 1/(p-1)) n².

main_results.informal: Turán's theorem — a p-clique-free simple graph on n vertices has at most (1/2)(1 - 1/(p-1)) n² edges.
For any weight distribution on a p-clique-free graph, the total edge weight is at most ((p-1)(p-2)/2)·(1/(p-1))², the bound used to derive the edge count.
Starting from any weight function, the minimal-support weight-non-decreasing improvement has support that forms a clique.
Equalizing weights between a maximum- and minimum-weight vertex in the clique support strictly increases the total edge weight.

projects.title: Tutte’s path theorem for matroids
projects.summary: Proves the modular-cut path theorem for finite matroids, with reusable rank-partition, hyperplane-separation, relative-complement, indecomposable-cover, and diamond constructions.

main_results.informal: In a finite connected matroid, any two hyperplanes containing a proper indecomposable flat and lying outside a modular cut are joined by a finite Tutte path all of whose vertices contain that flat and avoid the cut. Consecutive vertices are distinct hyperplanes with indecomposable corank-two intersection; repeated nonconsecutive vertices are permitted.

In any finite matroid, two hyperplanes containing an indecomposable flat F and lying outside a modular cut are joined by a Tutte path whose vertices contain F and avoid the cut. This strengthens the cited path theorem by requiring only connectedness of the contraction by F; properness of F follows from containment in an endpoint hyperplane.

If an indecomposable flat S and a flat U span the ground, every indecomposable flat T contained in both extends inside S to an indecomposable flat R spanning the ground with U, with corank R equal to rank U minus rank T.
For nested flats T contained in S, there is a flat U containing T whose intersection with S is T, whose join with S is the ground, and whose corank equals rank S minus rank T.

projects.title: Ulm's theorem for countable reduced abelian p-groups
projects.summary: Formalizes Ulm's classification theorem for countable reduced abelian p-groups in arbitrary Lean universes. The development constructs the transfinite Ulm filtration and invariants, proves their invariance under additive equivalence, establishes Kaplansky's one-generator extension lemma, and completes the countable back-and-forth classification. A finite-group regression distinguishes Z/4 x Z/4 from Z/2 x Z/8 at the zeroth Ulm invariant.

source.title: Ulm's theorem for countable reduced abelian p-groups

main_results.informal: For any prime p and any two countable reduced abelian p-groups in the same arbitrary Lean universe, the groups are additively isomorphic if and only if all of their classical Ulm invariants, indexed by universe-zero ordinals, agree.

Equal Ulm invariants at every universe-zero ordinal imply an additive equivalence between countable reduced abelian p-groups, via finite height-preserving partial isomorphisms and a back-and-forth limit.
An additive equivalence preserves every classical Ulm invariant.
The groups Z/4 x Z/4 and Z/2 x Z/8 are not additively isomorphic; the proof exercises the classification theorem and independently detects their different zeroth Ulm invariants.

projects.title: Unconditional Schauder Bases
projects.summary: Develops an API for Schauder bases and unconditional Schauder bases of complete normed spaces, including ordered partial-sum convergence, rearrangement criteria for unconditionality, and an arbitrary-index variant built on unconditional summability, then proves a finite sign criterion: a family with dense closed span, nonzero vectors, and a uniform finite sign bound is the basis of an unconditional Schauder basis.

source.title: Classical Banach Spaces I and II

main_results.informal: Finite sign criterion for sequences: if `x : ℕ → E` has dense closed linear span, every `x n` is nonzero, and finite sign changes are uniformly bounded by `C`, then `x` is the basis sequence of an unconditional Schauder basis.
main_results.source_ref: J. Lindenstrauss and L. Tzafriri, Classical Banach Spaces I and II, Chapter 1, Section c, unconditional bases, doi:10.1007/978-3-662-53294-2.

main_results.informal: Abstract-index form of the finite sign criterion: under the same dense span, nonzero, and uniform finite sign bound hypotheses for an arbitrarily indexed family, there is an abstractly indexed unconditional Schauder basis whose basis family is exactly `x`.
main_results.source_ref: J. Lindenstrauss and L. Tzafriri, Classical Banach Spaces I and II, Chapter 1, Section c, unconditional bases, doi:10.1007/978-3-662-53294-2.

projects.title: Virasoro Project
projects.summary: Formalizes the Virasoro algebra, its Witt-algebra central extension, Verma modules, and the basic bosonic Sugawara construction.

source.title: Infinite-Dimensional Lie Algebras

main_results.informal: Defines the Virasoro algebra as a one-dimensional central extension of the Witt algebra.
Constructs the basic bosonic Sugawara representation of the Virasoro algebra from locally truncated Heisenberg actions.

projects.title: Viscosity solutions, Aleksandrov differentiability and harmonic Dirichlet problems
projects.summary: Develops second-order semijets, smooth test-function equivalence, Jensen contact sets, convex Aleksandrov differentiability, the quadratic-penalty Ishii lemma and compact-domain comparison for degenerate elliptic equations. Perron assembly retains explicit comparison, barrier and bumping assumptions; these are discharged for classical harmonic Dirichlet existence on bounded open domains satisfying a uniform exterior sphere condition.

main_results.informal: A convex real-valued function on an open subset of any finite-dimensional real inner product space is second-order differentiable at Lebesgue-almost every point.
Under the localized semiconvexity and strict-contact hypotheses, the contact set arising from sufficiently small linear perturbations has positive Lebesgue measure.

For an upper semicontinuous function and a lower semicontinuous function on locally compact subsets of real coordinate space, doubled-variable maxima with the quadratic penalty yield closed semijets satisfying the Ishii block-matrix bounds.

A viscosity subsolution lies below a supersolution on a nonempty locally compact domain with compact closure, assuming boundary comparison, semicontinuity on the closure, properness, operator continuity, the Ishii structural condition and uniform scalar decrease.
On an open domain, semijet and smooth C² test-function formulations of viscosity subsolutions agree for Hessian-continuous, symmetric-part-invariant operators.

On a bounded open subset of finite-dimensional Euclidean space with a uniform exterior sphere condition, Lipschitz data on its closure admit a continuous extension that agrees on the boundary and is C² and harmonic in the domain, with a boundary modulus depending only on the domain and Lipschitz constant.

projects.title: Vizing's theorem and equitable edge colourings
projects.summary: Proves the maximum-degree-plus-one edge-colouring bound for finite simple graphs by fans and Kempe exchanges. A separate component-swapping argument equitably rebalances any finite proper edge colouring on its original palette. Together they give equitable proper edge colourings on any palette of at least maximum degree plus one colours, with every class bounded by the ceiling of the average class size. Extracted from the published Paper IV formalization; these are classical colouring results, not a claim to new mathematics or to the paper's clique-partition bound.

source.title: Vizing and equitable edge-colouring modules in the published Paper IV freeze

main_results.informal: The line graph of a finite simple graph G is colourable with maximum degree of G plus one colours.
main_results.source_ref: Vizing's theorem for finite simple graphs; Vizing (1964).

main_results.informal: The chromatic number of the line graph of a finite simple graph G is at most maximum degree of G plus one.
Every proper edge colouring of a finite simple graph with a finite palette admits a proper recolouring on the same palette in which any two colour classes differ in size by at most one.
For every finite simple graph G and natural c at least maximum degree of G plus one, there is an equitable proper edge colouring with c colours; each colour class has at most ceiling(|E(G)|/c) edges.

projects.title: Mean-field derivation and well-posedness of the Vlasov equation
projects.summary: Formalizes the mean-field limit, Dobrushin stability, and forward-in-time well-posedness for the Vlasov equation via Wasserstein-1 optimal transport.

source.title: A Formalization of the Mean-Field Derivation of the Vlasov Equation

main_results.informal: Forward-in-time existence of a Lagrangian solution to the Vlasov equation on any finite horizon, for interaction forces that are Lipschitz gradients of an even pair potential (class AssW) — with no smallness restriction on the Lipschitz constant.

A Wasserstein-1 form of Dobrushin's 1979 stability estimate (the original uses a truncated metric) - two Lagrangian Vlasov solutions with finite first moments at every time separate at most at an exponential Gronwall rate.

Conditional mean-field limit - given Wasserstein-1 convergence of the initial empirical data and a uniform Dobrushin stability estimate for the empirical curves, the N-particle empirical measures converge to the Vlasov solution uniformly on any finite horizon.

On a time window with L * T^2 < 1, a weak solution with the standing regularity (even C^2 pair potential AssW2, finite first moments, narrow continuity, time-continuity of the convolution force at each point, continuity of the convolution-derivative field, and a uniform spatial first-moment bound on the window) is Lagrangian - the pushforward of its initial datum along the characteristic flow.

projects.title: The Wallace problem in ZFC
projects.summary: Formalizes in ZFC a Hausdorff countably compact group topology without nontrivial convergent sequences on every torsion-free Abelian group of cardinality continuum. It specializes the construction to the rational direct sum and the additive real group, and derives a commutative Tychonoff countably compact cancellative semigroup that is not a group.

source.title: The Wallace problem and countably compact torsion-free Abelian groups in ZFC

main_results.informal: Every torsion-free Abelian group of cardinality continuum admits a Hausdorff countably compact group topology with no nontrivial convergent sequences.
Both the continuum-indexed rational direct sum and the additive group of real numbers admit such Hausdorff countably compact group topologies without nontrivial convergent sequences.
There exists a commutative Tychonoff countably compact topological semigroup with two-sided cancellation which is not a group.

projects.title: Whitehead's theorem for CW-complexes
projects.summary: Formalizes Whitehead's theorem — a continuous map between CW-complexes that induces isomorphisms on all homotopy groups is a homotopy equivalence — including the supporting theory of CW-complexes, relative homotopy groups, the homotopy extension property, and compression of maps.

main_results.informal: Proves that a continuous map between CW-complexes inducing isomorphisms on all homotopy groups is a homotopy equivalence.

projects.title: Irrationality of the Riemann zeta function at five
projects.summary: Proves that Mathlib's Riemann zeta function at five is an irrational real number, following Aabir Fauzan's September 2026 preprint. Constructs integer polynomials of degree 37n with positive values at zeta(5) that decay exponentially in n squared. Includes a general integer-polynomial irrationality criterion, Hankel determinant and moment-integral identities, logarithmic-energy estimates, prime-adic integrality bounds, and kernel-checked rational certificates. The formalization uses a different normalizer and a positive decay constant in place of the paper's specific constant 139/5. Reuses the prime number theorem infrastructure already in the MooreBound project.

source.title: Zeta5 formalization of Aabir Fauzan's zeta(5) is irrational

main_results.informal: There exists an irrational real number x whose complex coercion equals Mathlib's Riemann zeta function evaluated at five.
main_results.source_ref: Fauzan, zeta(5) is irrational, Theorem 1.1, September 17, 2026, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22826419; upstream Apery/Main.lean. The completed formalization was released on September 23, 2026.

main_results.informal: There is a positive real c such that, for all sufficiently large n, an integer polynomial Q of degree 37n is a positive rational multiple of the constructed determinant polynomial and satisfies 0 < Q(zeta(5)) < exp(-c*n^2).
main_results.source_ref: Upstream Apery/MainEstimate.lean; variant of the paper's Theorem 2.1 with c = -800*(Aeff + U) instead of 139/5.

main_results.informal: A real xi is irrational if, eventually, integer polynomials of degree at most d(n) have positive values at xi bounded by epsilon(n), and b^d(n)*epsilon(n) tends to zero for every positive natural b.
main_results.source_ref: Upstream Apery/Criterion.lean; the paper's Section 1.1.

projects.title: Thakur's hypotheses on power sums of F_q[t]
projects.summary: Formalizes four components of Thakur's hypotheses on power sums over finite polynomial rings, including uniqueness and monotonicity results for the carry-free digit optimization problems and the Laurent-series expansion of finite-field power sums.

source.title: Thakur's hypotheses on power sums of F_q[t]

main_results.informal: Proves uniqueness of the admissible base-q decomposition maximizing the H1 power-sum weight functional.
Proves the H2 unique-minimizer statement for the recursive digit/carry-free optimization problem defining the values s_d(k).
Proves the H3 monotonicity statement that s_d(k) is strictly less than s_d(k+1) when p does not divide k.
Proves the Lemma 4.1 Laurent-series expansion for S_d(k), with nonzero coefficients indexed by the carry-free tuples.

projects.title: Simple zeros of the Riemann zeta function
projects.summary: Formalizes Lamzouri's Hilbert-space proof of lower bounds for simple and distinct zeros of the Riemann zeta function. From explicit Riemann--von Mangoldt and unconditional pair-correlation hypotheses, the development proves that eventually more than 67.25% of nontrivial zeros are simple and on the critical line and more than 83.625% are distinct. It includes the finite-multiset Hilbert-space inequality, zeta-zero multiplicity symmetries, an admissible cutoff construction, and certified trigonometric estimates.

source.title: A new proof that more than 2/3 of the zeros of the Riemann zeta function are simple and on the critical line

main_results.informal: Assuming the stated Riemann--von Mangoldt and unconditional pair-correlation formulas, beyond some height more than 67.25% of nontrivial zeta zeros are simple and lie on the critical line.
Under the same two explicit analytic hypotheses, beyond some height more than 83.625% of nontrivial zeta zeros are distinct.
Bounds from below the number of multiplicity-one real points in a finite nonempty conjugation-invariant multiset using the squared test-kernel sum of any admissible function.
Bounds from below the number of distinct points in a finite nonempty conjugation-invariant multiset using the same Hilbert-space kernel method.

projects.title: Linear independence of 1, zeta(2), and zeta(3)
projects.summary: Proves that 1, the Riemann zeta function at 2, and its value at 3 are linearly independent over the rationals, using integer polynomial approximation, p-adic coefficient bounds, prime-edge nonvanishing, and logarithmic potential energy estimates for Hankel determinants. Includes reusable irrationality criteria, contour integration, Andreief identities, Newton-basis valuation bounds, and energy inequalities for finite measures. The cited source is the completed Lean proof; independent novelty of the informal argument is not claimed.

source.title: Linear independence of 1, zeta(2), and zeta(3), Lean formalization

main_results.informal: The three complex numbers 1, riemannZeta 2, and riemannZeta 3 are linearly independent over the rational numbers.
main_results.source_ref: Upstream Zeta32/Final.lean and Solution.lean at the pinned commit. First public proof release: 2026-09-30 03:47:38 UTC, commit ec4fcb5617126b0a861f9e0c16f95425b32d4638. The upstream README and NOTICE disclose substantial AI assistance. The polynomial argument is credited upstream to Fauzan; this card cites the Lean artifact, not a separately verified paper.

main_results.informal: For rational a, b, and c, if a plus b times the real sum of 1/(k+1)^2 plus c times the real sum of 1/(k+1)^3 is zero, then all three coefficients are zero; both sums range over natural numbers k.
For every rational r, the real series for zeta(3) minus r times the real series for zeta(2) is irrational.

projects.title: Irrationality of ζ(3)
projects.summary: Formalizes Beukers' proof of Apéry's theorem for ζ(3), including the integral identities, denominator estimates, positivity, upper bounds, and final irrationality contradiction.

source.title: A note on the irrationality of ζ(2) and ζ(3)

main_results.informal: Proves that ζ(3) is irrational.
Clears denominators in the Apéry integral to produce a linear form in 1 and ζ(3).
Proves positivity of the transformed Beukers-Apéry integral.
Bounds the Beukers-Apéry integral by a geometric factor times the ζ(3) series.
Shows that the denominator-cleared Apéry linear forms tend to zero.

projects.title: ZFLean
projects.summary: Develops a practical ZFC set-theory framework with von Neumann naturals, integers, rationals, functions, embeddings, isomorphisms, booleans, and sums.

source.title: Set Theory

main_results.informal: Proves a Cantor-Bernstein theorem for ZF sets.
Provides induction for the von Neumann natural numbers.
Provides induction for the quotient construction of ZF integers.

projects.title: The Zhang-Yeung non-Shannon information inequality
projects.summary: Formalizes the Zhang-Yeung inequality, the first known non-Shannon-type entropy inequality, together with its dual and averaged forms derived through the copy lemma.

main_results.informal: Proves the Zhang-Yeung non-Shannon-type information inequality for four discrete random variables.
Proves the dual form of the Zhang-Yeung inequality.
Proves the averaged symmetric form of the Zhang-Yeung inequality.
